papers.title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
papers.journal: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
papers.abstract: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

papers.title: Hypoxia-responsive supramolecular systems based on macrocycles and self-assembly structures.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Various representatives of the macrocyclic platforms, namely cyclodextrins, cucurbiturils, pillararenes, (thia)calixarenes, due to their properties such as molecular recognition, are used as molecular containers-carriers for pharmaceuticals and bio-organic fluorescent dyes. As a result of complex formation, the photostability and the signal-to-noise ratio of dyes increase. In addition, the solubility of hydrophobic guests in water improves, cytotoxicity is reduced, and targeted delivery promotes the accumulation of drugs/dyes in tumor cells.

papers.title: Nitric oxide in the occurrence and development of ischemic cerebrovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Since nitric oxide is a chemically highly reactive free radical that can act as both an oxidizing agent and a reducing agent, it is assumed that it has diverse effects on biological tissues. Nitric oxide is fundamentally important for the regulation of immune, reproductive and neuromuscular system functions and is the main signaling molecule and effector that can dilate blood vessels and modulate energy metabolism. This review examines the key role of nitric oxide in the mechanisms underlying the response to hypoxia, as well as in the effects of factors induced by hypoxia. The available conflicting information allowed us to conclude that at present, there is no consensus about the role of endogenous nitric oxide in the processes occurring after ischemic cerebrovascular disease.

papers.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for the treatment of traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy for traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury remains a subject of debate. To comprehensively evaluate the impact of hyperbaric oxygen on motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We performed a comprehensive search across PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and major Chinese databases for randomized controlled trials published through June 2025. A total of 15 randomized controlled trials were included. The pooled results indicated that hyperbaric oxygen therapy significantly improved the American Spinal Injury Association motor score (mean difference = 10.30, 95% confidence interval: 7.70-12.90), the total American Spinal Injury Association sensory score (mean difference = 29.29, 95% confidence interval: 18.82-39.75), the American Spinal Injury Association light touch score (mean difference = 9.84, 95% confidence interval: 6.15-13.53), and the American Spinal Injury Association pinprick score (mean difference = 8.75, 95% confidence interval: 4.40-13.11). Furthermore, hyperbaric oxygen therapy was associated with significant enhancements in the Barthel Index (mean difference = 16.60, 95% confidence interval: 10.51-22.68) and the Functional Independence Measure (mean difference = 17.41, 95% confidence interval: 10.83-23.98). In conclusion, adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy appears to improve motor function, sensory function, and activities of daily living in patients with traumatic incomplete spinal cord injury compared to conventional treatments alone. However, due to methodological limitations and potential publication bias in the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution, and further high-quality, multi-center randomized controlled trials are warranted.

papers.title: High levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite with protein nitration: a new therapeutic target for gliomas.
papers.abstract: The gap junction signaling pathway is a core hub mediating intercellular communication, which plays a vital role in maintaining tissue homeostasis, and its dysfunction is closely related to glioma. Nitroproteomics studies have shown that protein tyrosine nitration plays an important role in the progression of glioma, and gap junction is one of the significantly enriched nitroprotein signaling pathways in glioma; proteoformics reveals that nitration can produce various proteoforms of related proteins, which have different functional states in different subtypes of glioma, suggesting that nitration may alter the functional states of related proteins in gap junction pathways. When levels of nitric oxide and peroxynitrite (ONOO-) rise, they induce the tyrosine nitration of key proteins in the gap junction pathway; this nitration not only interferes with the function of the gap junction pathway, but also affects other gap junction-linked signaling networks. Forming an attack network on the gap junction pathway through multi-pathway cross-regulation has great potential for therapeutic strategies targeting the gap junction pathway. We recommend in-depth studies of the gap junction signaling pathway and potential drugs targeting gap junction signals, including drugs that target gap junction communication activators, nitration inhibitors, and drugs that directly target specific nitroproteins, combined with conventional chemotherapy or immune checkpoint inhibitors, as well as the construction of personalized medical frameworks as important future research directions.

papers.title: Antitrust Regulation of Algorithmic "Platform-Driven Involution'': From Governing the Corporate Person to Governing the Platform Ecosystem
papers.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly govern competition through algorithmically administered rules that allocate visibility, subsidies, commissions, participation opportunities, and sanctions. This article reconstructs ``platform-driven involution'' as a testable, portfolio-based theory-of-harm framework rather than a freestanding antitrust offense. Its application remains anchored in market definition, dominance, identified conduct under Article 22 of China's Anti-Monopoly Law, causal proof, competitive effects, and objective justification. The article clarifies that ecosystem analysis supplements rather than replaces relevant-market analysis and develops an evidence architecture for separating platform-induced effects from macroeconomic, demand, cost, and merchant-specific confounders. It then distinguishes preventive measures already supported by Chinese hard law or voluntary compliance guidance from compulsory competition-specific filing and pre-deployment assessment that would require clearer future authorization. The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories. Comparative analysis of EU platform regulation and Google Shopping supports calibrated procedural prevention, meaningful explanation, and causal discipline without protecting inefficient competitors or condemning aggressive competition.

The 2026 Trip.com decision is used to show how traffic allocation, exclusivity, lowest-price requirements, technical monitoring, and sanctions can form an integrated abuse architecture while liability remains tied to established statutory categories.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.abstract: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-performance validation.

papers.title: Current status of room temperature magnetic compensation in impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial thin films
papers.abstract: Mn4N, a ferrimagnet that does not contain rare-earth elements, possesses attractive properties for spintronics applications. In particular, Mn4N epitaxial films exhibit a small spontaneous magnetization of about 100 kA m(-1), a large spin polarization (p = 0.8), and large perpendicular magnetic anisotropy with a magnetic anisotropy constant of approximately 10(5) J m(-3). More importantly, achieving magnetic compensation at room temperature is possible through impurity doping. This property is particularly significant for spin-torque-based spintronics applications. In the vicinity of the magnetization and/or angular momentum compensation points, magnetization dynamics can be substantially accelerated, enabling high-speed switching and domain wall motion. This article surveys the magnetic properties of impurity-doped Mn4N epitaxial films grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates, highlighting recent results obtained with Cu-, Ag-, Au-, and Pd-doped Mn4N films in comparison with Ni- and Cr-doped Mn4N films. Furthermore, with a view to device applications of Mn4N, we present the formation of ultrathin (similar to 4 nm) Pt epitaxial films with a <100> orientation on MgO (001), which is essential for injecting spins into Mn4N-based overlayers by utilizing the spin Hall effect of heavy metals. papers.title: Reproducible chiroptical activity from aggregated chiral thienopyrroledione-fluorene π-conjugated polymers
papers.abstract: Chiral pi-conjugated polymers have attracted considerable interest because their chiral-aggregated structures can generate pronounced chiroptical responses. Here, we report the design, synthesis, and chiroptical characterization of fluorene - thienopyrroledione polymers bearing a single chiral center in each repeating unit, (R)- and (S)-PFTPD, prepared via direct arylation polycondensation to minimize structural defects. Although only weak chiroptical activity was observed in the solution, the addition of 1-butanol to CHCl3 solutions of the polymers induced the formation of stable aggregates that exhibited strong circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL). Systematic examination of the sample preparation parameters revealed that the mixing process critically influences the chiroptical properties. Dropwise addition of 1-butanol under controlled stirring provided the most reliable results, yielding highly reproducible CD spectra. Under these optimized conditions, the aggregates exhibited an average dissymmetry factor (|g abs|) of 1.5 & times; 10-2 and a CPL dissymmetry factor (|g lum|) of 1.9 & times; 10-2. These values rank among the highest reported for pi-conjugated polymer aggregates bearing only a single chiral source per repetition unit. This study demonstrates that precise control over the solvent-mixing process is essential for the reproducible emergence of chiroptical properties and highlights the chiral TPD unit as a promising platform for chiroptical polymer materials.

papers.title: Somatosensory phenotyping in women with persistent genital arousal disorder: a case-control study.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Persistent genital arousal disorder (PGAD) is a rare and distressing condition characterized by persistent, unwanted genital arousal in the absence of sexual desire or stimulation. Persistent genital arousal disorder is increasingly recognized as a disorder of abnormal genital sensory processing, but objective neurophysiological data remain limited. Methods: We conducted an exploratory case-control study to characterize somatosensory function in women with PGAD. Thirty women with PGAD and 30 age-matched healthy controls were recruited at Leiden University Medical Center. Participants underwent quantitative sensory testing (QST) at hand and external genital sites, conditioned pain modulation, and corneal confocal microscopy. Results: Hand QST values were within normal range in both groups. In the genital region, PGAD participants showed altered thermal pain processing, with cold and heat hyperalgesia compared with controls. Mechanical pain thresholds did not differ between groups; however, PGAD participants reported higher pain intensity ratings to mechanical stimuli and showed significantly greater temporal summation of pain in genital regions. Genital dynamic mechanical allodynia occurred more frequently in PGAD participants but did not differ significantly at the group level. Conditioned pain modulation magnitude did not differ between groups and showed substantial interindividual variability. Corneal confocal microscopy abnormalities were observed in a proportion of participants in both groups without significant between-group differences. Discussion: These findings show that QST is feasible in women with PGAD and indicate that PGAD is associated with altered somatosensory processing demonstrating genital thermal hypersensitivity and central pain sensitization in a subset of patients.

papers.title: Designing an Integrated Play Therapy Program Based on the Cognitive-Behavioral Approach and Sensory Integration for Children With Autism
papers.journal: The Psychological Research in Individuals with Exceptional Needs
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to design an integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative research design. Using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s (2006) six-phase framework, valid and up-to-date theoretical and empirical evidence was systematically reviewed and coded. A step-by-step framework illustrating the process of structuring and designing the integrated play therapy program based on the cognitive-behavioral approach and sensory integration for children with autism was developed according to Intervention Mapping (IM). The integrated cognitive-behavioral play therapy and sensory integration program was subsequently presented to 10 faculty members from the University of Tehran and experienced therapists working in a university clinic for children with neurodevelopmental disorders who were professionally involved in the field of autism spectrum disorder. They were asked to provide expert feedback on the developed intervention package to facilitate its refinement. Quantitative assessment of the content validity of the integrated play therapy program was conducted using the Content Validity Index (CVI) and Content Validity Ratio (CVR). The results indicated that the integrated program resulted in the development of a valid 12-session protocol. The inductive thematic analysis process progressed from 52 initial codes to 22 axial codes, 14 subthemes, and 8 main themes. These eight themes constituted the conceptual pillars of the protocol and integrated the cognitive-behavioral and sensory integration approaches within a spiral, play-based structure, thereby empirically demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed program design. Another finding of the present study was that the integrated program demonstrated satisfactory validity. The CVI calculated for each of the 12 items corresponding to the intervention sessions ranged from .80 to .90, with all values exceeding the accepted threshold of .79. Internal validity was confirmed through member checking and calculation of the CVI. The developed integrated program constitutes a valid intervention for improving sensory responses in children with sensory modulation disorder. Based on the findings, it is recommended that psychologists working with children with special needs use the 12-session integrated protocol developed in this study as a standardized intervention package.

In terms of purpose, this was an applied study, and in terms of methodology, it employed a qualitative research design. The results indicated that the integrated program resulted in the development of a valid 12-session protocol.

papers.title: Enhancing mass transport in redox flow batteries with 3D-printed triply periodic minimal surface electrode structures
papers.abstract: Triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures offer a compelling route for designing porous electrodes with tunable architectures for electrochemical applications such as redox flow batteries. In this study, we fabricated carbonaceous TPMS electrodes, including gyroid, diamond, IWP, and cubic geometries, using digital light processing, and evaluated their performance in single-electrolyte flow cells using an organic redox couple. The printing process and subsequent thermal treatment produced conductive porous electrodes that closely replicated the intended TPMS geometries, preserving the characteristic features of each design. Through a detailed analysis of pressure drop, surface area, and electrochemical behavior, we identified the diamond design as particularly effective in enhancing mass transport while maintaining low hydraulic resistance. We further assessed gyroid structures, selected for being the most well-known among TPMSs, across a range of porosities, finding that higher porosity improved flow performance despite a reduction in surface area, an advantageous trade-off for electrolytes with facile kinetics and low ionic conductivity. Comparison with a commercial carbon felt electrode revealed comparable ohmic resistance and favorable flow characteristics, though reduced electrochemical surface area limited the achievable current densities. To isolate mass transport effects, a kinetically facile organic redox couple was employed, after which a representative 3D-printed gyroid electrode was evaluated in a proof-of-concept full-cell vanadium redox flow battery. A full-cell test demonstrated the feasibility of printed electrodes, achieving a voltage efficiency of 76% at a current density of 50 mA cm−2. These findings demonstrate the potential of architected 3D printed electrodes for future redox flow batteries and highlight the importance of tuning geometry and porosity to balance power output, mass transport, and system-level pumping losses.

papers.title: Airdrop Sybil Attack detection framework supported by machine learning
papers.journal: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunication Systems
papers.abstract: A skilled hunter may earn thousands of dollars in tokens from a single airdrop, making airdrop Sybil assaults a profitable endeavor. In this situation, Sybil assaults are not always wanted by projects and are often seen as improper behavior by honest individuals, which may negatively impact a project's image. It is thus to be anticipated that detection methods for Sybil assaults would be continuously enhanced. This study presents a multistep structure. Its concept is to sort blockchain addresses and give each one a score that indicates whether it belongs to the Sybil or regular class. Topologies were classified using a graph isomorphism network, whose parameters were adjusted using a dataset that the authors labeled. In subsequent phases, the account clustering operation was performed using a DBSCAN. Each stage in the framework may be given arbitrary weights by users, which will decide how essential a step is to them and provide a different score for a particular address. A grid search strategy and a threshold after which the address is deemed Sybil were used to find the optimal weights. This article examined a collection of EOAs from the ZK sync rollup. Ultimately, 76% of the examined accounts were classified as Sybils. Compared to the official ZK sync eligibility list, we found 342 addresses that received airdrop tokens but were marked as Sybil by our solution.

papers.title: Preparation and properties of gel polymer electrolytes based on tetrafunctional cross-linked PEG network
papers.abstract: Abstract Thiol-yne click reaction between pentaerythritol tetrakis(3-mercaptopropionate) and α, ω-dipropiolate-terminated polyethylene glycol was carried out in propylene carbonate containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imideto obtain gel polymer electrolyte with tetra-branched network structure. The ionic conductivity was found to depend on the polymer content in the gel polymer electrolyte and the chain length of the polyethylene glycol constituting the tetra-branched network structure. These experimental results indicated that lithium cations moved not only within the electrolyte solution but also along the PEG chains that form a network structure.

papers.title: Cold atmospheric pressure plasma pretreatment as a novel tool to tailor the functional properties of quince seed mucilage biopolymer-based edible films
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Quince seed mucilage (QSM) is a promising polysaccharide for the fabrication of biodegradable edible films; however, its relatively limited functional performance restricts broader food-packaging applications. Scope and Approach: The present study investigated the effects of cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) treatment applied to QSM solutions at 6, 7, and 8 kV for 1, 3, and 5 min, followed by a comprehensive evaluation of the physicochemical, surface, barrier, mechanical, and thermal properties of the resulting films. Key Findings: CAP treatment did not significantly affect film thickness regardless of the applied processing conditions. Contact angle analysis demonstrated that the highest surface hydrophobicity was achieved under a 7 kV for 3 min plasma treatment. Water vapor barrier measurements revealed that films treated for 3 min exhibited the lowest permeability, irrespective of the applied voltage. Surface topography analysis indicated that 6 kV for 1min plasma exposure generated the greatest surface roughness, whereas increasing either the treatment duration or applied voltage produced a denser, more homogeneous, and compact film microstructure. Compared with the untreated control, CAP treatment significantly enhanced the mechanical performance of the films, with the optimum tensile properties obtained following treatment at 6 kV for 1 min. Thermal characterization by TGA and DSC further demonstrated that 5 min plasma exposure time adversely affected the thermal stability of the films, while optimized CAP conditions (3 min) provided the most favorable thermal performance. Conclusions Overall, the findings demonstrate that appropriately optimized CAP treatment effectively improves the structural integrity and functional performance of QSM-based biodegradable films.

papers.title: Modulating Sulfur Composition toward Ultralow Dielectric Loss Polymers: A Miscible Blending Strategy with Poly(phenylene oxide)/Poly(phenylene sulfide) Alternating Copolymers
papers.abstract: Abstract In recent high-speed communications (i.e., 5G and 6G), insulating polymers exhibiting both a minimized dielectric constant (Dk) and dissipation factor (Df) have been extensively used to reduce dielectric loss, although the empirical Dk–Df trade-off relationship has prevented further reductions in these values. Here, we describe a rational approach for the simultaneous reduction of both Dk and Df through simple polymer blending, wherein a low-Dk ether polymer is hybridized with a low-Df sulfide polymer. Specifically, upon mixing poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene sulfide) (PMPS) or poly(2,6-dimethyl-1,4-phenylene oxide) (PPO) with their alternating copolymer, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) thermograms of the resulting polymer blends revealed their miscibility, as verified by shifting of glass-transition temperatures, allowing for the successful film preparation and the tuning of their dielectric properties without compromising other material properties (e.g., thermostability). In particular, the observed enhancement in free fractional volume for the polymer blends suggests a reduction in Dk, finally minimizing dielectric loss (Dk = 2.43, Df = 0.00081 at 10 GHz). Specifically, those dielectric losses are significantly lower than the empirical limits defined for single-component polymers. Overall, this study describes a rational strategy for the preparation of diverse insulating polymers with extremely low dielectric losses.

papers.title: DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY OF ULTRA-LOW-DOSE CT VS. STANDARD-DOSE CT FOR PULMONARY NODULE DETECTION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS
authors: KHALED BONNA , RASHA GALAL ELSAFTY , NORA EID ALANAZI , RANIN JABER M ALMAJRASHI AHLAM ALI Y ASIRI , WALEED MUFAREH ALSHAHRANI , SOMAYYAH SOHAIL MITHA , SHOUG NASSER ALKHAMMASH , BANDAR SAAD ALSHREEF
papers.journal: TPM Testing, psychometrics, methodology in applied psychology
papers.abstract: Background: Standard dose computed tomography (CT) is a primary modality for detecting pulmonary nodules (PNs), but the health risk from cumulative radiation exposure has prompted the emergence of ultra-low-dose CT (ULDCT) as an alternative to reduce this dose, because its diagnostic accuracy remains variable, this systematic review and meta-analysis aims to synthesize the existing evidence to determine the diagnostic accuracy and effective radiation dose of ULDCT for pulmonary nodule detection. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Ovid MEDLINE for original research published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of ULDCT for PN detection, for which a meta-analysis using random-effects models was performed to calculate the pooled sensitivity for nodule detection and the pooled mean effective radiation dose, with a subgroup analysis conducted to assess the impact of different reconstruction algorithms. Results: Forty-two studies comprising 15,792 patients were included, from which a meta-analysis of 11 studies demonstrated a pooled sensitivity of 91.9% (95% CI: 84.6%–97.1%) for PN detection with heterogeneity (I²=93.0%), and a pooled mean effective dose from 12 studies of 0.22 mSv (95% CI: 0.11–0.33 mSv), a level comparable to standard chest radiography, while subgroup analysis revealed a trend towards higher sensitivity with advanced reconstruction algorithms (96.7%) compared to standard iterative reconstruction (87.9%) that was not statistically significant (p=0.091), and a narrative synthesis confirmed ULDCT's accuracy for solid nodules but identified reduced sensitivity for subsolid, ground-glass, and small (<6 mm) nodules, with performance limited in patients with a high body mass index (BMI). Conclusion: ULDCT combined with advanced reconstruction techniques offers high diagnostic accuracy for the detection of solid pulmonary nodules and reduces radiation exposure to levels approaching that of a chest X-ray, but its utility is limited for detecting subsolid and small nodules and in obese patients, making protocol standardization and patient-specific considerations essential to optimize its clinical implementation.

papers.title: Impacts of Polymeric Excipients on the Physicochemical Properties of Ritonavir Solid Dispersions
papers.journal: VNU Journal of Science Medical and Pharmaceutical Sciences
papers.abstract: Abstract: Amorphous solid dispersion (ASD) formulation prepared by solvent‑evaporation was employed to enhance the apparent solubility of the poorly water‑soluble drug ritonavir (RTV), a BCS Class IV compound widely used in HIV therapy. This study investigated the influence of polymeric excipients on ritonavir’s solid‑state form, apparent solubility, and dissolution behavior in ASDs prepared by the film casting–solvent evaporation. Thermal analysis and X‑ray diffraction examination (DSC, XRD) demonstrated a complete conversion of RTV from the crystalline to the amorphous state in most formulations, except the formulation containing 50% Copovidone, where total amorphization was not achieved. FTIR spectroscopy indicated non‑covalent interactions between RTV and polymers such as hydroxypropyl methylcellulose acetyl succinate (HPMCAS) and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose phtalate (HPMCP). Among the screened polymers, HPMCAS and Copovidone promoted the greatest improvement in apparent solubility, up to approximately 22-to-30-fold relative to crystalline RTV. Dissolution testing results exhibited that formulations containing HPMC P55, Eudragit L100‑55 and Eudragit E100 provided superior drug release. Increasing drug load in the ASD inversely influenced both the enhancement of apparent solubility and the ability to sustain supersaturation; high drug fractions in the solid dispersion promoted phase separation and surface precipitation of RTV, which impeded diffusion and reduced dissolution performance. Intrinsic dissolution and diffusion assays underscore the critical role of polymer selection in modulating molecular mobility and stabilizing the amorphous drug. Overall, findings in this study provide a scientific basis for applying amorphous solid dispersion to improve dissolution and enhance apparent solubility of ritonavir through appropriate polymer selection and drug loading optimization. Keywords: Amorphous solid dispersion (ASD), Ritonavir, Apparent solubility, Intrinsic dissolution rate.

papers.title: Synergistic Absorption Mechanism in Flexible Polymer Composites Reinforced with Rare Earth Cobaltite and Molybdenum Carbide for EMI Shielding Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract The sudden growth of digital devices and fifth-generation (5G) communication systems has generated increasing concerns regarding electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding in advanced technological applications, due to the high necessity for development of flexible, lightweight and efficient shielding materials. In this study, low thickness polymer composite films based on poly(vinylidene fluoride) polymer that is incorporated with gadolinium cobaltite and molybdenum carbide fillers were successfully fabricated through a solution casting technique. The chemical, structural, and morphological characteristics of the composite films were investigated using XRD, FTIR, FESEM, HR-TEM, tensile strength and contact angle. Thermal stability was assessed through thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and electromagnetic properties were evaluated in terms of complex permittivity and permeability across the X-band frequency range. The EMI shielding was examined in terms of shielding effectiveness due to absorption, reflection, and transmission and further validated using CST software. The selected composite film with an ultralow thickness of ∼0.15 mm exhibited a maximum EMI shielding efficiency of ∼49 dB in the X-band region with the absorption dominant shielding as the primary attenuation mechanism. The composite films displayed an enhanced mechanical strength and hydrophobicity behavior, making them suitable for flexible and durable shielding applications. These results suggest that the developed PVDF/GdCoO3/Mo2C composite films are promising candidates for advanced electromagnetic interference shielding applications in wearable electronics, stealth technology, and defense systems.

papers.title: Deep Learning for AD Risk Screening and Progression Prediction
papers.abstract: Timely intervention for Alzheimer's disease (AD) requires early detection. The development of immunotherapies targeting amyloid-beta and tau underscores the need for accessible, time-efficient biomarkers for early diagnosis. Here, we directly applied our previously developed MRI-based deep learning model for AD to the large Chinese SILCODE cohort (722 participants, 1,105 brain MRI scans). The model - initially trained on North American data - demonstrated robust cross-ethnic generalization, without any retraining or fine-tuning, achieving an AUC of 91.3% in AD classification with a sensitivity of 95.2%. It successfully identified 86.7% of individuals at risk of AD progression more than 5 years in advance. Individuals identified as high-risk exhibited significantly shorter median progression times. By integrating an interpretable deep learning brain risk map approach, we identified AD brain subtypes, including an MCI subtype associated with rapid cognitive decline. The model's risk scores showed significant correlations with cognitive measures and plasma biomarkers, such as tau proteins and neurofilament light chain (NfL). These findings underscore the exceptional generalizability and clinical utility of MRI-based deep learning models, especially in large and diverse populations, offering valuable tools for early therapeutic intervention. The model has been made open-source and deployed to a free online website for AD risk prediction, to assist in early screening and intervention.

papers.title: Structure–Performance Relationships in Metal–Organic Framework Mg 2 (olz) Catalysts for CO 2 Adsorption and Hydrogenation to Methanol
papers.abstract: We investigated a Cu–Zn‐modified Mg 2 (olz) catalyst for carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) hydrogenation to methanol under low CO 2 partial pressures, relevant to dilute CO 2 streams in industrial gas treatment and carbon capture. The catalyst was prepared via wet impregnation of presynthesized Cu–Zn species into the metal‐organic framework (MOF). Batch tests under mild temperatures and low CO 2 concentration showed that the MOF‐based system achieved higher methanol yields than a commercial catalyst at 150 °C. Step‐response experiments in a plug‐flow reactor revealed that the MOF retained a significant amount of CO 2 under high‐pressure and dynamic conditions. In situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy identified methanol‐related surface intermediates, while ex situ postreaction 1 H nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported the formation and retention of methanol and oxygenated species in the MOF‐based catalyst. X‐ray absorption spectroscopy showed partial reduction of oxygenated Cu species during reaction, while in situ X‐ray diffraction demonstrated structural stability of the Mg 2 (olz) MOF framework. These results indicate that Mg 2 (olz)‐based materials combine CO 2 adsorption capacity with catalytic functionality. Adsorption and catalytic functions coexist rather than being directly coupled. The material exhibits methanol productivity at low temperature in the presence of a solvent phase and remains structurally stable under the investigated catalytic conditions.

papers.title: MadAgents
papers.abstract: We uncover an effective and communicative set of agents working with MadGraph. Agentic installation, learning-by-doing training, and user support provide easy access to state-of-the-art simulations and accelerate LHC research. We show in detail how MadAgents interact with inexperienced and advanced users, support a range of simulation tasks, and analyze the results. In a second step, we illustrate how MadAgents automatize event generation and run an autonomous simulation campaign, starting from a pdf file of a paper. We also present successive MadAgents updates, including a Claude Code implementation with a self-improvement loop.

papers.title: Stromal VEGF-C expression predicts nodal metastasis: implications for axillary surgery de-escalation in breast cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is critical for de-escalating breast cancer surgery, sparing node-negative patients the morbidity of sentinel lymph node biopsy while ensuring appropriate staging for those at risk. Yet reliable molecular predictors of LNM remain lacking. VEGF-C, a key driver of lymphangiogenesis, is expressed in both cancer cell and stromal compartments, but its clinical utility is unclear. In a prospectively enrolled cohort, we assessed stromal and cancer cell VEGF-C expression by immunohistochemistry using both manual scoring and a novel automated image analysis script enabling objective, reproducible quantification of stromal versus epithelial VEGF-C fractions at scale. Stromal VEGF-C was independently associated with LNM after adjustment for established predictors (P = 0.004), with prediction models reaching AUCs of up to 0.784. Cancer cell VEGF-C added no predictive value. Critically, stromal VEGF-C showed potential to replace vascular invasion, which is a strong but preoperatively inaccessible predictor in LNM prediction models. Stromal VEGF-C assessment in preoperative biopsies could therefore enable more precise nodal staging, supporting informed surgical decision-making and the identification of patients who may safely avoid unnecessary axillary intervention.

papers.title: The two-level systems in cryogenic solids, or how to avoid stressful memories
papers.abstract: Structural glasses prepared by bulk quenching a liquid melt universally exhibit puzzling low-energy excitations commonly known as the ‘two-level systems’ (TLSs). Recent studies indicate that ultrastable glassy films made by vapor deposition exhibit substantially fewer TLSs and, at the same time, are more stable enthalpically than conventional glasses made by quenching a melt. A similar phenomenon is observed in very stable glasses of model liquid mixtures prepared using swap Monte Carlo sampling. However, in a separate set of enthalpically stable solids, exemplified by amber matured over geological times, the two-level systems persist. In addressing this seeming conflict, we emphasize that a depletion of the TLSs, if any, means the configurational entropy of the material is lower than that of conventional glasses made by bulk-quenching a melt. Ageing does induce reduction in configurational entropy, but amber, we speculate, achieves enthalpic stabilization through increased bonding, not ageing. We separately comment on the discrepancy among existing predictions for the extent of cooperativity of the two-level systems. Several experiments are suggested to test the present picture.

papers.title: CERES: a cryogenic experiment to reconstruct energy systematics in $$\hbox {TeO}_2$$ bolometers
papers.abstract: Abstract Cryogenic calorimetric detectors are a powerful tool in the search for rare events such as neutrinoless double beta decay ( $$0\nu \beta \beta $$ 0 ν β β ), due to their excellent energy resolution and low intrinsic background. The performance of these detectors depends critically on a precise understanding of their energy scale and energy resolution. Recent studies suggest that both energy scale and energy resolution may vary depending on the spatial location and topology of energy deposition within the detector, indicating the presence of previously uncharacterized systematic effects. The Cryogenic Experiment to Reconstruct Energy Systematics (CERES) is a dedicated experiment designed to directly measure the position dependence of calorimetric response in Tellurium Dioxide ( $$\hbox {TeO}_{2}$$ TeO 2 ) crystals. This paper details the experimental design, current status, and future upgrade plans for CERES.

papers.title: GaN Nucleation Landscape on Patterned Sapphire Shaped by the Growth Temperature of Directly Grown Boron-Compound Masks
papers.abstract: Abstract The growth temperature of directly grown boron-compound masks on patterned sapphire is associated with changes in the inferred effective accessibility of the underlying sapphire surface and in the subsequent nucleation behavior of GaN. In this work, we investigate how ammonia-borane-derived boron-compound masks grown at different temperatures shape the GaN nucleation landscape within circular SiO2 openings during the initial stage of epitaxial lateral overgrowth. The preferential nucleation position of GaN changes systematically with mask growth temperature: masks grown at 700−750 °C produce pronounced edge-biased distributions, whereas higher-temperature masks lead to more inward-shifted and spatially sparse GaN domains. Quantitative analysis of the GaN areal fraction, the number of visibly isolated domains, and the radial distribution of domain centers show that the mask growth temperature affects both the amount of GaN coverage and the spatial arrangement of GaN domains within each opening. The nonmonotonic change in the number of visibly isolated domains is interpreted as a consequence of competition between reduced lateral merging and reduced effective substrate accessibility rather than as a direct measure of the number of active nucleation sites. Coarse-grained kMC-type simulations provide a qualitative consistency test by varying the effective density and radial distribution of substrate-accessible sites. These results suggest that the growth temperature of directly formed boron-compound masks can serve as a pre-growth process parameter for tuning the early-stage intra-opening GaN nucleation landscape. This behavior is described in terms of effective substrate accessibility inferred from the GaN nucleation morphology, while the microscopic origin of the accessible regions remains to be resolved by direct structural characterization.

papers.title: Synthesis and characterization of 2-methylimidazole end capped Zwitter ion functionalized Polyaniline
papers.abstract: Abstract Due to the lack of functional groups, the processability of polyanilines (PANIs) are limited. Poor solubility in common solvents, high rigidity and hydrophobicity are the important problems associated with PANI. To enhance its processability, acid and amine groups were grafted onto the PANI backbone via a Friedel-Crafts (FC) alkylation reaction, carried out at 85°C for 6 hours under a nitrogen atmosphere with vigorous stirring. Prior to this, the PANI backbone was synthesized through free radical (FR) solution polymerization, initiated by peroxy disulphate (PDS), using aniline monomer at 0–5°C under nitrogen purging. A key modification during synthesis was the inclusion of 2 -methylimidazole ( 2 MI), which imparted hydrophilicity and facilitated end-capping of the polymer chains. The functionalized PANIs were thoroughly characterized by various analytical tools, antimicrobial properties and thermal properties. Following acid functionalization, the water contact angle (WCA) increased to 61.4°, attributed to the formation of Zwitter ionic structures, as evidenced by an FTIR peak at 1640 cm⁻¹. This modification also significantly improved the water solubility of PANI. The % yield of A3 sample was found to be low due to the availability of few reaction cite on the aromatic ring of PANI for second grafting reaction. A plausible reaction mechanism was proposed based on the experimental findings, which were carefully analyzed and compared with values reported in the literature.

Prior to this, the PANI backbone was synthesized through free radical (FR) solution polymerization, initiated by peroxy disulphate (PDS), using aniline monomer at 0–5°C under nitrogen purging. The % yield of A3 sample was found to be low due to the availability of few reaction cite on the aromatic ring of PANI for second grafting reaction.

papers.title: Characterization of the organelle genomes of mycoheterotrophic Thismia angustimitra and evidence suggesting horizontal gene transfer
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Our knowledge about mitochondrial genome evolution in plants is lacking far behind our knowledge of plastome evolution. In heterotrophic plants, it is well-known that plastome degradation and reduced or lost photosynthesis go hand in hand, and there is little if any difference between plastome evolution in mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites. The mitochondrial genome appears less affected by a heterotrophic lifestyle, although exceptions occur. In contrast to plastome evolution, mitochondrial evolution may differ between mycoheterotrophic and haustorial parasites, in particular with regards to the occurrence of horizontal gene transfer. However, data from mycoheterotrophs are scarce, and complete mitogenomes are only known from three of ten clades. Results Here we present data from the complete plastome and mitogenome from Thismia angustimitra , representing a fourth clade of mycoheterotrophs. The 18,215 bp plastome is much reduced and includes only few genes. The mitogenome has a multicircular structure consisting of 22 chromosomes with a total length of 422,400 bp. The gene content and the pattern of RNA editing are normal. The mitogenome includes only few repeats and recombinational activity is limited. A search for foreign DNA did not reveal any fungal sequences, and the content of plastid DNA is low. Just a few inserts appear to have originated through intracellular transfer, whereas others most likely stem from horizontal gene transfer. Conclusion The highly reduced plastome of T. angustimitra fits completely the general picture of plastome degradation in heterotrophic plants. Whereas the mitogenome in many aspects appears unaffected by the lifestyle, the recombinational activity is unusually low. Surprisingly, we find evidence of horizontal gene transfer, suggesting that this phenomenon may be more common among mycoheterotrophic plants than previously thought.

papers.title: Statistical shape model–based refinement of dental surface geometries for digital manufacturing workflows
papers.journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract Digital manufacturing workflows in dentistry require accurate and anatomically consistent tooth models derived from heterogeneous acquisition modalities. However, preliminary tooth segmentations obtained from CBCT or intraoral scanning often exhibit incomplete or ambiguous regions, particularly at interdental contacts, which can compromise downstream design and manufacturing processes. This work presents a fully automated, anatomy-aware refinement pipeline based on an enhanced Statistical Shape Model, designed as a post-processing stage for preliminary tooth reconstructions. The method integrates target geometries with population-based anatomical priors, explicitly preserving reliable surface regions while reconstructing uncertain or missing areas through a globally constrained statistical deformation. Semantic anatomical information embedded in the eSSM enables contact-aware refinement relevant to design-oriented applications. The pipeline was evaluated on adult maxillary first molars using target models derived from both CBCT-based segmentations and intraoral scans. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach produces complete, smooth, and anatomically plausible tooth models while maintaining fidelity to the observed geometry. The refined reconstructions are directly suitable for downstream manufacturing-related applications, reducing manual intervention and improving robustness within digital dental workflows.

papers.title: Hz-resolution wide-span photonic integrated terahertz signal analyzer
papers.abstract: Wide-span spectral and noise characterization at millimeter-wave and terahertz frequencies is increasingly important for emerging wireless, sensing, and spectroscopy systems, yet remains challenging for conventional electronic instrumentation because of the complexity and calibration burden of extender-, multiplier-, and mixer-chain architectures. Here we show that photonics can provide attractive alternatives to this highly challenging electronic instrumentation through an antenna-coupled thin-film lithium niobate electro-optic receiver. Our implementation performs fast spectral reconstruction across the widely separated WR 9.0 (80-125 GHz) and WR 2.8 (240-380 GHz) bands with a single component, with carrier-frequency errors below 3 MHz, scan speeds up to 25 THz/s, and a displayed average noise level below -104 dBm/Hz. We then extend to Hz-level resolution and demonstrate phase-noise characterisation capabilities across these ultra-wide bands by using a mode-locked femtosecond-laser frequency comb as a sampling clock, mapping high-frequency carriers to aliased intermediate-frequency tones. We validate the method by measuring the phase noise of 90.225 GHz and 270.675 GHz carriers using the same chip and system configuration. We further improve the sensitivity of the phase-noise measurement through cross-correlation between two optical probe-pulse channels. Finally, we show that the same technique can be applied synchronously to ten widely spaced frequencies distributed across more than 100 GHz, with the option to quantify their mutual coherence. These results establish TFLN integrated photonics as a scalable route toward compact millimeter-wave/terahertz instrumentation.

papers.title: Automatic generation of exchange–correlation response kernels
papers.abstract: Computing density-functional response properties requires contracting derivatives of the exchange–correlation (xc) energy with perturbed densities on a grid. While the xc functional’s derivatives have long been available to high orders from libraries such as Libxc, the surrounding contraction layer—the chain rule that combines them with the grid-based basis-function and density data into the total xc contribution—has instead been hand-derived and hand-coded in every program, for every functional family, spin case, and property. We present libxckernel, a library that automatically generates this layer by symbolic differentiation. The xc functional’s ingredients are expressed as sesquilinear forms in the density matrix, so the xc energy can be differentiated to any order while the functional derivatives remain opaque. The basis functions and the orbital coefficients may both be complex. The chain rule then produces any xc matrix element: Fock matrices, orbital Hessians, or any other response terms of any order. Terms sharing a pattern are collapsed for efficiency. Extensible plugins emit the expressions as NumPy Einstein sums, compiled C++ kernels with C/Fortran interfaces, or host-program specific source code. libxckernel is free and open-source software under the BSD-3-Clause license, enabling rapid implementation of functionality missing from many electronic structure programs. We demonstrate it by extending Psi4 with meta-generalized gradient approximation (mGGA) response kernels for orbital stability analysis and time-dependent density-functional theory (TD-DFT), GGA and mGGA analytic nuclear Hessians, and exact quadrature grid response, as well as by extending GPAW with mGGA and triplet TD-DFT kernels and gradient-corrected kernels for periodic dielectric response.

papers.title: Evaluating nursing performance during heatwave simulations: Protocol for a repeated measures cross-over study
papers.abstract: Abstract This study protocol combines clinical simulations with climatic chamber experiments, to evaluate 1) the impact of heat stress on hospital nurses’ physiological strain, physical and mental fatigue, vigilance, and clinical performance; and 2) the efficacy of a practical cooling intervention (i.e. electric fan) in mitigating the negative impact of heat stress. UK-based, registered adult nurses working in hospital settings will be recruited to partake in a repeated-measures cross-over design study, consisting of five separate 3-hour experimental sessions simulating clinical work, and taking place within a climatic chamber at Southampton General Hospital (UK). Sessions will differ by ambient temperature and cooling intervention as follows: 1) control (CTR; 18°C, 50% relative humidity [RH]); 2) warm (WARM; 26°C, 50%RH); 3) warm with electric fan (WARM+FAN; 26°C, 50%RH); 4) hot (HOT; 34°C, 50%RH); 5) hot with electric fan (HOT+FAN; 34°C, 50%RH). This study has been registered on a publicly accessible clinical trial registry ( ISRCTN45793399 ). During each session, participants will first complete a standardised fatigue-induction protocol simulating shift work (i.e. low-intensity cycling with cognitive tasks); followed by a simulated hospital ward round involving six simulated patients and two simulated cardiac arrest scenarios. Nursing cognitive and physical performance will be assessed using a standardised observational assessment battery, along with objective cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) performance metrics. Physiological responses will be assessed by monitoring changes in core temperature (T core ), skin temperature (T skin ), heart rate, and whole-body sweat loss (WBSL). Fatigue and vigilance will be measured using the Swedish Occupational Fatigue Inventory (SOFI) and Brief Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT-B), respectively. Baseline (i.e. prior to fatiguing protocol) to post simulation changes in 1) vigilance assessed via the PVT-B (i.e. a determinant of role-specific cognitive performance); 2) CPR quality score (i.e. a determinant of role-specific physical performance); and 3) T core (i.e. a determinant of thermo-physiological state); will be analysed using linear mixed models to determine the effects of ambient temperature and cooling intervention on nurses’ clinical and physiological performance. By providing a controlled methodological framework for assessing the effects of heat exposure on hospital nurses’ physiological, perceptual, and clinical performance, this study will provide empirical evidence on air temperature-related changes in nursing performance and physiological strain and the role of cooling interventions in modifying these responses. This will support the development of evidence-based climate adaptation strategies to protect healthcare staff wellbeing and maintain patient safety during periods of extreme heat.

papers.title: Investigation of the microstructural and magnetic properties of Ni on GeSn layers
papers.journal: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal processing of nickel (Ni) layers on germanium–tin (GeSn) can strongly modify the Ni film and the Ni/GeSn interface within a restricted thermal budget; however, the influence of GeSn crystalline quality on Ni–Ge–Sn interfacial evolution and the magnetic response of the Ni layer remains incompletely understood. Here, Ni (15 nm)/Ge 1 − x Sn x /Ge/Gd 2 O 3 /Si(111) heterostructures ( x = 0.08 and 0.10 ) were investigated following rapid thermal annealing at 573 and 973 K for 10 s using x-ray diffraction, pole-figure analysis, x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling, and temperature- and field-dependent magnetization measurements. Annealing at 573 K preserves the crystallographic texture of Ge 0.92 Sn 0.08 , whereas Ge 0.90 Sn 0.10 exhibits microtwin formation and reduced structural integrity. Annealing at 973 K, employed as a severe upper-bound thermal reference, causes extensive structural degradation in both heterostructures, with substantially greater deterioration in the higher-Sn sample. XPS depth profiling reveals progressive Ni–Ge–Sn intermixing accompanied by pronounced Sn surface segregation with increasing annealing temperature. Magnetization measurements show coexisting ferromagnetic and superparamagnetic contributions in the as-deposited and 573 K samples, whereas annealing at 973 K strongly suppresses the ferromagnetic response, producing highly unsaturated M ( H ) loops together with reduced saturation magnetization and coercivity. These magnetic changes are consistent with extensive interfacial alloying and dilution of the metallic Ni layer. This study establishes a direct correlation between GeSn crystalline quality, interfacial diffusion, and magnetic behavior.

papers.title: Functional edible films and coatings enriched with flower extracts: advances in bioactivity and food preservation
papers.abstract: Although flower-derived bioactive compounds have gained attention as potential functional additives in edible packaging materials, no recent review has critically focused on their extraction strategies, interactions with film-forming biopolymers, and applications in food preservation. This review critically discusses recent research on the extraction, characterization, and application of important flower-derived bioactive compounds, including anthocyanins, flavonoids, phenolic acids, carotenoids, and essential oils, in active and intelligent edible packaging. Contemporary extraction techniques, such as ultrasound-assisted extraction, microwave-assisted extraction, deep eutectic solvents, and supercritical fluid CO 2 , provide higher yields (up to ~14 mg/g phenolics and over 70% pigment recovery) compared to traditional techniques. Nevertheless, each method has specific advantages and drawbacks. These flower-derived bioactive compounds modify the mechanical behavior and physicochemical characteristics of natural polymer-based packaging matrices, including starch, pectin, chitosan, and protein systems, mainly through hydrogen bonding and polyphenol–matrix interactions. Active films show improved oxidative stability. Antioxidant activity may increase two fold to tenfold, while antimicrobial action can reduce microbial load by approximately 1–3 log CFU/g. Moreover, the mechanical response to these compounds depends on extract–matrix compatibility, with phenolic compounds acting either as plasticizing or strengthening components depending on the polymer system and concentration. Anthocyanin-rich flower extracts from hibiscus and butterfly pea provide pH-responsive color-changing behavior, making these intelligent packaging systems capable of tracking food spoilage. Food applications show shelf-life extension of 5–21 days in fruits, vegetables, and meat systems, mainly through antioxidant activity, antimicrobial effects, delayed oxidative deterioration, reduced microbial growth, and improved moisture regulation. In contrast, biodegradability and renewable biopolymer use should be viewed as sustainability advantages rather than direct preservation mechanisms. However, wider application of flower-extract-based edible films still requires further validation of scale-up feasibility, food-contact regulatory approval, migration behavior, sensory acceptability, and safety of released bioactive compounds.

papers.title: Enhancement mechanism of high temperature stability for in-situ oxide scale on high-entropy carbide coatings induced by rare earth
papers.abstract: Abstract For ultra-high temperature ceramic (UHTC) coatings used in aerospace thermal protection systems, enhancing the oxygen barrier capability and thermal stability of in-situ oxide scale during ablation is crucial for stable service. Herein, a high-entropy design strategy is proposed to boost the compactness and phase stability of oxide scales by leveraging multi-component synergistic effects. Three high-entropy carbide coatings, (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Sm)C (HEC-Sm), (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Er)C (HEC-Er) and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y-Lu)C (HEC-Lu), with better ablation resistance than ZrC, (Hf-Zr-Ti)C, and (Hf-Zr-Ti-Sc-Y)C coatings,were designed. HEC-Lu delivers optimal ablation resistance, featuring a linear ablation rate of -0.173 ± 0.012 μm·s-1, superior to HEC-Sm (-0.111 ± 0.032 μm·s-1) and HEC-Er (-0.144 ± 0.022 μm·s-1). This superior performance is correlated with higher Ti retention and stronger calculated Ti-O bonding, increasing Ti content in the oxide scale by 53.85 % and 33.33 % compared to HEC-Sm and HEC-Er, thereby inhibiting volatilization. Rare-earth (Sm, Er, Lu) incorporation can reduce the diffusion coefficients of Ti and O atoms in oxide scales by one order of magnitude at 2573 K compared with TiO2. Notably, Lu introducing yields a higher Mulliken population (0.279) for Ti-O bonds than that of Sm (0.268) and Er (0.274), which strengthens Ti-O bonds inside the oxide scale. This work presents a novel material selection scheme for anti-ablation coatings in extreme environments.

papers.title: Biomass to bioenergy transition through sustainable bioconversion and circular bioeconomy strategies
papers.abstract: Access to modern electricity and clean cooking technologies remains uneven across much of Africa, despite the continent's abundant biomass resources, which have the potential to enhance energy security while supporting the transition toward a circular bioeconomy. However, a substantial proportion of agricultural, forestry, municipal, and marine organic residues is still treated as waste rather than valorized within the formal energy sector. Morocco exemplifies this disconnect. Although the country has achieved near-universal rural electrification, biomass derived from agricultural and marine resources contributes less than 2% of the modern energy mix, highlighting that the principal challenge lies not in resource availability but in the development of efficient conversion pathways and integrated deployment strategies. This review examines recent advances in biomass-to-bioenergy technologies, with particular emphasis on sustainable bioconversion processes, including enzymatic hydrolysis, microbial fermentation, anaerobic digestion, and microbial fuel cells. Beyond evaluating technological progress, we assess research trends, innovation dynamics, and technology transfer through bibliometric and patent analyses to identify leading research areas, emerging technologies, and geographical disparities across Africa. We further discuss the role of life cycle assessment in evaluating the environmental sustainability of biomass conversion pathways and demonstrate its importance in identifying low-carbon alternatives capable of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. We conclude that Africa's energy sovereignty depends on moving away from generic policies toward integrated, country-specific deployment strategies that prioritize locally available biomass within circular bioeconomy frameworks.

papers.title: Baculovirus-Mediated Expression and Functional Characterization of a Glycyrrhizin-Specific Single-Chain Variable Fragment in Sf9 Cells
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Glycyrrhizin (GC) is a major bioactive saponin in licorice plants ( Glycyrrhiza spp.). A GC-specific single-chain variable fragment (GC-scFv) was constructed from anti-GC monoclonal antibody 2H2. To obtain a soluble recombinant recognition reagent for GC immunoassays, GC-scFv was expressed using a baculovirus–insect cell platform. Methods The variable heavy- and light-chain genes were amplified from 2H2 hybridoma-derived complementary DNA (cDNA) and assembled using a (Gly 4 Ser) 3 linker. The construct was transferred through pET-28a(+) and pCold I into pFastBac1Mel, which contains the honeybee melittin signal sequence for secretion in Sf9 insect cells. GC-scFv was recovered by nickel-chelate affinity chromatography and characterized using indirect competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (icELISA). The calibration curve was analyzed by semi-logarithmic regression using triplicate wells at each concentration. Results An anti-T7-tag Western blot detected GC-scFv at approximately 29 kDa in the eluate recovered from culture medium. Free GC produced concentration-dependent inhibition, with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 0.46 μg/mL and a semi-logarithmic calibration interval of 0.0488–3.125 μg/mL. The apparent limit of detection and apparent limit of quantification, defined as 10% and 20% inhibition, were 54.2 and 92.8 ng/mL, respectively. Cross-reactivity was 24.47% toward glycyrrhetinic acid 3- O -glucuronide, 6.52% toward glycyrrhetinic acid, and below 0.92% toward the remaining tested compounds. Conclusions The baculovirus–Sf9 platform produced GC-scFv with competitive binding activity toward GC. The recovered reagent and its assay characteristics provide a basis for developing recombinant antibody-based immunoassays for licorice-containing products.

papers.title: Pregnancy Risk Information Systems for Psychotropic Medications: A Practical Review for Clinical Decision-Making
papers.abstract: Objective This review aimed to summarize pregnancy risk information systems for psychotropic medications and recent evidence on reproductive safety, with the goal of improving clinicians’ awareness of drug-specific risk information relevant to individualized clinical decision- making in women with psychiatric disorders of reproductive age.Methods We narratively reviewed official reproductive safety information resources from Australia, Europe, Korea, the United Kingdom, and the United States, together with recent umbrella-review evidence on psychotropic medication safety during pregnancy. Information on selected agents was organized by drug class.Results National systems differed in structure and clinical utility. Australia and Korea retain category-based elements, whereas sources from Europe, the United Kingdom, and the United States provide more descriptive, context-based information. Antipsychotics were mainly associated with neonatal extrapyramidal or withdrawal symptoms and metabolic risk signals for selected agents. Mood stabilizers and anticonvulsants were more strongly associated with congenital malformations and neurodevelopmental disorders. Benzodiazepines and hypnotics were mainly associated with neonatal sedation, respiratory depression, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, and withdrawal symptoms after late-pregnancy or labor exposure. Antidepressants were associated with neonatal adaptation symptoms, persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, and postpartum hemorrhage. Recent umbrella-review evidence showed that most reported associations remained at suggestive or weak levels of evidence.Conclusion Psychotropic medication use during pregnancy should be guided by individualized risk–benefit assessment, integrating drug-specific safety signals, evidence quality, exposure timing, lactation and fertility considerations, and the risks of untreated psychiatric illness.

papers.title: Prevalence and Intervention Gaps for PTSD and CPTSD Following Interpersonal Trauma in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Objective The psychological burden of interpersonal trauma is a significant global concern, yet a critical gap remains in identifying and treating trauma-related disorders in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Following the introduction of the International Classification of Diseases 11th Revision (ICD-11), understanding the distinction between post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and complex PTSD (CPTSD) has become essential, particularly in resource-constrained settings where chronic trauma is prevalent.Methods We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines to examine prevalence of interpersonal trauma, PTSD/CPTSD prevalence, and available interventions in LMICs. Thirty-five studies were selected following independent data extraction and quality appraisal by two reviewers based on JBI Critical Appraisal and Cochrane Risk of Bias assessments.Results The findings indicate a substantial gap between high interpersonal trauma exposure and clinical recognition. Children, adolescents, and women were identified as the most vulnerable populations, frequently exposed to domestic and gender-based violence. While PTSD prevalence rates were high across LMICs, only three studies utilized the ICD-11 criteria for CPTSD. Regarding interventions, while evidence-based models such as trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy and narrative exposure therapy have been implemented, evaluation research in LMICs remains limited compared to the high trauma burden.Conclusion This review highlights a diagnostic lag and research-to-practice gap in LMICs, particularly concerning the CPTSD recently introduced in ICD-11. Addressing these disparities requires prioritizing implementation science frameworks, focusing on task-shifting models, cultural tailoring of evidence-based interventions, and the integration of digital health solutions to ensure sustainable care for vulnerable survivors.

papers.title: A biosynthetic paradox implicating dynamic zeaxanthin biosynthesis at the ER-LD interface
papers.abstract: Traditional metabolic engineering often treats lipid droplets (LDs) as inert storage sinks and assumes shortening enzyme-substrate distance inherently enhances pathway efficiency. Harnessing Yarrowia lipolytica for zeaxanthin production, we uncovered a pivotal “spatial paradox” challenging this conventional dogma. A selective shielding strategy first identified the hydroxylase Pa CrtZ as the primary biosynthetic bottleneck. Subcellular localization trials revealed that directly targeting Pa CrtZ to the β-carotene-rich LD surface unexpectedly yielded the lowest zeaxanthin relative fraction (9.87%), significantly underperforming compared to cytosolic (27.15%) or peroxisomal targeting (43.16%). To investigate this counterintuitive phenomenon, multidimensional engineering strategies were implemented to boost zeaxanthin accumulation. Subsequently, in situ , label-free stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy unequivocally demonstrated the co-localization of β-carotene and zeaxanthin within LDs, confirming that substrate inaccessibility was not the limiting factor. Guided by principles of LD biogenesis, these findings led us to conceptualize a dynamic endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–LD interface functional microenvironment model. We propose that robust Pa CrtZ-catalyzed hydroxylation is sustained predominantly at transient ER–LD junctions, where hydrophobic β-carotene "skimming" is dynamically synchronized with efficient O 2 and NADPH cofactor exchange. This model redefines lipid organelles as active, organized metabolic hubs beyond mere storage, offering a novel transformative framework for future organelle-targeted metabolic interface design.

papers.title: Terbium-Doped Graphene Quantum Dots: A Highly Efficient and Selective Fluorescent Nanoprobe for Vanillin Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Vanillin, an extensively used flavoring compound in our daily life, may lead to health problems when overused, adulterated, or poorly controlled in commercial settings, necessitating the development of sensitive and rapid detection techniques. In this work, terbium-doped graphene quantum dots (Tb-GQD) were synthesized using carbonization and chemical conjugation methods for developing an efficient fluorescent probe for vanillin detection. The structural and optical characteristics of Tb-GQD confirm that terbium is doped in GQDs, without disturbing the sp2 graphitic core of GQD, and efficient energy transfer from GQD to Tb3+ was observed from the photoluminescence emission studies. Upon addition of vanillin to Tb-GQD, a decrease in fluorescence emission intensity and a change in lifetime were observed, suggesting a dynamic, photoinduced electron transfer mechanism. The Tb-GQD shows a linear detection range of 0.2–85 μM with a detection limit of 13.2 nM. The synthesized fluorescent probe shows excellent selectivity, and was implemented in real-sample analysis with a good recovery range of 96.4–100.06% and an RSD below 3.6%. These findings show that Tb-GQD will serve as an efficient platform for detecting vanillin.

papers.title: Advances in Wire-Laser Metal Deposition: Bimetallic Fabrication, Defect Mitigation, and Future Directions
papers.journal: Lasers in Manufacturing and Materials Processing
papers.abstract: Abstract Wire-Laser Metal Deposition (W-LMD) is a transformative additive manufacturing technology that utilizes a laser heat source to melt metallic wire feedstock for the high-efficiency fabrication of large-scale, near-net-shape components. The technology is distinguished from other manufacturing processes due to its high material utilization efficiency and superior safety compared to metal powder-based systems. W-LMD systems are composed of a focused laser, a wire feeder mechanism, a multi-degree of freedom motion system, cooling system, and a shielding gas supply to prevent oxidation. Deviation in process parameters of the system components can lead to external defects such as stubbing (insufficient melting) and dripping (melting above the melt pool), or other forms of internal defects such as porosities. A key feature of W-LMD systems is their capability of fabricating bimetallic structures. This paper reviews key studies on W-LMD systems and their advancements in bimetallic fabrication. The review highlights the current gaps and required research work in the field for bimetallic W-LMD manufacturing and its significance.

papers.title: Evaluation of recovered Carbon black as a sustainable alternative to commercial Carbon black in solid tyre cushion compounds
authors: D. M. D. A. De Zoysa
papers.abstract: Pyrolysis is a sustainable solution for waste tyre (WT) management. Recovered carbon black (rCB), is a second highest by-product of tyre pyrolysis process, contains a high amount of carbon, ash and inorganic impurities. In the present study, rCB derived from WTs was upgraded through magnetic separation, ball milling, and purified treating twice with 2M HCl and once with 2M NaOH at 60⁰C for one hour using 2 g/mL rCB: leachate ratio to obtain demineralized rCB(drCB). Both raw rCB and drCB were characterized by particle size analysis, proximate and ultimate analyses, TGA, ICP-OES, FT-IR, XRD, and iodine adsorption. The drCB exhibited a substantial reduction in ash content from 22.20% to 3.42 % (by weight) and an increase in carbon content up to 94.41 % (% wt). The upgraded drCB was subsequently incorporated into solid tyre cushion compounds as a partial replacement for commercial carbon black (CCB, N550) to evaluate industrial feasibility. Physico-mechanical properties of the drCB compound demonstrated improved modulus, tear strength, hardness, and other properties such as tensile strength, rebound resilience within the industrial standard limits. These findings confirm the technical feasibility of rCB as a partial replacement of the filler in industrial solid tyre cushion compounds, supporting circular economy concept in the rubber and tyre industry.

papers.title: Preformulation Study of Aqueous Extracts of Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) Seed from Criollo and Hass Cultivars for Solid Dosage Forms
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Avocado (Persea americana Mill.) seed is an agro-industrial by-product with significant pharmacological potential. This study aimed to conduct a preformulation assessment of aqueous seed extracts from Criollo (M1) and Hass (M2) cultivars. Methods: The extracts were characterized for total phenolic content (TPC) and ABTS•+ scavenging capacity, and their compatibility with pharmaceutical excipients was evaluated in binary mixtures by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy with Pearson correlation and hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and isothermal stress testing (50 °C, 15 days) with HPLC quantification of epicatechin (IST-HPLC). Results: M2 showed significantly higher TPC (192.80 ± 4.90 µg GAE/mg) than M1 (27.08 ± 0.51 µg GAE/mg; p < 0.0001). ABTS•+ inhibition was 59.92 ± 1.76% for M1 (0.05 mg/mL) and 50.79 ± 1.19% for M2 (0.01 mg/mL). The DSC transition enthalpies of both extracts did not differ significantly (p = 0.1271). Maltodextrin and gum arabic were compatible with both extracts, suggesting that they could serve as common excipients for both cultivars, whereas the chemical stability of five M2 mixtures could not be determined by IST-HPLC. Sodium carboxymethylcellulose (CMC) was incompatible with M1, as shown by a 29.44 percentage-point decrease in epicatechin recovery (p < 0.0001), separate HCA clustering (Euclidean distance > 0.009), and the lowest FTIR spectral correlation (r = 0.990). Conclusions: These findings provide a scientific basis for the rational development of solid dosage forms from avocado seed extracts.
