papers.title: Gut Microbiota-Derived Trimethylamine N-Oxide (TMAO) and Its Association with Atherosclerotic Burden in Vegetarian versus NonVegetarian Populations: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Background: Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, has been associated with cardiovascular disease and atherosclerotic burden. Dietary patterns may influence circulating TMAO concentrations through differences in the availability of substrates for microbial trimethylamine production; however, the relationship between dietary pattern, TMAO, and subclinical atherosclerosis remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to compare circulating TMAO concentrations and carotid atherosclerotic measures, including carotid intima-media thickness (CIMT) and carotid plaque, between vegetarian and non-vegetarian adults and to assess the association between TMAO concentration and atherosclerotic burden. Methods: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted among 200 adults, comprising 100 vegetarian and 100 non-vegetarian participants. Demographic, clinical, anthropometric, dietary, and lifestyle data were collected using a structured questionnaire. Blood samples were analyzed for TMAO, lipid profile, glucose parameters, and renal function. Carotid ultrasonography was performed to assess CIMT and carotid plaque. Associations between TMAO and CIMT were evaluated using correlation and multivariable linear regression, while binary logistic regression was used to assess the association between TMAO and carotid plaque after adjustment for relevant cardiovascular risk factors. Results: Mean TMAO concentration was significantly higher among non-vegetarians than vegetarians (4.21 ± 2.05 vs 2.86 ± 1.34 µmol/L; p<0.001). Mean CIMT was also higher in non-vegetarians (0.69 ± 0.11 vs 0.62 ± 0.09 mm; p<0.001). Carotid plaque was present in 27.0% of non-vegetarians compared with 14.0% of vegetarians (p=0.022). TMAO showed a positive correlation with mean CIMT (r=0.38; p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment, each 1 µmol/L increase in TMAO was associated with a 0.018-mm increase in mean CIMT (adjusted β=0.018; 95% CI: 0.010–0.026; p<0.001) and higher odds of carotid plaque (adjusted OR=1.42; 95% CI: 1.13–1.78; p=0.002). TMAO concentrations were also associated with total cholesterol and LDL-C. Conclusion: In this cross-sectional study, non-vegetarian participants had higher circulating TMAO concentrations, greater CIMT, and a higher prevalence of carotid plaque than vegetarian participants. Higher TMAO concentrations were positively associated with CIMT and carotid plaque after adjustment for relevant cardiovascular risk factors. These findings support an association between circulating TMAO and subclinical atherosclerotic burden; however, the cross-sectional design does not establish causality.
papers.summary: Background: Trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived metabolite, has been associated with cardiovascular disease and atherosclerotic burden. Associations between TMAO and CIMT were evaluated using correlation and multivariable linear regression, while binary logistic regression was used to assess the association between TMAO and carotid plaque after adjustment for relevant cardiovascular risk factors. TMAO showed a positive correlation with mean CIMT (r=0.38; p<0.001).

papers.title: Formulation and Evaluation of Nanostructured Lipid Carriers for Enhanced Drug Solubility and Bioavailability
papers.journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: The present study was undertaken to develop and optimize CTZ-loaded nanostructured lipid carriers (CTZ-NLCs) using a Quality by Design (QbD) approach for improved drug delivery. Initially, Preformulation studies were performed to evaluate the solubility of CTZ in various solid lipids, liquid lipids, surfactants, and co-surfactants. Based on the solubility results, suitable formulation components were selected. The NLCs were developed using selected lipid, surfactant, and homogenization conditions. A Box–Behnken Design (BBD) was employed to investigate the effects of three independent variables, namely lipid concentration (A), surfactant concentration (B), and homogenizer speed (C), on drug content (Y1), entrapment efficiency (Y2), and drug release (Y3). The quadratic models obtained for all three responses were found to be statistically significant. The optimized formulation F9 was selected based on the desirability criteria and evaluated for physicochemical characteristics and drug release. FTIR analysis of F9 showed characteristic absorption bands at 3322.75 cm⁻¹ (O–H), 2972.73 cm⁻¹ (aliphatic C–H), 1720–1740 cm⁻¹ (C=O), 1585.20 cm⁻¹ (C=C), 1381.75 cm⁻¹ (C–H bending), 1032.69 cm⁻¹ (C–O), and 879.38 cm⁻¹ (C–H out-of-plane bending), which were within the reported ranges. The absence of major peak shifts or disappearance indicated compatibility between CTZ and the selected excipients. In-vitro drug release was performed using the dialysis membrane method in phosphate buffer pH 6.8 for 6 h. Overall, the study demonstrated that the QbD-based approach was effective for systematic optimization of CTZ-NLCs, and the optimized F9 formulation showed satisfactory physicochemical characteristics and controlled drug release, indicating its potential as a promising lipid-based drug delivery system.

Overall, the study demonstrated that the QbD-based approach was effective for systematic optimization of CTZ-NLCs, and the optimized F9 formulation showed satisfactory physicochemical characteristics and controlled drug release, indicating its potential as a promising lipid-based drug delivery system.

papers.title: Developing Creative Polymer-Centered Research Experiences within an Undergraduate Chemistry Curriculum
papers.abstract: Abstract The National Science Foundation Student Mini-grant Research Program (NSF SMRP) was created to expand access to research experiences for undergraduate students with limited opportunities to engage in summer internships or other external research opportunities. Unlike faculty-intensive, course-based undergraduate research experiences (CUREs) and resource-intensive undergraduate research experiences (UREs), these research experiences were intentionally designed to be creative, short-term, student-driven, and minimally faculty-supervised, making research participation more accessible. To provide research experiences to 35 students, 10 polymer-centered research experiences indirectly introduced students to polymer science. Enabled by the establishment of a Rheology and Thermal Analysis Instrumentation (RTAI) suite, the NSF SMRP supported students on projects that showcased how polymers are infused into nearly every aspect of their lives.

papers.title: Software-defined lock-in detection for photoacoustic gas sensing
papers.abstract: Introduction Photoacoustic spectroscopy enables compact and selective gas sensing, but its weak acoustic signals require effective phase-sensitive detection. Conventional PAS systems commonly rely on standalone lock-in amplifiers, which separate the demodulation function from excitation generation, sensor control, and data management, limiting system integration and reconfigurability. Methods This work presents a real-time software-defined digital lock-in amplifier that unifies modulation-waveform generation, phase-coherent signal acquisition, quadrature demodulation, configurable filtering, real-time visualization, and data logging within a single LabVIEW application interfaced with a National Instruments USB-6361 data-acquisition module. The S-DLIA was integrated into a CO 2 PAS platform employing a distributed-feedback diode laser at 4992.5157 cm -1 , a differential resonant photoacoustic cell, and second-harmonic wavelength modulation. It was benchmarked against a commercial SR830 lock-in amplifier processing the same photoacoustic signal under matched conditions. Results The sensor responded linearly to CO 2 concentrations from 100 to 1,000 ppm ( R 2 = 0.999). Allan deviation analysis at an integration time of 220 s yielded minimum detection limits of 0.505 ppm for the S-DLIA and 8.909 ppm for the SR830 under the tested configuration, corresponding to a 17.6-fold lower detection limit compared with the SR830. Continuous operation over 24 h at a fixed laboratory location tracked indoor CO 2 variations without apparent drift. Discussion These results validate the S-DLIA as a reconfigurable and flexible alternative to dedicated lock-in instruments in PAS, demonstrating the potential of software-defined synchronous detection for integrated gas-sensing systems.

papers.title: Lead-free soft hybrid materials for piezoelectric sensors: A paradigm shift from toxic lead-based ceramics to sustainable electronics
papers.abstract: The development of piezoelectric materials has significantly transformed modern electronic and sensing technologies, and their use has extended from extremely precise actuators to wearable self-powering devices. But the problem is that these materials are commonly made out of lead-based ceramics, and for example, lead zirconate titanate (PZT) contains 60% of lead. Such materials entail great risks to the environment and people's health. This extensive paper elaborates on the evolution of lead-free soft hybrid piezoelectric materials with special emphasis on bismuth iodide-based organic-inorganic hybrids that can be a safe choice of the electronic sensor market of tomorrow. The latest breakthrough research demonstrates that owing to a well-planned halogen bonding between the organic and the inorganic components of the material, there occurs a slight structural instability which in turn opens the way to the improved piezoelectric performance thus making the piezoelectric coefficients comparable to those of commercial PZT with zero toxic lead content (d 3 3 =161.5 pm/V). This review connects developments in sensing mechanisms, material chemistry, crystal engineering, wearable electronics, energy harvesting, and medical implants.

papers.title: Biomedical properties and emerging translational potential of bovine milk extracellular vesicles
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles have garnered significant attention in the biomedical field due to their potential as therapeutic agents and diagnostic tools. Bovine milk extracellular vesicles (BMEVs), in particular, have emerged as a promising tool in biomedical research due to their unique biocompatibility, stability, and ease of isolation. As an alternative to extracellular vesicles sourced from human cells, such as stem cells or blood, these naturally occurring nanovesicles are increasingly recognized for their dual role as potential therapeutic carriers and diagnostic candidates. To map the evolution and knowledge structure of the field, we conducted a CiteSpace analysis that reveals how BMEVs research has expanded beyond nutritional science to emerge as a versatile biomedical platform with rapidly broadening applications. Also, this review systematically examines the biogenesis, isolation techniques, and structural features of BMEVs, while highlighting their applications in drug delivery, disease therapy, and diagnostics. Current preclinical studies provide preclinical evidence supporting potential therapeutic applications. However, clinical safety, therapeutic efficacy, reproducibility, dosing, biodistribution, immunogenicity, large-scale manufacturing, and regulatory acceptance remain to be established. Future research should focus on optimizing drug-loading strategies, enhancing targeted delivery, and exploring novel biomedical applications.

papers.title: Thermochemical upgrading of cereal brans into pyrolytic chars for solid fuel applications
papers.abstract: Abstract The growing production of cereals in Europe generates large quantities of milling by-products, including cereal brans, whose valorisation is important in the context of circular bioeconomy and renewable energy production. Although brans are commonly used in food and feed chains, low-grade or surplus fractions may require alternative management pathways. This study evaluated the potential of selected cereal brans, namely spelt, oat, wheat, rye, barley, durum wheat, triticale and millet brans, as feed-stocks for the production of pyrolytic char intended for energy recovery. The brans were pyrolysed at 500 °C, and the resulting chars were assessed in terms of solid yield, ash content, higher heating value and energy-related indicators. The char yield ranged from 30.27 to 37.04%, depending on the feedstock. Pyrolysis increased the higher heating value from 16.58 to 22.80 MJ/kg in raw brans to 24.45–30.15 MJ/kg in the corresponding chars, confirming the effectiveness of carbonisation in improving the energy density of the solid product. However, ash content also increased markedly, from 3.69 to 7.36% in raw brans to 11.41–23.31% in the chars, indicating that mineral concentration is a key constraint for combustion-oriented applications. The integrated evaluation of heating value and ash load showed that oat, rye and durum wheat chars offered the most favourable balance between high energy content and relatively low ash burden. To conclude, cereal brans can be considered promising feedstocks for thermochemical upgrading into charcoal-like solid fuels, particularly when they are unsuitable for food or feed uses.

papers.title: Light-Activated Antimicrobial Coatings Based on Porphyrin-Functionalized Poly(vinyl chloride) Synthesized via MADIX
papers.abstract: Abstract Bacterial surface contamination is a significant public health concern, particularly for immunocompromised individuals, and has driven the development of self-sanitizing materials. Photodynamic inactivation (PDI)has emerged as a sustainable antimicrobial strategy that uses photosensitizers (PS) upon light activation. In this study, a porphyrin-functionalized xanthate was synthesized and used as a chain transfer agent in the MADIX polymerization of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under environmentally friendly conditions. PVCs functionalized with porphyrin and having varied molecular weights were fully characterized by MALDI-TOF-MS, 1H NMR, SEC, DSC, and TGA to determine their composition, molecular weight, dispersity (Đ), and thermal properties. The obtained polymers were applied as antimicrobial coatings on glass substrates pretreated with a PVC-co-poly(butyl acrylate) (PBA) film-forming layer, and their surface morphology was analyzed by SEM. The antimicrobial performance against representative Gram-positive and Gram-negative strains, Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, respectively, was assessed under three conditions: dark, blue light (BL), and white light (WL). BL exposure produced the most pronounced cellular effects, resulting in a significant reduction in bacterial viability. These effects were further confirmed by SEM analysis, which showed visible structural damage to the bacterial cells. Cytocompatibility was confirmed using normal human dermal fibroblast (NHDF) cells. The PS polymer coatings (0.09 mg/cm2) demonstrated strong antimicrobial activity under light exposure and low cytotoxicity, highlighting their potential as photoactive antimicrobial surfaces for biomedical and hygiene-sensitive applications.

papers.title: Structural characterization and prebiotic activity of a novel polysaccharide from rice bran
papers.abstract: The chemical structure and prebiotic activity of a novel rice bran polysaccharide (RBP) were elucidated in this study. RBP was determined to be a typical heteropolysaccharide composed of arabinose (6.95%), galacturonic acid (2.13%), glucose (82.93%), galactose (5.15%), xylose (2.07%), and glucuronic acid (0.78%). DSC, TG, and XRD indicated RBP to be thermally stable and predominantly in an amorphous form. Results from methylation analysis and NMR spectroscopy suggested the main backbone of RBP to be predominantly →4)-α-D-Glc p -(1→, and →4,6)-α-D-Glc p -(1→. Fecal fermentation experiments demonstrated that RBP promoted the production of short-chain fatty acids, facilitated the propagation of beneficial bacteria ( Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus ), and suppressed the proliferation of harmful bacteria ( Fusobacterium ) and pathogens ( Escherichia-Shigella ), thereby exerting probiotic effects. This study comprehensively analyzed the structure and probiotic activity of RBP and highlights its potential as a functional food.

papers.title: Crystal Engineering of Multicomponent Crystals of Norfloxacin with N-Heterocyclic Coformers: Structural Diversity, Solubility and Antibacterial Activity
papers.abstract: Abstract For decades, crystal engineering has provided an attractive approach for modifying the physicochemical properties of active pharmaceutical ingredients without altering their molecular structures while preserving their intrinsic biological activity. In this study, the design and synthesis of multicomponent crystal forms of norfloxacin with N-heterocyclic coformers (pyridine, pyrazine and quinoline derivatives) are reported. The obtained multicomponent forms were structurally characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Structural analysis revealed diverse hydrogen-bonding motifs, supramolecular architectures and π−π stacking arrangements, reflecting the structural versatility of the norfloxacin molecule in the solid state. The physicochemical properties of ten representative multicomponent forms were further investigated by thermogravimetric analysis, solid- and solution-state spectroscopic methods and equilibrium solubility measurements in simulated gastric and intestinal fluids. Biological evaluation included antibacterial activity assays against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria as well as cytotoxicity studies using human fibroblasts. The results demonstrated that the equilibrium solubility of the norfloxacin multicomponent forms strongly depended on the dissolution medium. A substantial differentiation was observed under simulated intestinal conditions. Most investigated multicomponent forms exhibited enhanced bactericidal activity compared with pure norfloxacin and maintained low cytotoxicity toward human fibroblasts. These results demonstrate that crystal engineering approach used for norfloxacin with N-heterocyclic coformers provides an effective strategy to generate structurally diverse multicomponent forms with promising physicochemical properties and pharmaceutical performance arising from solid-state modification.

papers.title: Natural bioactive compounds in estrogen deficiency-induced osteoporosis: Classification and an integrated gut microbiota-metabolite-immune-bone framework
papers.abstract: Postmenopausal osteoporosis is primarily driven by estrogen deficiency, while gut dysbiosis, inflammation, microbial metabolites, and immune reprogramming may modify bone loss, although current evidence remains largely preclinical or associative.Natural bioactive compounds, probiotics, fermented foods, and medicinal-food resources have emerged as potential interventions, but existing research is fragmented and rarely distinguishes direct skeletal effects from microbiota-dependent actions.This review proposes a hypothesis-generating microbiota-dependent classification, rather than a validated clinical system, comprising phytoestrogens; polyphenols, flavonoids, and terpenoids; polysaccharides and dietary fibers; probiotics and postbiotics; fermented foods and dietary-pattern interventions; and complex traditional herbal formulations.These interventions may act directly on bone cells or indirectly through microbial biotransformation, intestinal barrier-mmune signaling, endocrine and estrobolome pathways, and epigenetic regulation.We additionally propose a microbiota-etabolite-xtracellular vesicle microRNA-one marrow cell fate axis as an unvalidated regulatory model.Preclinical evidence is strongest for short-chain fatty acid-related and gut barrier-mmune mechanisms, whereas the skeletal roles of bile acids, tryptophan-derived metabolites, microbiota-associated vitamins, and extracellular vesicle microRNAs remain uncertain, particularly in humans.Future studies should prioritize causal validation and microbiota-stratified clinical investigations.

papers.title: YOLOv8-CNR: a lightweight fire and smoke detection model for forest fire scenarios based on improved YOLOv8
papers.journal: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
papers.abstract: Introduction To address irregular morphology and drastic scale variations of flame and smoke targets in forest fire detection, and the difficulty of lightweight models in balancing accuracy and real-time performance, this paper proposes YOLOv8-CNR based on improved YOLOv8n. Methods The model optimizes backbone, neck, and loss function: C3_ConvNeXtv2 enhances flame texture and smoke edge representation; RepNCSPELAN4 strengthens multi-scale flow and small-target smoke features; SIoU improves localization of irregular targets. Results On M4SFWD with its trajectory-level split, YOLOv8-CNR achieves 79.8% mAP50 and 39.4% mAP50-95 with 2.52 M parameters, improving 7.5 and 2.6 percentage points over tuned YOLOv8n, at 238.1 FPS. This split eliminates near-duplicate frame leakage across subsets. Because the test set consists entirely of six Scene 4 camera runs that are absent from both training and validation, the M4SFWD results are interpreted as controlled comparisons under a scene-held-out setting rather than same-distribution generalization. Cross-dataset transfer is further evaluated through zero-shot transfer: trained only on M4SFWD, the model achieves 78.3 and 82.7% mAP50 on SMOKE_dataset and FLAME_dataset, respectively. Retrained on these datasets, it achieves 90.2 and 90.4% mAP50, demonstrating favorable real-world applicability. Ablation experiments show complementary and partially overlapping effects among the three modules, with the complete model achieving a 2.6 percentage point improvement in mAP50-95 over the baseline. Discussion The proposed model improves overall and smoke-related precision and recall, while flame precision slightly decreases (81.1% vs. 82.4%), flame mAP50-95 increases from 42.0 to 45.2%. This method provides an efficient solution for real-time flame and smoke detection in complex forest scenarios.

papers.title: Breed-related differences in meat quality, hydrolyzed amino acid and nucleotide profiles, and metabolomic features of pigeons
papers.abstract: Breed-related differences in breast meat quality and chemical composition were evaluated in 28-day-old Shiqi, Dabao, and White King squabs ( n = 10 per breed). Dabao pigeons had the highest 24-h drip loss and largest muscle fibers, whereas White King pigeons showed the lowest drip loss and shear force, higher pH, lower L , and higher a and b* values. Hydrolyzed aspartic acid, serine, alanine, cysteine, and methionine were generally higher in Shiqi pigeons. Among nucleotides, only cytidine monophosphate differed among breeds. Untargeted LC–MS metabolomics showed clearer separation in comparisons involving White King pigeons. After multiple-testing correction, five unique differential metabolite features remained significant. Exploratory pathway analysis of the Dabao–White King comparison indicated linoleic acid and arachidonic acid metabolism, although each pathway was supported by limited features. Overall, breed-related variation in meat quality was accompanied by differences in muscle structure, hydrolyzed amino acid composition, and metabolic profiles.

papers.title: Management rather than climate and biodiversity shapes long-term delta15N dynamics in grassland soils
papers.abstract: The bulk soil δ 15 N signature in grassland soils serves as a fingerprint of nitrogen inputs, turnover and losses, reflecting the influence of land management, climate, plant biodiversity and abiotic soil properties.Although natural abundance δ 15 N has been proposed as an indicator for these factors, previous studies yielded mixed results regarding the importance of its drivers.In this study, we quantified changes in soil δ 15 N across 72 German grassland sites after 12 years (2011 vs. 2023) and analysed relationships with detailed records of land use intensity, plant biodiversity, climate, and soil properties.Land use intensity was quantified on a continuous scale based on mowing, grazing and fertilisation.In the top 10 cm of soil, δ 15 N changes ranged from -0.86 to + 2.49‰, equating to an average increase of + 0.35‰ per decade.Over two-thirds of our study sites showed a long-term increase in δ 15 N associated with high land use intensity.Our findings indicate that fertiliser application and grazing are the dominant drivers of δ 15 N increases, while a biodiversity-mediated decrease via reduced N losses was not observed.The slow decadal-scale shifts suggest that single soil δ 15 N measurements without known initial values are only informative for long-term management processes and not for assessing recent management impacts.

papers.title: A Quantitative Framework for Assessing Digital Sovereignty
papers.journal: UPM Digital Archive (Technical University of Madrid)
papers.abstract: Digital sovereignty is a political buzzword. However, there are diverging views on how to define and measure it. Throughout this study we propose the creation of a quantitative framework to measure digital sovereignty capabilities on a country's performance in three key areas: technology, government, and users. Through our analysis covering 123 countries, we have shown the different paths towards achieving sovereignty that are imprinted into how the countries contribute to the digital economy and reflect the asymmetries existing in the global value chains. The US and China both show a strong technological leadership, especially regarding emerging technologies, while the EU maintains a balance between innovation and regulations that the new strategies and MFF must address in order to become a relevant global player.

papers.title: Effects of Thermal Induction on the Structural and Functional Properties of Bamboo Shoot Protein
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: To develop novel plant protein resources and enhance the high-value utilization of bamboo shoot processing by-products, bamboo shoot protein (BSP) was extracted using ammonium sulfate precipitation. The effects of different heat treatment temperatures (room temperature, 50, 75 and 100 ℃) on the structural and functional properties of BSP were systematically evaluated. The results showed that heat treatment markedly altered the structural properties of BSP. SDS-PAGE analysis revealed that thermal treatment facilitated the aggregation of BSP, while scanning electron microscopy (SEM) indicated that the spherical protein particles became loose and porous after heating. Particle size and Zeta potential analyses showed that BSP treated at 50 ℃ exhibited the smallest particle size (1024.5 nm) and the highest absolute Zeta potential (14.42 mV), indicating good dispersion stability. In terms of chemical characteristics, the free sulfhydryl (-SH) content decreased with increasing temperature, while the water and oil binding capacities increased. In addition, BSP treated at 50 ℃ showed the highest foaming capacity (108.00%) and foam stability (37.24%). Thermogravimetric analysis (TG) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further demonstrated that BSP treated at 50 ℃ exhibited enhanced thermal stability; meanwhile, BSP exhibited good free radical scavenging capacity and reducing power. In conclusion, moderate heat treatment at 50 ℃ improves the structural and functional properties of BSP, providing a theoretical basis for its application in food processing.

In addition, BSP treated at 50 ℃ showed the highest foaming capacity (108.00%) and foam stability (37.24%). Thermogravimetric analysis (TG) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) further demonstrated that BSP treated at 50 ℃ exhibited enhanced thermal stability; meanwhile, BSP exhibited good free radical scavenging capacity and reducing power.

papers.title: Structural Characterization and Prebiotic Activity of Selenized Polysaccharide from Passiflora edulis Peel
papers.journal: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
papers.abstract: To investigate the potential of acid-extracted polysaccharides from the peel of Passiflora edulis Sims (APEP) as prebiotics, the APEP were complexed with sodium selenite. The selenized acid-extracted polysaccharide from Passiflora edulis Sims peel (APEP-Se) was successfully prepared. The physicochemical properties of APEP and APEP-Se were characterized. The structural characteristics of the samples were examined using a variety of analytical methods, including ultraviolet scanning, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, Congo red staining, thermogravimetric analysis, and scanning electron microscopy. The present study was conducted to ascertain the effects of APEP and APEP-Se on the growth of Lactobacillus plantarum, Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus, Lactobacillus brevis, and Streptococcus thermophilus. The physicochemical analysis revealed that, in comparison with APEP, APEP-Se exhibited increased uronic acid content but reduced total sugar content, protein content, and solubility. The selenium content of APEP-Se was 932.70±29.59 µg/g, thereby confirming the successful preparation of the selenated polysaccharide. Structural characterization indicated that both APEP and APEP-Se are composed of seven monosaccharides: Man, Rha, GlcA, GalA, Glc, Gal, and Ara, with Glc being the main component. After selenylation modification, the molecular weight of APEP-Se decreased from 281.05 kDa to 210.02 kDa. The infrared spectrum exhibited characteristic absorption peaks indicative of polysaccharides and selenylation modification. Additionally, the structure transitioned from lacking a triple-helical conformation to possessing a triple-helical structure, while thermal stability improved and the external morphology changed. Prebiotic experiments demonstrated that both APEP and APEP-Se effectively promoted the proliferation and metabolic activities of four probiotic strains—Lactobacillus plantarum, Lactobacillus delbrueckii (subsp.) bulgaricus, Lactobacillus brevis, and Streptococcus thermophilus—thereby exhibiting certain prebiotic effects. This study provides a theoretical foundation for the prebiotic application of selenium-enriched polysaccharides from Passiflora edulis peel, offers insights for developing them into novel functional foods, and indirectly promotes the resource reuse of the fruit peel.

papers.title: SYNTHESIS, CHARACTERIZATION, AND CATALYTIC ACTIVITY OF ZNZRO₃ MIXED METAL OXIDE FOR METHYLENE BLUE OXIDATION
authors: Ibraheem Asaad Ismaeel Zeina Loai Al-Yousef*
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Zinc zirconate (ZnZrO₃) is a mixed-metal oxide with potential applications in heterogeneous catalysis and advanced oxidation processes. In the present study, ZnZrO₃ was synthesized by the sol-gel method under the optimized experimental conditions previously established and reported by the authors.[1] The synthesized material was subjected to thermal treatment at different temperatures and characterized using differential thermal analysis (DTA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR) to investigate its thermal behavior, phase evolution, and structural characteristics. The catalytic activity of ZnZrO₃ was evaluated for the oxidative degradation of methylene blue (MB) in the presence of hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) under heterogeneous catalytic conditions. For comparison, NiZrO₃, which had previously been synthesized and characterized by the sol-gel method according to the authors’ earlier work[2], was evaluated under the same catalytic conditions. The results showed that the ZnZrO₃ phase was formed at high calcination temperatures, with the ZnZrO₃ phase obtained at 1000 °C. The catalytic experiments demonstrated that ZnZrO₃ exhibited higher catalytic efficiency toward MB oxidation than NiZrO₃, with catalytic efficiencies of 58.33% and 28.57%, respectively. These findings indicate that ZnZrO₃ possesses promising catalytic activity for the heterogeneous oxidative treatment of methylene blue using hydrogen peroxide and demonstrate its potential as a mixed-metal oxide catalyst for advanced oxidation applications.

papers.title: DEVELOPMENT AND OPTIMIZATION OF CURCUMIN UFASOMAL VAGINAL GEL USING DoE APPROACH
authors: Chaithanya Nagesh*1 Dr. J. Adlin Jino Nesalin1
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to develop and characterize a Curcumin-loaded ufasomal vaginal gel for vaginal cancer therapy to enhance drug permeation and therapeutic efficacy. Curcumin, a BCS Class IV drug with low solubility and permeability, was incorporated into ufasomes using the ethanol injection method. A Central Composite Design (CCD) was employed to optimize formulation variables, including oleic acid, Span 60, and cholesterol concentrations. The optimized formulation was evaluated for entrapment efficiency, particle size, zeta potential, in vitro drug release, and vesicle morphology. The optimized ufasomal formulation exhibited an entrapment efficiency of 61.8 ± 0.012%, particle size of 138 nm, zeta potential of 8.5 mV, and drug release of 78.2 ± 0.859% after 8 hours. FTIR and DSC studies confirmed the absence of drug–excipient interactions, while SEM revealed spherical vesicles with smooth morphology. The vaginal gel formulation showed desirable pH, viscosity, spreadability, and drug-content uniformity. These results suggest that the developed Curcumin-loaded ufasomal vaginal gel provides controlled drug release and could serve as a promising vaginal delivery system for improving the therapeutic efficacy of Curcumin in vaginal cancer.

papers.title: Cropland and population exposure to extreme precipitation events in Central Asia under future climate change
papers.abstract: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing rapid warming, leading to more Extreme precipitation events (EPEs). However, the anticipated changes in cropland and population exposure to EPEs are still unexplored. In this study, projected changes in EPEs characteristics, as well as cropland and population exposure from EPEs are quantified using global climate model simulations. Our findings reveal a significant increase in the exposure of cropland and population to extreme precipitation over time. Specifically, under the high-emission SSP5-8.5 future pathway, the amount, frequency, intensity, and spatial extent of extreme precipitation in CA are projected to considerably amplify, particularly in the high mountain regions. Under the SSP5-8.5 scenario, cropland exposure in CA increases by 46.4%, with a total cropland exposure of approximately 190.7 million km² expected between 2021 and 2100. Additionally, under the SSP3-7.0 scenario, population exposure in CA increases by 92.6%, resulting in a total population exposure of about 48.1 billion person-days during the same period. The future maximum centers of exposure are concentrated over northern Kazakhstan and the tri-border region of Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. Notably, the climate effect is more dominant than the other effects, whereas changes in population effect contribute to the total change in population exposure. Given the heterogeneous distribution of population and cropland in CA, it is imperative for the countries in the region to implement effective measures that harness extreme precipitation and cope with the impacts of these extreme climate events.
papers.summary: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing rapid warming, leading to more Extreme precipitation events (EPEs). Our findings reveal a significant increase in the exposure of cropland and population to extreme precipitation over time. Additionally, under the SSP3-7.0 scenario, population exposure in CA increases by 92.6%, resulting in a total population exposure of about 48.1 billion person-days during the same period.

papers.title: Effectiveness of a Theatre-Infused Script-to-Skills Teaching Model in Undergraduate Otorhinolaryngology Education: A Randomized Two-Period Crossover Trial.
papers.abstract: Background: Otorhinolaryngology teaching in undergraduate medicine is often compressed, and lecture-based delivery does not consistently sustain engagement or durable retention. Objectives: To evaluate whether a theatre-infused script-to-skills teaching model improves immediate knowledge acquisition, short-term retention, communication-related competencies, and learner satisfaction compared with conventional didactic lectures among final-year MBBS students. Methods: This randomized, controlled, two-period, two-sequence crossover trial included 60 final-year undergraduate medical students. Two otorhinolaryngology topics, chronic suppurative otitis media and deviated nasal septum, were taught sequentially. The intervention combined pre-session script preparation, doctor-patient role-play, facilitator-guided collaborative problem-solving, take-home reinforcement tasks, and structured feedback, while the control arm received conventional didactic lectures. Pre-test, immediate post-test, and two-week retention scores were analyzed, together with facilitator-rated communication, empathy, clinical reasoning, professionalism, collaborative rubric scores, and student satisfaction. Knowledge was measured using topic-specific 20-item single-best-answer multiple-choice tests scored from 0 to 20 at baseline, immediately after teaching, and after two weeks. Communication, empathy, clinical reasoning, and professionalism were rated with a four-domain analytic grid using 1-5 anchors; collaborative performance was scored with a 20-point rubric, and satisfaction was assessed on a five-point Likert scale. Results: Baseline pre-test scores were comparable between the groups in both study periods. The intervention produced higher immediate post-test gains for both chronic suppurative otitis media and deviated nasal septum. Retention scores at two weeks also remained significantly higher after the theatre-infused model. Communication, empathy, clinical reasoning, and professionalism scores in the intervention arm were consistently high, and learner satisfaction clearly favored the interactive strategy. Mixed-effects analysis confirmed the intervention as an independent predictor of improved post-test and retention performance. Conclusion: The theatre-infused script-to-skills teaching model was superior to didactic lecture for promoting knowledge gain, retention, communication-oriented performance, and student satisfaction in undergraduate otorhinolaryngology teaching. This model offers a feasible, learner-centered approach for strengthening clinically relevant undergraduate ENT education.

Communication, empathy, clinical reasoning, and professionalism were rated with a four-domain analytic grid using 1-5 anchors; collaborative performance was scored with a 20-point rubric, and satisfaction was assessed on a five-point Likert scale. Conclusion: The theatre-infused script-to-skills teaching model was superior to didactic lecture for promoting knowledge gain, retention, communication-oriented performance, and student satisfaction in undergraduate otorhinolaryngology teaching.

papers.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of REVIT in Supporting Sustainability Criteria in Buildings: A Case Study
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering and Sustainable Development
papers.abstract: This study examines the importance of BIM technology in construction projects and its major role in achieving sustainability, with a particular focus on the Revit software package. Its contributions to building sustainability were analyzed through a descriptive-analytical methodology involving an applied case study of a specific building modeled using Revit. The findings indicated that Revit plays a significant role in promoting building sustainability through its contribution to improving the indoor environment of buildings and achieving thermal and visual comfort, with direct implications for energy savings, as it enables designers to take into account solar movement and prevailing wind direction at the construction site. It also contributes to detecting clashes and conflicts before they occur during construction. In addition, Revit plays an important role in water conservation, as it enables accurate identification of pipe diameters used in plumbing and drainage systems, as well as their quantities, lengths, required fittings, bends, expected maintenance points, and other related data. The study concluded that BIM technologies should be adopted in the construction industry, particularly Revit, due to their major benefits in improving building quality and achieving the desired level of sustainability.

papers.title: Natural leather enabled skin-friendly, multifunctional and durable flexible display with integrated electroluminescent displaying and electromagnetic interference shielding performances
papers.abstract: Next-generation displays demand flexibility with skin-friendliness, durability and multifunctionality for emerging applications. Herein, a skin-friendly, multifunctional and durable flexible display with integrated electroluminescent displaying and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding performances was developed by the engineering of natural leather using leather retanning and finishing derived treatment processes. Polypyrrole was in-situ grown on natural leather via retanning-like process to fabricate the conductive leather, followed by successive coating of the electroluminescent layer and the top electrode layer through finishing-like process, thus obtaining a novel multifunctional natural leather-based flexible display. The conductive leather served as flexible bottom electrode to work with other functional layers to endow the flexible display with high-luminance and patterned color-tunable electroluminescence, which also presented strong durability after 1000 bending cycles or water washing. The conductive leather with unique hierarchically fibrous structure also facilitated the flexible display to achieve high EMI shielding effectiveness. Moreover, the collagenous nature of natural leather guaranteed the skin-friendliness of the flexible display with exceptional water-vapour transmission rate. Therefore, engineering the skin-friendly natural leather showed intriguing advantages to achieve durable, high-quality electroluminescent displaying and high-performance EMI shielding performances.

Herein, a skin-friendly, multifunctional and durable flexible display with integrated electroluminescent displaying and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding performances was developed by the engineering of natural leather using leather retanning and finishing derived treatment processes. Therefore, engineering the skin-friendly natural leather showed intriguing advantages to achieve durable, high-quality electroluminescent displaying and high-performance EMI shielding performances.

papers.title: Parasocial Interaction and Perceived Value as Determinants of Intention to Buy Made-in-Thailand Products through Live- Streaming Personal Shoppers
papers.journal: International Review of Management and Marketing
papers.abstract: This research investigates the rising trend of live shopping and jasa titipan (jastip) in Southeast Asian digital commerce, focusing on the growing popularity of Made in Thailand products among Indonesian consumers. Livestream commerce has changed consumer behaviour by offering immediacy, interactivity, and immersive digital experiences that lessen psychological distance between sellers and buyers. In Indonesia, live personal shopper sessions have become a key method for cross-border purchases of Thai cosmetics, fashion items, herbal supplements, and packaged foods, which are widely viewed as authentic and high-quality. Despite the market's rapid growth, previous research has mostly examined individual aspects like interactivity, trust, or entertainment, with limited attention to understanding the combined psychological factors influencing purchase intentions in livestream shopping. This study develops and tests a structural equation model (SEM) that includes social presence, parasocial interaction, perceived trust, perceived value, and perceived enjoyment to explain Indonesian consumers’ willingness to buy Thai products via live personal shoppers. The model captures both utilitarian and hedonic evaluation aspects, showing how relational bonding, immediacy, credibility cues, and experiential enjoyment collectively reduce uncertainty in cross-border transactions. This work contributes to theory by providing a comprehensive framework for understanding purchase intention formation in livestream commerce. Practically, the findings suggest strategic approaches for personal shoppers and digital platforms to enhance credibility and build consumer trust. Additionally, the study supports SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), and SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) through sustainable digital trade and inclusive economic participation.

papers.title: Plasma-Induced Surface Functionalization of Polymer Powders for Integration into UV-Resistant Functional Composites
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering and Sustainable Development
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effects of plasma surface treatment on the thermal and morphological properties of polyamide 12 (PA12) powder. The powders were treated for 1 h and 2 h under full power in an air environment. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) results demonstrated that the plasma action improved the maximum decomposition temperature from 449.3 °C for the untreated polyamide 12 to 461.7 °C for the 2-h-treated sample, indicating improved thermal stability. The analysis of differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) revealed a marked increase in the temperature of crystallization (Tc) from 133.31 °C for the untreated PA12 sample to 141.7 °C for the 2-h sample, while the melting temperature is approximately constant at 185 °C. The SEM images demonstrated that plasma treatment resulted in a roughened, more homogeneous surface morphology with significantly fewer surface defects and irregularities. Plasma treatment enhanced the wettability and water dispersion of PA12, as plasma-treated powders showed fast spreading and stable suspension in water due to the introduction of polar groups and increased surface pores. The change from a water-hating grouping to a water-loving scattering provides a strong basis for water-based processing and future composite design that will need strong interfacial interactions. Thus, these results confirmed the importance of plasma treatment as an environmentally friendly method in tailoring the properties of PA12 for UV-resistant applications.

papers.title: Neutron Depth Profiling: The Core Link Connecting the Microscopic Mechanisms of Lithium‐Ion Batteries With Intelligent Design
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Neutron Depth Profiling (NDP) is a non‐destructive, in situ quantitative depth‐analysis technique underpinned by neutron‐induced nuclear reactions. Offering high 6 Li‐isotope sensitivity and nanometer‐to‐micrometer depth resolution, NDP delivers isotope‐resolved lithium spatial information hardly accessible via conventional probes including secondary‐ion mass spectrometry (SIMS), X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and operando neutron imaging, yet it suffers from depth‐dependent resolution degradation, limited lateral performance, and requires large‐scale neutron‐beam facilities. This paper systematically reviews NDP fundamentals, global neutron‐source progress, and cutting‐edge battery applications, covering lithium‐ion migration in electrodes, lithium dendrite nucleation and growth, and the “reversible short‐circuit” effect at solid‐electrolyte interfaces. The unique merit of NDP for quantitative 6 Li depth‐profiling is highlighted, while noting that NDP cannot independently resolve full‐element maps or nanoscale interfaces and demands complementary characterizations. A roadmap integrating NDP with multimodal measurements and physics‐informed machine learning for intelligent battery design is outlined, alongside open challenges: inversion non‐uniqueness under low‐signal conditions and translation from model cells to practical batteries. This work provides actionable guidelines to leverage NDP for bridging microscopic lithium mechanisms and rational design of next‑generation batteries with high safety and high energy density.

papers.title: Preparation, Characterization, and Evaluation of Tetrabutylphosphonium Octanoate Reinforced Chitosan/Polyvinyl Alcohol Composite Films as Biodegradable, Antibacterial, and Antioxidant Active Food Packaging Materials
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Bioplastics have become an alternative green source for implementing a circular economy as a result of the globally prevalent pollution caused by traditional petroleum‐based plastic packaging. Chitosan (CS) is a crucial biopolymer with potential applications in numerous fields due to its biocompatibility and biodegradability. However, the CS used to make food packaging films is not particularly flexible or durable. In order to overcome this problem, tetrabutylphosphonium octanoate (TBPOct) ionic liquid (IL) functionalized polymeric films using CS and polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) have been synthesized. The effect of varying concentrations of IL (0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80%) and that of the biopolymer was thoroughly studied to optimize the biofilm composition with desired properties. The recently developed bioplastic films were evaluated by using multiple physical tests, including water solubility, film thickness, moisture content, and swelling properties, as well as spectroscopic methods like Fourier transform infrared (FTIR), thermal gravimetric analysis (TGA), opacity testing, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM).

papers.title: Synergistic graphene immobilization and electrolyte engineering enables durable lithiated organic cathodes
papers.abstract: Lithiated small-molecule organic carbonyl compounds are promising cathode candidates for lithium-ion batteries yet suffer from severe electrolyte dissolution and low electronic conductivity, which severely compromise their cycling stability and rate capability. Herein, we propose a synergistic strategy combining graphene immobilization and localized high-concentration electrolyte (LHCE) regulation to overcome these limitations. Specifically, a typical lithiated cathode, 8 O-4Li, is uniformly anchored on graphene via π–π interactions, constructing a conductive composite (8 O-4Li@G) with inhibited molecular dissolution and accelerated electron transfer. The LHCE further suppresses solvent-induced active material loss. The integrated design enables the 8 O-4Li@G composite to deliver a high reversible capacity of 219 mAh g −1 at 0.02 A g −1 with a high average discharge voltage of 3.5 V, achieving a remarkable energy density of ~760 Wh kg −1 based on the mass of 8O-4Li. Furthermore, it achieves impressive cycling stability with 96% capacity retention over 300 cycles at 1 A g −1 and superior rate capability. This work presents an effective strategy to unlock the full potential of lithiated organic cathodes for high-energy-density batteries.

papers.title: Self-aggregation separation of microplastics from water induced by topological cationic organogels
papers.abstract: This work reveals a novel functionality and mechanism for the electric field-induced self-aggregation separation of microplastics from water, mediated by a topological cationic organogel. Nine self-synthesized topological cationic organogels were adopted as model probe materials, and analysis of their structure–activity relationships revealed that the densely secondary-crosslinked poly(amine salt) gel (PMASG) exhibited a superior treatment capacity of 2426.80 mg/g for polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs), significantly outperforming most reported analogous materials. Furthermore, PMASG maintained a stable treatment performance in different water environments and for various types of other microplastics (PET, PVC, PTFE), and achieved efficient removal in ultra-dilute systems with microplastic concentrations as low as 0.01 mg/L, demonstrating excellent practical application potential. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated that the post-treatment residue can be completely thermally degraded under an inert atmosphere and possesses favorable combustion characteristics in air (ignition temperature: 328.96 °C, burnout temperature: 761.9 °C, comprehensive combustion characteristic index: 3.39 × 10 −5 ), enabling the elimination of post-treatment solid waste and achieving a green cycle for valorization. Based on kinetic/thermodynamic behavior studies and multi-spectroscopic micro/mesoscopic structural evolution analysis, a novel localized electrostatic-induced nucleation-driven self-aggregation (LEIN-SA) mechanism was established. In this mechanism, the topological cationic network of PMASG generates a localized electrostatic field that destabilizes and captures nearby microplastics, leading to the formation of a critical PMASG–PS composite cluster (nucleus). and subsequently driving the rapid aggregation of microplastics in water. In summary, this study develops a new strategy for water microplastic pollution remediation that combines ultra-high efficiency and total environmental friendliness.

In summary, this study develops a new strategy for water microplastic pollution remediation that combines ultra-high efficiency and total environmental friendliness.

papers.title: PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
papers.abstract: Protein phosphorylation cascades are essential for cell proliferation. Here, we identify protein arginine methyltransferase 1 (PRMT1) as a key stabilizer of phosphoproteins that is indispensable for hepatocyte proliferation during liver regeneration. PRMT1 is upregulated by epidermal growth factor (EGF) via receptor tyrosine kinase signaling and catalyzes the asymmetric dimethylation (ADMA) modification of SKP1 at the R81 residue. This methylation event disrupts FBXW7 recruitment to the SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein (SCF) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex, thereby preventing FBXW7-mediated ubiquitination. Since FBXW7 targets multiple pro-proliferative phosphoproteins, this mechanism prevents their degradation, ensuring the transduction of proliferative signals via phosphorylation cascades. Furthermore, in vivo administration of S-adenosylmethionine, the methyl donor for PRMT-catalyzed methylation, significantly accelerates liver regeneration in both mice and patients. Collectively, these findings establish PRMT1 as a central post-translational regulator of hepatocyte proliferation, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target for liver diseases. During liver regeneration, EGF upregulates PRMT1, leading to increased asymmetric arginine dimethylation at R81 of SKP1. This impedes the interaction between SKP1 and FBXW7, protects pro-proliferative phosphoproteins from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, and thereby maintains hepatocyte proliferation.

papers.title: AI-to-Capability Conversion in SMEs: The Mediating Role of Digital Sales Capability in Shaping Entrepreneurial Preparedness
papers.journal: International Review of Management and Marketing
papers.abstract: This study develops and empirically validates an AI-Augmented Digital Sales Capability and Entrepreneurial Preparedness framework explaining how artificial intelligence translates into entrepreneurial readiness among SMEs. Contrary to the assumption that AI directly enhances preparedness, the findings show that AI functions primarily as an enabling resource whose impact is realized through Digital Sales Capability. Drawing on Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study conceptualizes preparedness as a capability-driven outcome rather than a result of mere technology adoption. Using a quantitative design and PLS-SEM on 346 SME respondents in the Philippines, the results reveal that Digital Sales Capability is the strongest predictor of Entrepreneurial Preparedness, while AI Utilization exerts both direct and significantly stronger indirect effects through capability mediation. The model demonstrates strong reliability, validity, explanatory power, and predictive relevance, confirming its robustness in explaining digital entrepreneurial readiness. Findings further highlight a persistent digital execution gap, where SMEs possess AI tools but lack the capability to convert them into actionable sales intelligence and market responsiveness. This study contributes to entrepreneurship literature by reconceptualizing AI as a resource trigger within a capability transformation process, extending Dynamic Capabilities Theory into AI-augmented contexts. It offers a validated explanatory model for understanding how SMEs evolve into future-ready ventures in digitally intensive environments.

papers.title: From Waste to Function: Phase Change Composites of Lead-Containing Recycled Nanosilica/ Paraffin/Silicon rubber
papers.abstract: Polymeric Phase Change Materials (PCMs) are widely used for energy storage and thermal management, but their performance is often limited by leakage, low latent heat, and poor thermal conductivity. This study addresses these challenges by utilizing recycled lead-containing silica (Pb-silica) from spent lead-acid battery separators as a supporting material for form-stable PCMs (FSPCMs) integrated into a silicone rubber matrix. The composites were characterized using FESEM, EDS, ICP, BET, DLS, FTIR, DSC, thermal conductivity, and tensile testing, alongside leakage behavior evaluations. Results show that Pb-silica provides a latent heat of ∼88 J/g, comparable to commercial silica, with slightly higher leakage due to its lower specific surface area. Importantly, the incorporation of Pb-silica increased the thermal conductivity by up to 40.7% compared with silicone rubber, whereas the corresponding increase achieved with commercial A70-silica was 19.1%. This work presents a potential approach for utilizing battery waste to produce form-stable PCMs for thermal management applications.

papers.title: Upcycling of polyethylene terephthalate sourced from waste plastic bottles into graphene oxide and its evaluation for CO2 absorption
papers.abstract: The human-made “plastic” resource has turned into an environmental concern for years now. The ideal solution to the problem is still under research. Our research aims to deplete the huge amount of plastic waste on Earth by converting it into a functional material. The carbon chain of this polymer cannot be broken; however, it can be altered into a different category. Plastic waste, specifically PET, was chosen for the experiment and was converted finally into graphene oxide. Catalytic graphitization was used to convert one carbon form into another. The obtained graphene oxide was characterized using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, energy dispersive spectroscopy, thermal analysis, and electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. The FT-IR and EDS results confirm the synthesis of graphene oxide. The thermal stability and magnetic behavior of graphene oxide are satisfactory. Catalytic behavior toward CO 2 adsorption is a potent application of PETGO. The desorption curve indicates CO2 adsorption on the surface through chemisorption. A high amount of desorbed CO2 indicates a high reaction surface area and electronic interaction.

papers.title: AI in HRM: a unified model of AI capabilities and process efficiency for enhanced HRM effectiveness
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming human resource management (HRM) by supporting recruitment, training, performance management, workforce planning, talent analytics, and employee engagement. Nevertheless, limited evidence explains how different AI-enabled HRM practices contribute to process efficiency, decision-making, workforce agility, and overall HRM effectiveness. This study examined six AI-enabled HRM capabilities through an integrated Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory framework. The proposed model included AI in Recruitment and Selection, Training and Development, Performance Management, Strategic HR Planning, Talent Analytics and Retention, and Employee Engagement and Wellbeing. HR Process Efficiency, Decision-Making Accuracy, and Workforce Agility and Innovation were examined as organizational mechanisms contributing to Enhanced HRM Effectiveness. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 256 h professionals from public-sector, private-sector, and higher-education settings in Saudi Arabia and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. The findings showed that recruitment and performance-management AI were positively associated with HR process efficiency, while strategic-planning and talent-analytics AI were positively associated with decision-making accuracy. Employee engagement and wellbeing AI was positively associated with workforce agility and innovation. However, training and development AI was not significantly associated with process efficiency, and decision-making accuracy was not significantly associated with enhanced HRM effectiveness. The study demonstrates that the contribution of AI to HRM effectiveness depends on the HR function and the organizational mechanism involved. The findings provide theoretical and practical guidance for integrating AI with HR expertise, organizational routines, workforce capabilities, and responsible governance.

The findings showed that recruitment and performance-management AI were positively associated with HR process efficiency, while strategic-planning and talent-analytics AI were positively associated with decision-making accuracy.

papers.title: Ionic lipid–surfactant complex based on phosphatidylcholine and sodium dodecyl sulfate for enhanced curcumin encapsulation and sustained delivery
papers.abstract: Developing stable, efficient nanocarriers for hydrophobic anticancer agents remains a major challenge in pharmaceutical nanotechnology. In this study, we engineered a novel ion-pair amphiphile through electrostatic complexation between zwitterionic phosphatidylcholine and the anionic surfactant sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), forming a phosphatidylcholine–SDS (P-SDS) ionic complex with enhanced hydrophobicity and self-assembly capability. The resulting hybrid amphiphile was further stabilized with Tween-80 and formulated into nanoscale micellar structures to encapsulate curcumin. 1H-NMR and FT-IR spectroscopy confirmed the formation of the P-SDS ionic complex, while DSC analysis showed the disappearance of crystalline curcumin, indicating successful amorphous dispersion within the micellar core. Fluorescence spectroscopy revealed a low critical micelle concentration (CMC) of 3.1 × 10−4 M, suggesting favorable thermodynamic stability of the self-assembled system. Dynamic light scattering measurements showed an average particle size of approximately 239 nM with a strongly negative zeta potential ranging from −37 to −44 mV, indicating good colloidal stability. The optimized formulation achieved 19% drug loading with an encapsulation efficiency of 39.8%. In vitro release studies showed a biphasic release profile: an initial moderate burst followed by sustained curcumin release over 72 h. Morphological analyses using ESEM and TEM confirmed the formation of spherical nanoscale assemblies with relatively uniform morphology. The developed P-SDS nanoassembly is a simple, scalable, and biocompatible platform for delivering hydrophobic therapeutic agents. The ion-pair engineering strategy proposed in this work provides a versatile approach to tuning amphiphilicity, self-assembly behavior, and drug-loading capacity in lipid-based nanocarriers, with potential applicability for passive tumor targeting through the enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effect.

papers.title: Performance Evaluation of Radio Frequency Identification Tag Antenna for Commercial Applications
papers.journal: Journal of Engineering and Sustainable Development
papers.abstract: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) has emerged as an effective technology for automatic identification across industries due to its capability to use radio signals while providing security. The most common type is the passive RFID tag, consisting of an RFID chip and an antenna. The tag's antenna plays a crucial role in determining system performance and impacting various metrics. This paper investigates different designs of commercial tag antennas. With computer processing, selecting the optimal design for business applications becomes more flexible, minimizing the need for specialized expertise. These tags are widely available at low costs, reducing reliance on antenna design tools. The procedure outlined in this paper provides a method for evaluating tag performance. Three standard Ultra High Frequency (UHF) RFID antenna models- tag 1, tag 2, and tag 3- were simulated and evaluated in the 0.6-2 GHz range using the Antenna Toolbox in MATLAB. Comparison metrics include return loss, mismatch loss, bandwidth (BW), and current distribution. The second tag design achieved the best return loss of 18 dBm and a lower Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) of 1.4 dB, while the first design offered the longest range between the tag and the reader.
papers.summary: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) has emerged as an effective technology for automatic identification across industries due to its capability to use radio signals while providing security. The procedure outlined in this paper provides a method for evaluating tag performance. Three standard Ultra High Frequency (UHF) RFID antenna models- tag 1, tag 2, and tag 3- were simulated and evaluated in the 0.6-2 GHz range using the Antenna Toolbox in MATLAB.

papers.title: Robust perovskite lattice for durable and efficient pure-red light-emitting diodes
papers.abstract: Metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes are rising as promising candidates for next-generation display technologies. The bromine-iodine mixed halide perovskites contribute to straightforward emitters for pure-red emission, however, suffering from limited electroluminescent durability and efficiency due to highly sensitive optical properties to the featured soft lattice. Here, we report robust perovskites by intrinsically reinforcing the lattice with synergistic rigid ring ammonium and dedicated electrostatic polymer. We reveal the mechanism of enhanced lattice stiffness by sequentially clarifying the rigid cation-induced high atomic packing factor and the electrostatic polymer-derived strong octahedral Coulomb force. The resultant perovskites exhibit more than 100% improvement in bulk modulus and over 75% decrease in bond angle fluctuation under a high electric field of 107 V m−1. The robust perovskite lattice strongly suppresses the electric field-induced lattice distortion and ion migration, and strengthens the carrier radiative recombination. Consequently, we demonstrate durable and efficient pure-red PeLEDs with a long lifetime of 343.3 h and a high external quantum efficiency of 31.3%. Moreover, we reveal good compatibility of this approach in boosting the blue and green device performances. Mixed-halide perovskites enable pure-red displays but suffer from poor durability and efficiency because their soft lattices distort. Zhou et al. stiffened the lattice with rigid ammonium rings and an electrostatic polymer, producing durable, efficient devices.
papers.summary: Metal halide perovskite light-emitting diodes are rising as promising candidates for next-generation display technologies. Consequently, we demonstrate durable and efficient pure-red PeLEDs with a long lifetime of 343.3 h and a high external quantum efficiency of 31.3%. Moreover, we reveal good compatibility of this approach in boosting the blue and green device performances.

papers.title: Supporting MedTech Innovation in Australia: The Role of the Therapeutic Goods Administration
papers.abstract: Australia has recognised strengths in MedTech, yet pivotal trials and first approvals (including for Australian-origin devices) often occur offshore. The Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) is well-positioned to further support local innovation while maintaining confidence in the medical devices approved for use by shifting effort earlier in development. We outline the current landscape of risk-based regulation across the medical device lifecycle and frame the issues for clinicians during an upcoming period of active discussion and consultation. The existing priority review pathway could be refined for devices under development. Targeted early access approaches must recognise unmet needs and carefully weigh uncertainties around safety and performance. Internationally, regulators increasingly act as collaborators as well as adjudicators of innovation, helped by targeted programs. The TGA aims for an optimised regulatory system that responsibly facilitates access by Australians to MedTech innovation, while aligning timelines with clinical need and sustaining public trust.

papers.title: Voltage–Current-Emission Framework of Time-Resolved Electroluminescence
papers.abstract: Abstract Time-resolved electroluminescence has been a central methodology for the development of LED devices. However, it still lacks quantitative theoretical descriptions of time-resolved electroluminescence. By combining the equivalent circuit models of semiconductor devices and the carrier dynamics of electroluminescence processes, here we have developed a voltage–current-emission framework to illustrate time-resolved electroluminescence from the pulse voltage as input, to injection current, and finally generate electroluminescence as output. The features of different LED devices can be quantitatively interpreted, confirming their universal applicability across LEDs with different materials and device structures. Importantly, the curves of time-resolved electroluminescence can be simulated to quantitatively describe the dynamics of current and carriers of the LED operation. In all, the voltage–current–emission framework offers theoretical guidance for achieving advanced LED devices for artificial intelligence (AI) technology.

papers.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
papers.abstract: Abstract Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. We identify individual hyperfine-Zeeman-rotational components of the fundamental vibrational transition of the nitrogen molecular ion, $${{{{{\rm{N}}}}}}_{2}^{+}$$ N 2 + , and perform coherent population transfer between energy levels. Our work opens up new perspectives for precision molecular spectroscopy, for high-fidelity qubits encoded in the rotational-vibrational motion of molecules, for precise infrared molecular clocks and for searches for new physics.

papers.title: X-ray Crystallography of a Nanobody/JAM-1 Complex Informs Barrier Weakening and Enhanced Drug Permeability in a Cellular Blood–Brain Barrier Model
papers.abstract: Abstract For pharmacological treatments of brain disorders, the blood–brain barrier (BBB) poses a formidable obstacle, tightly restricting the cerebral uptake of therapeutic agents. Tight junction (TJ) binders, including peptides, proteins, and monoclonal antibodies, that specifically bind to the extracellular domains (ECDs) of TJ proteins are increasingly being explored as BBB-weakening agents for enhanced drug delivery to the brain. Given that nanobodies (Nbs) can access epitopes that are often inaccessible to conventional antibodies, we obtained 16 Nbs with unique CDRs via immunization of alpaca with the ECD of either human (h) or murine JAM-1 (mJAM-1), a major TJ protein. Twelve Nb candidates exhibited high-affinity binding to mJAM-1, as measured by surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and these interactions were further validated for 9 Nbs by immunostaining of JAM-1-overexpressing cells. Five Nbs were found to weaken the barrier of the eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII cellular monolayer, as shown by reduced transendothelial electrical resistance (TEER). X-ray crystallography revealed that the lead barrier-weakening Nb, E6, binds to the membrane-proximal nondimeric D2 domain of mJAM-1. Mutating key residues at this interface eliminated the BBB-weakening effect of E6, as evidenced by unaltered sodium fluorescence (NaFI) leakage in both eGFP-hCldn5-MDCKII and mJAM1-mGL-MDCKII cellular monolayers compared with the nontreated control. Our study highlights the potential of JAM-1-targeting Nbs as BBB modulators, offering a promising approach for generating TJ binders to enhance brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Unveiling the binding dynamics of banana lectin with L-fucose through integrative spectroscopic, crystallographic, and in silico studies
papers.abstract: Banana lectin (Banlec) is a homodimeric plant lectin with glucose/mannose specificity and is also capable of recognizing other carbohydrates. The present study was conducted to evaluate the binding modalities of Banlec with L -fucose. Such structural and biophysical characterization is essential for understanding the molecular basis of Banlec–carbohydrate recognition and its potential applications in glycobiology. Banlec was purified from Musa paradisiaca , and its binding with L -fucose was analyzed via different biophysical techniques. In the first step, the binding affinity of Banlec with L-fucose was analyzed via UV–Vis spectroscopy, which revealed a decreased absorption intensity at 280 nm with increasing concentrations of L-fucose. The binding constant (K b = (4.78 ± 0.08) ×10 4 M −1 ), dissociation constant (K d =21.8 ± 0.3 µM), and Gibbs free energy (ΔG°= − 26.7 kJ mol −1 ), suggest a favourable interaction. Results of circular dichroism spectroscopic (CD) analysis showed that binding of fucose did not alter the secondary structure of Banlec. Differential scanning fluorimetry showed a slight increase in melting temperature (ΔTm = + 0.5 °C) upon L -fucose binding. Additionally, the X-ray crystal structure of Banlec–fucose complex was resolved at 2.95 Å. Two molecules of L -fucose showed binding with Ser33, Gly34, His63, His84, and Gly105 amino acid residues. Molecular docking studies further supported the experimental findings. Hence, this study provides structural insights into the carbohydrate-binding features of Banlec, particularly its interaction with L-fucose.

papers.title: Role of bio-polymeric binders on combustion and fire suppression performance of KNO3/KClO4–3,5 DNB pyrotechnic composite
papers.abstract: Traditional pyrotechnic composites (PCs), often synthesized with epoxy or other synthetic binders, can combust at temperatures up to ​ 2100 °C, creating secondary fire and explosion risks. This study examines how renewable, cost-effective binders: starch, guar gum, tannic acid, and sodium carboxymethyl cellulose affect the combustion behavior, exothermicity, temperature profiles, and fire-suppression performance of PCs in a 4.57 kW n-heptane pool fire. Characterization of the aerosol particulates was performed using XRD, FTIR, and SEM. SEM-EDX and DSC for the PCs. PC-1, with a linear burning rate (LBR) of 10.05 ± 2.158 mm/s, extinguished the fire within 5 s and generated the highest ignition temperature (210 °C), whereas PC-4 and PC-5 with LBRs of 9.3 ± 0.742 mm/s and 9.7 ± 0.693 mm/s, respectively showed a noticeable decrease in ignition temperatures (184 °C and 182 °C, respectively) and suppressed the fire within 7 s and 5 s, respectively. It can be concluded that starch-based PC exhibited optimal fire performance parameters, making it a promising bio-based binder for the KNO 3 -KClO 4 -3, 5 DNB pyrotechnic composition.

papers.title: Piracetam attenuates cyclophosphamide-evoked pulmonary injury in rats; the role of AMPK/NF-κB/NLRP3/caspase-1 and caspase-3 mediated apoptosis signaling cascades
papers.abstract: Abstract Cyclophosphamide (CP) is often employed in the treatment of numerous malignancies and autoimmune diseases, although it is accompanied by numerous side effects. Piracetam (PIRA) is used as a nootropic agent and reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties in addition to its established cognitive-enhancing effects. This study aimed to investigate the potential protective effects of PIRA against CP-induced lung damage in rats. CP was utilized to provoke pulmonary damage. Molecular docking was performed to predict the binding affinity of piracetam for NF-κB p65, NLRP3, caspase-1, caspase-3, and AMPK. Arterial blood gas parameters (PaO₂ and PaCO₂) were assessed to evaluate pulmonary gas-exchange function. The lung contents of MDA, GSH, and CAT activity were measured. Levels of lung IL-18, IL-1β, TNF-α, and caspase-1 were evaluated using ELISA. Immunohistochemistry was employed to evaluate NF-κB p65 and caspase-3. The Western blot technique was utilized to evaluate the protein expression of NLRP3 and p-AMPK. Lung Bax and Bcl-2 gene expression was assessed using qRT-PCR. The histological examination of lung tissues was conducted. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinities of piracetam. CP caused a notable reduction in PaO₂ and elevation in PaCO₂, alongside a notable increase in lung MDA, IL-18, IL-1β, TNF-α, caspase-1, and Bax levels, with a substantial reduction in GSH, CAT, p-AMPK, and Bcl-2. CP administration also led to the upregulation of NLRP3 protein. Additionally, the immunopositivity of both NF-κB p65 and caspase-3 was elevated in the CP group. PIRA markedly ameliorated all previously described functional, biochemical, and histopathological anomalies. PIRA pretreatment significantly improved CP-induced pulmonary injury, an effect associated with suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3/caspase-1 and caspase-3 signaling and with increased p-AMPK expression.
