papers.title: Precision maize crop height mapping using multispectral and LiDAR data from unmanned aerial system
papers.abstract: Abstract Context Spatially explicit and accurate maize crop height maps are essential for supporting site-specific management in precision agriculture. Although low-cost unmanned aerial system (UAS)-based multispectral imagery offers a promising approach for maize crop height estimation, it’s accuracy under varying canopy conditions remains uncertain. Aims In this study, we used 3D point clouds to estimate maize crop height during sparse and dense canopy cover based on UAS-captured multispectral images and compare with light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-based estimates. Methods The 3D point clouds from multispectral images and LiDAR data were processed using a spatially localized grid (SLG) filtering approachto derive digital terrain model (DTM) and canopy surface model (CSM), which were then used to estimate maize crop height.Furthermore, two strategies were explored — (1) grid expansion, and (2) using ground reference derived during sparse canopy aspotential tools to mitigate issues during dense canopy cover for multispectral image-based estimations. Results Results showed that the crop height estimated from multispectral images during sparse canopy cover show comparable accuracy (r = 0.9, nRMSE = 32%) to LiDAR-based estimation (r = 0.81, nRMSE = 17%). The accuracy of multispectral-based estimation, however, significantly declined under dense canopy cover, where no meaningful correlation was observed (r = − 0.1, nRMSE = 61%). In contrast, LiDAR-based estimates show consistent level of accuracy under the same conditions (r = 0.78, nRMSE = 15%). When grid expansion strategy was implemented for multispectral-based estimation during the dense canopy cover, the nRMSE was observed to decrease up to 28%. Meanwhile, with the use of sparse canopy cover ground reference, the nRMSE decreased up to 17%, comparable to the LiDAR-based estimate. Conclusion Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of deriving crop heights cost-effectively using multispectral imaging from UAS. This approach offers a scalable and economically viable alternative to expensive LiDAR systems, enabling wider integration of crop height information into precision agriculture applications.

papers.title: Fabrication and characterization of Fe 3 O 4 -reinforced PEG–PCL magnetic shape memory nanofibers
papers.abstract: Abstract In this study, magnetic shape memory nanofibers based on PEG–PCL (1:1) reinforced with Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles were produced using the electrospinning method. The structural properties of the nanofibers were analyzed using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), while their surface morphologies were examined using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Thermal properties were determined using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), while magnetic behavior was assessed with a physical property measurement system (PPMS). XRD results indicated that Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles were homogeneously distributed in the matrix, with an increased contribution from the magnetic crystal phase. FTIR indicated that the additive was integrated into the structure via physical interactions, without establishing chemical bonds with the polymer chains. Based on SEM and AFM images, the fiber diameters have grown significantly as the Fe 3 O 4 content has increased. TGA analyses indicate that the thermal stability of nanocomposites has increased, while DSC results demonstrate that as the filler amount increases, the degree of polymer crystallization decreases. Magnetic measurements have shown that saturation magnetization increases with dopant and that composites transition from diamagnetic to ferromagnetic behavior. It has also been found that nanofibers show shape memory properties when heated.

It has also been found that nanofibers show shape memory properties when heated.

papers.title: High-Pressure Solid–Liquid Equilibrium and Volumetric Behavior of Choline Chloride-Based Eutectic Solvents
papers.abstract: Abstract Over the past two decades, eutectic solvents (ESs) have attracted attention due to their potential in various fields, from chemical processing to materials science. Despite this growing interest, their use is still restricted to fixed stoichiometric mole ratios. This limitation arises from the difficulty in accurately identifying eutectic compositions, a consequence of the scarcity of reliable thermophysical property data. In particular, properties such as density and solid–liquid equilibrium (SLE) remain poorly documented in the literature, especially under elevated pressure. In this context, this work reports SLE and volumetric data for mixtures of choline chloride with four hydrogen-bond donors: ethylene glycol, glycerol, 1,3-propanediol, and glycolic acid. SLE measurements were performed in the pressure range between 6 MPa and 25 MPa and compared with available data at atmospheric pressure. Density measurements were carried out for the ESs at their eutectic compositions over ranges of pressure (5 MPa to 50 MPa) and temperature (293.15 K to 353.15 K). The experimental density data were correlated using the modified Tammann–Tait equation, yielding average relative deviations below 0.45 %. Based on the fitted parameters, the isothermal compressibility ( $${\kappa}_{T}$$ κ T ) and the isobaric thermal expansivity ( $${\alpha}_{T}$$ α T ) were calculated. Both properties exhibited dependence on pressure and temperature, in agreement with the behavior of incompressible liquid systems. This study enlarges the thermodynamic database of ChCl-based ESs by providing the first high-pressure SLE data along with new volumetric measurements. These results improve the understanding of ES phase behavior and offer valuable inputs for thermodynamic modeling, process design, and the development of ES-based applications.

These results improve the understanding of ES phase behavior and offer valuable inputs for thermodynamic modeling, process design, and the development of ES-based applications.

papers.title: Effect of reduced graphene oxide and maleic anhydride compatibilization on the curing, morphological, and pre-/post-aging mechanical properties of EPDM/NBR blends
papers.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the development of elastomeric composites based on ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (EPDM) and nitrile-butadiene rubber (NBR) reinforced with reduced graphene oxide (rGO). Given the limited literature on the combined use of rGO and compatibilizing agents in EPDM/NBR systems, this research focused on the effect of a maleic anhydride-grafted ethylene elastomer (E–g-MA) in EPDM, NBR and a 70/30 EPDM/NBR blend prepared using two-roll mill mixing. The rGO was characterized through X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with quantitative energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy and thermogravimetric analysis, while the elastomer compounds were evaluated for cure characteristics, morphology, chemical resistance and mechanical properties before and after accelerated aging. SEM micrographs revealed that the combination of E–g-MA and rGO reduced the number of pull-out voids and produced a more homogeneous fracture surface in EPDM and in the EPDM/NBR blend. At higher E–g-MA and rGO content (1 phr), tensile strength improved 127% for EPDM and 81% for the blend, and the elongation at break of EPDM increased from 216 to 490%. Welch's ANOVA with Games-Howell post-hoc tests (α = 0.05) confirmed that these differences are statistically significant. For NBR, neither additive significantly changed the tensile properties, although 1 phr of rGO reduced the volume change in propanone from 70 to 41%. After accelerated aging, EPDM/NBR/1E-g-MA/1rGO reached a tensile strength of 5.1 MPa, compared with 2.2 MPa for the neat blend. This composite also showed a lower volume change than the neat blend after immersion (16% versus 31% in propanone and 194% versus 229% in fuel oil), whereas EPDM/1E-g-MA/1rGO showed increased swelling in propanone. These findings indicate that combining rGO and E–g-MA is an effective strategy for improving the strength and aging behavior of EPDM/NBR composites, although the reduced resistance of EPDM to polar solvents at the highest loading should be considered.

These findings indicate that combining rGO and E–g-MA is an effective strategy for improving the strength and aging behavior of EPDM/NBR composites, although the reduced resistance of EPDM to polar solvents at the highest loading should be considered.

papers.title: DBAASP V4: condition-resolved bioactivity and chemical structures for data-driven peptide and peptidomimetic discovery
papers.abstract: The current peptide renaissance-driven by metagenomic and proteomic mining, molecular de-extinction, protein language models, and generative or evolutionary design-is producing millions of candidates, but useful machine learning depends on experimentally anchored, context-rich labels. The Database of Antimicrobial Activity and Structure of Peptides (DBAASP) is a manually curated resource linking peptides and peptidomimetics to quantitative antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anticancer, hemolytic, and mammalian-cell cytotoxicity measurements and their experimental conditions. DBAASP v4 contains >25 000 entries and extends the resource from a sequence-centered database to a structure-aware repository. Major additions include systematic SMILES representations, enhanced annotation of intrachain bonds and ring architectures, dedicated antibiofilm, and synergy records, PubChem links, >9200 molecular-dynamics trajectories, and new prediction services. The condition-resolved data support supervised learning, strain-, and target-specific models, model calibration, and surrogate fitness functions for genetic algorithms. SMILES representations further enable modeling of noncanonical peptides and peptidomimetics that cannot be adequately described by sequence alone. DBAASP therefore complements large peptide catalogues by providing the experimentally curated activity and structure layers, needed to convert sequence information into testable predictions, design, and optimization of biologically active compounds. DBAASP v4 is freely available at https://dbaasp.org.

papers.title: A comprehensive review of computational strategies in the rational design of biosensors based on allosteric transcription factors for pollutant detection
papers.abstract: Allosteric transcription factor (aTF)-based biosensors are powerful analytical tools for the detection of different analytes such as environmental pollutants and are widely used in medical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. These biosensors rely on ligand-induced conformational changes in transcription factors that regulate gene expression, thereby positioning them as low-cost, sensitive and selective components in biosensor design. In recent times, computational biology and chemistry techniques such as homology modelling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, free energy perturbation (FEP), enhanced sampling techniques and machine learning have been widely employed in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors. With these methods, the structures of proteins could be predicted, the ligand-binding pockets could be identified and characterized, the interactions therein could be analyzed and binding affinities could be predicted. Also, the conformational dynamics, allosteric and transition pathways, free energy landscapes, relative binding free energies of the ligand-aTF complexes can be predicted. Taken together, these can facilitate the engineering of aTFs with improved sensitivity and specificity. Therefore, this review highlights the individual and complementary roles of these computational techniques in the design and optimization of aTF-based biosensors and discusses the recent advances, current limitations and future directions in the design of next-generation aTF-based biosensors.

papers.title: A hybrid transformer and Mamba network with mixture of experts for deformable multimodal 3D medical image registration
papers.abstract: Deformable 3D multimodal medical image registration is a fundamental yet challenging task that requires accurate alignment of volumetric image pairs acquired from different imaging modalities, such as MRI and CT or MRI and TRUS, where large appearance differences, structural variability, and geometric misalignment make correspondence estimation particularly difficult. We propose DH-TMReg, a weakly supervised deformable cross-modality hybrid registration framework that integrates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) bottleneck to achieve accurate and robust 3D multimodal volumetric alignment. The architecture couples a Swin Transformer (ST) branch processing the fixed image and a Mamba Vision (MV) state-space model branch processing the moving image through a sequential cross-fusion strategy that progressively enriches each modality with complementary representations from the other across four hierarchical levels. To address the inherent geometric inconsistency between unregistered multimodal 3D image pairs, Deformable Cross-modal self-attention Fusion Skip Connections (DCASC) are applied at every encoder level to adaptively realign and fuse spatially inconsistent dual-branch features through learned deformable sampling offsets. At the bottleneck, a MoE module with top-2 gating over 8 expert networks dynamically routes features through specialized sub-networks to increase representational capacity without proportional computational overhead. Extensive experiments on two challenging 3D multimodal registration benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving a mean Dice score of 0.837 ± 0.077 and ASSD of 3.386 ± 1.696 mm on the prostate MRI/TRUS dataset, and a mean Dice score of 0.9451 ± 0.0079 and ASSD of 0.916 ± 0.286 mm on the abdominal MRI/CT dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art multimodal registration methods on held-out test data.

papers.title: Human PSC-Derived Cardiac Cells for Heart Failure: From Cell Therapy to Engineered Tissue Patches
papers.journal: Current Treatment Options in Cardiovascular Medicine
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review This comprehensive overview evaluates recent progress in human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte therapies to improve the outcome of heart failure patients, with emphasis on delivery routes, early clinical employment, and the barriers for sustained functional cardiac repair. Recent Findings Multiple complementary strategies for cardiac remuscularization are being pursued in parallel, including single cell suspension, multicellular spheroids, cardiomyocyte sheets, and engineered myocardial tissues. Early clinical translation has established feasibility across several platforms, while engineered heart muscle has provided the clearest evidence of persistent graft retention and structural myocardial augmentation. Cardiomyocyte sheets have reached conditional regulatory approval, and catheter-based spheroid delivery is entering clinical evaluation. However, arrhythmogenicity, immune rejection, incomplete maturation and manufacturing complexity remain major challenges on the path to the clinic. Summary Pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiac products are transitioning from experimental concepts to clinically tested therapies. Future progress will depend on identifying the optimal patient population, product format and delivery route, reducing the need for immunosuppression, and demonstrating meaningful improvements in patient hospitalization, quality of life, and survival.

papers.title: Complementary Hydrogen-Bonded Dual-Network Bismaleimides for Cohesive Adhesion at Metal–Polymer Interfaces
papers.abstract: Abstract Herein, we present a strategy for designing thermally stable adhesive compositions that synergistically balance hydrogen-bond-mediated interfacial adhesion with network-derived bulk cohesion. Complementary hydrogen bonding between carbazole- and benzophenone-based bismaleimides (BMIs) establishes a cohesive molecular framework, while 2,2′-diallylbisphenol A (DABPA)-mediated allyl–maleimide ene reactions regulate network evolution to alleviate brittleness and improve processability. Subsequent incorporation of low-viscosity epoxy prepolymer promotes substrate wetting and generates hydroxyl functionalities during curing while yielding an interpenetrating polymer network. Nonisothermal differential scanning calorimetry analyses of the BMI compositions revealed pseudo-first-order curing behavior, and kinetic modeling demonstrated composition-dependent curing kinetics that govern curing reactivity and melt processability. With the subsequent incorporation of 30 phr of epoxy prepolymer, BMI–DABPA exhibited a low melt viscosity of 0.019 Pa·s, providing sufficient fluidity for resin spreading and substrate wetting. The resulting complementary hydrogen-bonded dual-network BMI adhesive delivered a lap shear strength of 11.53 MPa on an Fe substrate while maintaining excellent thermal stability (Td5% > 407 °C; char yield >43% at 800 °C). This work demonstrates the potential of balancing adhesion, cohesion, and processing characteristics in BMI adhesives by designing a reactive monomer system of sufficiently low viscosity, providing a rational molecular design strategy for future developments.

papers.title: Advances in electrode materials and interfacial chemistry of lithium-ion-based energy storage devices
papers.abstract: Recently, lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) have emerged as a new energy-storage technology that combines the characteristics of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) and supercapacitors. Their development has been driven by the growing demand for electrified transportation, stationary grid-storage systems, and portable electronic devices. In this review, recent advances in electrode materials and electrolyte chemistry, as well as interfacial phenomena for performance evaluation of LIBs and LICs, are discussed. Various carbon anodes and cathodes, transition metal oxides, phosphates, and chalcogenide-layered materials, as well as aqueous, nonaqueous, solid-state, and gel-polymer electrolytes used in LIBs and LICs are reviewed. Performance comparisons among electrode materials and full cells are presented, and the limitations of using metal electrodes, as well as strategies to improve them, are evaluated. The kinetic trade-off between the battery anode and the capacitor cathode, the balancing of electrode mass ratios, and the SEI/CEI interphases under high-voltage and high-rate regimes are considered in detail, along with recycling technologies and environmentally friendly synthesis routes for biomass-based electrode materials. Through systematic comparison of materials, mechanisms, performance, and degradation pathways, this review offers a practical approach to screening suitable electrode-electrolyte pairs for safer, more durable, and higher-performing future LIBs and LICs.

papers.title: Cellulose Nanocrystal‐Reinforced Polyurethane Foams From Sawdust Liquefaction Using Crude Glycerol and Polyethylene Glycol
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Rigid polyurethane (PU) nanocomposite foams were prepared from a sawdust‐derived polyol obtained by liquefaction with crude glycerol (CG) and polyethylene glycol (PEG) and reinforced with cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) at 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt% relative to polyol mass. CNC morphology was examined by atomic force microscopy (AFM), while foam morphology, chemical structure, thermal stability, density, compressive strength, and thermal conductivity were evaluated by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), density measurements, compression testing, and thermal conductivity analysis. Increasing CNC content decreased the average cell diameter from 170 to 80 μm. Foam density increased from 0.071 to 0.093 g cm −3 , while compressive strength enhanced from 0.275 to 0.410 MPa. The density‐normalized compressive strength promoted from 3.87 to 4.41 MPa (g cm −3 ) −1 , indicating that the mechanical improvement was not attributable to density alone. In addition, the degradation temperature increased and thermal conductivity decreased from 0.034 to 0.022 W m −1 K −1 . The FTIR spectra confirmed the successful formation of urethane linkages during the polymerization process. The results demonstrated the potential of CNCs to improve the performance of bio‐based polyurethane foams containing sawdust‐derived polyols.

papers.title: Microwave‐Assisted Synthesis of Fly Ash/Bamboo Leaf Ash‐Based Geopolymer for Methylene‐Blue Adsorption
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Despite its significant economic contribution, the textile industry remains a major source of dye pollution due to extensive untreated wastewater discharge. This study introduced a facile microwave–assisted strategy for converting fly ash (FA) and bamboo leaf ash (BLA) into value‐added porous geopolymer composites for the adsorption of methylene blue (MB) from aqueous solutions. By systematically varying the FA/BLA ratio, it reveals how BLA incorporation governs composite properties and organic‐dye removal performance. As the BLA content increased from 0% (100FA) to 60% (40FA60BLA) in the geopolymer composition, both the BET surface area and BJH pore volume increased significantly. The sample 100FA showed a surface area of 24.4 m 2 /g and a pore volume of 0.019 cm 3 /g, whereas 40FA60BLA reached 54.6 m 2 /g and 0.045 cm 3 /g, respectively. The high silica content in BLA facilitated the formation of smaller pores in the geopolymer network, fitting the Langmuir isotherm model and achieving a maximum MB‐adsorption capacity of 26.6 mg/g. Moreover, these geopolymers with the addition of BLA still gained above 50% of removal percentage of MB molecules after five consecutive cycles. Moreover, the incorporation of BLA also enhanced the treatment of real textile wastewater compared to those of FA geopolymer. These findings suggested that the incorporation of BLA into FA‐based geopolymers provided an effective and sustainable strategy for dye removal in wastewater treatment while promoting the valorization of industrial by‐product and agricultural waste.

papers.title: Multifunctional composite magnetic particles combined with static magnetic field for treating infectious bone defects via SLC2A1-mediated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT pathways
papers.abstract: Abstract Infectious bone defects are a major challenge in orthopedics and stomatology, requiring strategies that eliminate bacteria and promote osteogenesis. Here, we developed a multifunctional composite magnetic particle system (F-Fe 3 O 4 ) and demonstrate its synergistic combination with a static magnetic field (SMF) for treating infectious bone defects. In vitro, F-Fe 3 O 4 demonstrated good biocompatibility with human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (hBMSCs) and facilitated their proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation, while inhibiting the growth of Escherichia coli , Staphylococcus aureus , and Enterococcus faecalis . With the application with SMF, the aforementioned effects are further enhanced. The in vivo studies in the rat model further revealed that F-Fe 3 O 4 combined with SMF can reduce early infection, alleviate inflammation, and accelerate new bone formation. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing and verification experiments revealed that the combination therapy upregulated SLC2A1 -mediated glucose uptake and activated HIF-1 and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways, thereby enhancing the osteogenic differentiation of hBMSCs. In conclusion, this study developed an efficient treatment approach for infectious bone defects by integrating F-Fe 3 O 4 and SMF.

papers.title: Computation or Weight Adaptation? Rethinking the Role of Plasticity in Learning
papers.abstract: The human brain is an adaptive learning system that can generalize to new tasks and unfamiliar environments. The traditional view is that such adaptive behavior requires a structural change of the learning system (e.g., via neural plasticity). In this work, we use artificial neural networks, specifically large language models (LLMs), to challenge this traditional view and suggest that such adaptive behavior can be also achieved solely through computation if the learning system is sufficiently trained. We focus on statistical learning paradigms. These require identifying underlying regularities in seemingly arbitrary word sequences and are primarily considered to require neural plasticity. LLMs can capture arbitrary structures without requiring weight adaptation, even though these structures carry no semantic content and lie far from the natural language distribution on which the models were trained. Our work provides novel insights into the role of plasticity in learning, demonstrating that sufficiently trained learning systems are highly flexible, adapting to new tasks and environments solely through computation, much more than previously acknowledged. Furthermore, our work opens the door for future research to use deep learning models to conjure hypotheses about the brain.

papers.title: Cell surface proteomics of patient-derived malignant rhabdoid tumor organoids identifies ROBO1 as CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors
papers.abstract: Abstract Malignant rhabdoid tumors are highly aggressive pediatric malignancies with limited treatment options and poor outcomes. To expand therapeutic options, we employed mass spectrometry-based cell surface proteomics on malignant rhabdoid tumor and patient-matched normal kidney organoids to identify potential CAR T cell targets. Integrating these findings with transcriptomics and protein expression data, we revealed ROBO1 as a promising target, showing strong and uniform expression across malignant rhabdoid and other pediatric tumors. ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells displayed potent anti-tumor activity in vitro , effectively eliminating tumor cells in co-cultures with organoids from malignant rhabdoid tumors, rhabdomyosarcoma, and neuroblastoma. In vivo, ROBO1 CAR T cells infiltrated tumors, induced potent tumor regression and significantly increased survival in malignant rhabdoid tumor-bearing mice. These findings establish ROBO1 as a compelling therapeutic target for CAR T cell therapy and offer a promising approach to address the critical need for effective treatments in high-risk pediatric solid tumors. Statement of significance This study identifies ROBO1 as a promising CAR T cell target for pediatric solid tumors. Using patient-derived tumor organoids and tissues, we demonstrate strong ROBO1 expression across several tumor entities and robust anti-tumor efficacy of ROBO1-targeted CAR T cells in vitro and in vivo , underscoring its potential for clinical translation.

papers.title: Demonstration of a Two‐Electron Pathway in Piezoelectric Mechanochemistry: Synthesis and Mechanical Adaptation of Polythiourethane
papers.abstract: Mechanochemically initiated reactions have garnered interest as an unconventional method for generating new forms of reactivity. Previous studies have focused on radical-mediated processes or two-electron processes mediated by a ball-milling mechanism. In this work, we present a novel mechano-mediated reaction that utilizes focused ultrasound and mechanical vibration to generate both one-electron and two-electron thiol reactions in the same reaction pot. Interestingly, we find that the final reaction product can be biased depending on the reactive partner. We employ this newly reported two-electron reaction to create the first vibrationally driven polythiourethane (PTU) through a two-electron mechanism, as well as its adaptive polymer composites. This research presents an eco-friendly, vibrationally promoted approach to polymer synthesis.

papers.title: Modular Biofabrication of Functional Skeletal Muscle Incorporated with Endothelialized Microvascular Seed‐Derived Lumenized Microvessels
papers.abstract: The clinical translation of engineered skeletal muscle (eSM) for volumetric muscle regeneration is hindered by the challenge of establishing a functional vascular network capable of sustaining its high metabolic demand and ensuring graft survival. Here, we present a bottom-up biofabrication strategy to generate a pre-vascularized in vitro eSM model through the modular assembly of independently matured muscle and vascular compartments. C2C12 myoblasts were encapsulated within core-shell fibers using rotary wet-spinning (RoWS), yielding anisotropically aligned, multinucleated, and contractile myofibers expressing myosin heavy chain and sarcomeric α-actinin. In parallel, gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)-based microvascular seeds (µVS), pre-endothelialized with human umbilical vein endothelial cells, were engineered to guide rapid and structurally stable vascular formation while preventing uncontrolled capillary self-organization. Fully endothelialized µVS were incorporated into a pro-angiogenic bioink and processed via RoWS to generate tubular vascular fibers with physiological diameters (100-200 µm) and continuous CD31-positive lumens. After independent maturation, muscle and vascular constructs were bioassembled into a hierarchically organized tissue and co-cultured. By decoupling myogenic and angiogenic differentiation, this strategy overcomes medium incompatibility typical of conventional co-cultures, preserving compartment-specific architecture and function and establishing a versatile platform for muscle-vascular modeling and translational muscle repair.

papers.title: Brain PDGFR β + Cells Exhibit Diverse Reactive Phenotypes After Stroke Without Requiring KLF4
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The pathobiology of ischemic stroke is associated with the activation of brain platelet‐derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) β + perivascular cells. While Krüppel‐like factor (KLF)4 is a well‐established mediator of peripheral PDGFR β + cell activation, its role in brain PDGFR β + cells remains elusive. Herein, we aimed to characterize the spatiotemporal reactivity of brain PDGFR β + cells, while assessing KLF4 contribution upon experimental ischemic stroke using transgenic mice that enable tracking PDGFR β + cells or conditionally depleting KLF4 in PDGFR β + cells. Moving beyond the qualitative descriptors, we sought to develop point pattern analysis (PPA) and topological data analysis (TDA) workflows to generate robust and reusable mathematical models to assess spatial cell responses and tissue scar topological changes. First, we report the emergence of phenotypically distinct reactive parenchymal PDGFR β + cells, which cannot be causally and exclusively linked, as it is currently proposed, to local cell proliferation or adjacent vascular detachment. Furthermore, we show that KLF4 is barely expressed in brain PDGFR β + cells under normal conditions and that it is only marginally induced in reactive PDGFR β + cells at the injured brain. Notably, the conditional attenuation of KLF4 expression specifically in reactive PDGFR β + cells does not alter spatial cellular distribution nor scar organization. This suggests that, in contrast to peripheral PDGFR β + cells upon ischemic insults, KLF4 is not a main regulator of the reactivity of brain cells in response to ischemic stroke. Ultimately, our findings supported by open‐source spatiotemporal models indicate that the reactivity of brain PDGFR β + perivascular cells is highly heterogeneous and fundamentally distinct from peripheral PDGFR β + cells.

papers.title: Sequential preparation of styrene/vinyltriethoxysilane-derived precursors for hybrid and porous materials
papers.abstract: Abstract Converting sequence-prepared copolymer precursors into hybrid and porous materials remains challenging because alkoxysilane condensation can reduce structural definition during isolation and processing. Here, styrene/vinyltriethoxysilane (VTES)-derived precursors were prepared by sequential anionic polymerization and transformed into polysiloxane-containing hybrids by acid-catalyzed sol–gel treatment. FTIR and SEC/GPC of the soluble fraction are consistent with incorporation of VTES-derived units, although the isolated products are better regarded as operational sequential precursors than as rigorously defined diblock copolymers. After acid treatment, SAXS, SEM, TGA, DSC, and ²⁹Si MAS NMR indicate weakly ordered nanostructured hybrids with short-range compositional correlations, multiscale heterogeneity, and extensively condensed T²/T³ silsesquioxane environments. Exploratory post-treatments showed moderate porosity after calcination of the 1:1 hybrid (51.7 m² g⁻¹) and substantially higher surface area after carbonization of the 7:3 hybrid followed by HF etching (561.9 m² g⁻¹). These results establish the feasibility of the precursor-to-material route while showing that processing-induced condensation limits rigorous structure-property assignment.

papers.title: Graphene oxide with tailored low thermal conductivity by defect engineering, for thermal insulation
papers.abstract: The present study suggests a viable strategy for the development of next-generation nanomodified materials, exhibiting tunable intrinsic thermal management properties by adjustment of physicochemical aspects of graphene oxide (GO) dopants. Starting from a modified Hummers-based synthesis route, two complementary defect engineering strategies were investigated for suppressing thermal transport, namely lateral size control by mechanical treatment such as ultrasonication and defect introduction by oxygen plasma. The Raman ID/IG defect index was increased with both sonication duration and oxygen plasma exposure, confirming the progressive introduction of structural defects. Hybrid treatments yielded synergistic enhancements in the defect index, with values reaching 20% higher than the as-synthesized nanocarbon. Thermal conductivity, measured under the Transient Plane Source configuration exhibited plausible reductions in value, of ca. 26%, comparable with the value measured for an independent graphene oxide variant, stemming from oxidation of pristine graphene nanoplatelets. The finding demonstrates that chemical oxidation is equally effective to mechanical treatment for thermal transport suppression. While the two defect engineering pathways operate through distinct and complementary mechanisms, namely edge-related phonon scattering for mechanical treatment and basal-plane sp³ defect introduction for chemical treatment, their synergistic combination in the hybrid approach is envisioned to achieve further reductions in thermal conductivity.

papers.title: Engineering an Enzymatically Active Granular Matrix for On‐Chip Modeling of Bone‐Like Mineralization
papers.abstract: Controlled biomineralization is central to engineering physiologically relevant hard-tissue models, yet achieving spatially organized, three-dimensional (3D) mineral deposition in microfluidic on-chip systems remains challenging. While cell-based bone-on-chip platforms offer biological complexity, they couple mineral initiation to matrix remodeling and paracrine signaling, complicating isolation of the earliest biochemical drivers of mineralization. Inspired by bottom-up synthetic biology, we engineered an enzymatically active granular matrix that recapitulates a key osteogenic function within a perfusable 3D microenvironment. Alkaline phosphatase (ALP), the key driver of native bone formation, was covalently conjugated to poly(ethylene glycol)-based (PEG) microgels via thiol-ene photochemistry, retaining over 90% of its initial activity after 24 h. These monodisperse microgels were assembled into a jammed, perfusable matrix on-chip, enabling independent control over enzyme loading and substrate delivery. The system supported in situ mineralization (24-48 h), yielding a calcium-deficient, poorly crystalline apatite-like phase characteristic of early-stage bone mineral. We demonstrate 3D localization of enzymatic activity to the granular matrix, which, coupled with interstitial perfusion, enabled mineral formation whose spatial distribution depended on the perfusion regime. This mechanistically defined, acellular platform provides a tunable foundation for investigating ALP-driven 3D mineralization and establishes a modular route toward hybrid biosynthetic models of (patho)physiological tissue mineralization.

papers.title: Sustainable chemical approach for room temperature immobilization by geopolymerization of heavy metals cations and amphoteric moieties from galvanic waste
papers.abstract: This study investigates the ability of an aluminosilicate network, characteristic of geopolymers , to immobilize heavy metals. In order to optimize the incapsulation of caions and anions the geopolymeric formulation was combined with reducing and chelating agents, sodium sulfide (Na₂S), ferrous sulfate heptahydrate (FeSO₄·7H₂O), dithiocarbamates (DTC), ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and citric acid (C₆H₈O₇) in order to prevent metals release. Galvanic sludge, from the electroplating industry, containing high levels of Cr and Ni (27 wt% and 14 wt% of dry waste, respectively) was used as received. The effectiveness of metal immobilization was assessed by determining the incorporated metal content in each sample through digestion analyses, followed by leaching tests to evaluate metal release. Considering that Cr is also present in its hexavalent form as an anion, a speciation analysis for this element was conducted on the leachates. Among the stabilizing agents tested, FeSO₄ and Na₂S as reducing agents and DTC, as chelating/reducing, were the most effective, achieving Cr immobilization up to 99.73% and significantly lowering the fraction of Cr(VI) relative to total Cr release. This study proposes geopolymers, known for their sustainability in terms of low CO2 emisisons, as matrix with targeted redox and chelation chemistry for real high Cr-Ni waste, effectively controlling chromium speciation and limiting Cr(VI) mobility even under highly alkaline conditions.

papers.title: Exploring the interface of soil organic matter with phosphorus cycling: A size density fractionation approach
papers.abstract: Soil organic matter (SOM) is a key determinant of soil fertility, as it regulates soil physical properties and nutrient cycling. Because SOM generally declines in agricultural soils, the application of organic matter-rich amendments is a common mitigation strategy. However, the processes underlying SOM accrual after the application of these materials remain insufficiently understood and are likely to intersect with both abiotic and biotic processes involving P and other elements. Since SOM and soil P are often studied using separate methodological approaches, we applied a sodium polytungstate (SPT)-based size-density fractionation method adapted to combined SOM and P analyses. We hypothesized that this approach would isolate particulated and mineral-associated fractions relevant to SOM and P cycling, and that long-term application of organic amendments would produce detectable changes in the fractional distribution of C, P, and selected elements, potentially providing insight into the associations involved in SOM accrual. We fractionated Luvisols subjected to long-term fertilization with sewage sludge or household waste compost, as well as to unfertilized controls as follows: Coarse particles (2 mm-50 µm) were separated into fractions CL (< 1.8 g cm-3), CDA (> 1.8 g cm-3), and CDB (≫ 1.8 g cm-3), while fine particles (< 50 µm) were separated into fractions FL (< 2.4 g cm-3), FDA (> 2.4 g cm-3), and FDB (≫ 2.4 g cm-3). Fraction δ15N and total element concentrations were measured, fractional recoveries of C, N, P, Fe, and Ca were calculated relative to whole soils, and dominant organic matter species were characterized using pyrolysis-GC-MS. Compost-amended soils reached 3.5% C and sludge-amended soils 2.2% C, compared with 1.2% in unfertilized soils, despite the sludge treatment receiving only one quarter of the cumulative C inputs of compost over two decades. Recovery of C across fractions was influenced by amendment type. For example, in compost-amended soils, C recovery in the CDA fraction increased significantly. Recoveries of C and P were positively correlated across fractions (R2 = 0.58-0.83), and, in some fractions, were also associated with Ca or Fe recoveries, suggesting a role of P-, Ca- and Fe-mediated associations in SOM accumulation. Our results show that size-density fractionation can provide an exploratory approach for studying the physical fractions where C and P processes co-occur, providing a basis for further investigations.

Our results show that size-density fractionation can provide an exploratory approach for studying the physical fractions where C and P processes co-occur, providing a basis for further investigations.

papers.title: Advanced modeling of the mechanical behavior of natural fiber-reinforced earthen bricks: A second-order gradient theory approach
papers.abstract: Flax fiber-reinforced earthen bricks offer a sustainable alternative to conventional masonry but exhibit complex mechanical behavior due to their heterogeneous microstructure. This study addresses this challenge by combining experimental three-point bending tests with a multiscale numerical framework based on gradient elasticity theory. We first implement first-order gradient elasticity using Code\_Aster and an in-house FFT-based code to compute the effective stiffness tensor $\mathbb{A}^{0,0}$. This approach yields relative errors of 3\% and 4\% for bricks reinforced with 16 and 64 long fibers, respectively, compared to experimental data. To improve accuracy, we extend the framework to second-order gradient elasticity, incorporating size effects and non-local interactions through higher-order tensors $\mathbb{B}^{0,1}$ and $\mathbb{C}^{0,0}$. The refined model reduces relative errors to below 0.1\%, demonstrating its robustness in capturing microstructural phenomena. Our findings confirm that second-order gradient theory significantly enhances predictive accuracy for fiber-reinforced composites and validate the potential of flax-reinforced earthen bricks as eco-friendly construction materials.

papers.title: Efficient deoxygenation of palm oil to green diesel using a metal oxide catalysts supporting on ZrO2-enhanced graphene oxide
papers.journal: Universiti Putra Malaysia Institutional Repository (Universiti Putra Malaysia)
papers.abstract: NiO, Fe2O3, and bimetallic oxide NiFe2O4 catalysts supported on graphene oxide and promoted with ZrO2 were synthesized via wet-impregnation approach. A systematic characterization of the catalysts physicochemical properties was evaluated using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR), Temperature-programmed desorption CO2 (TPD-CO2), Brunaur-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area, Field emission Scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis. The catalysts were evaluated as heterogeneous catalysts in the deoxygenation (DO) of palm oil for green diesel production under varying operating conditions. Among the catalysts tested, Fe2O3/ZrO2-GO (calcined at 400 °C for 4 h, 5 wt% loading) demonstrated superior catalytic activity, achieving a maximum hydrocarbon yield (HC%) of 98.0%, bio-jet fuel (BJF) selectivity of 40%, and kerosene yield of 86%. The exceptional performance is attributed to the catalyst’s large BET surface area (18.64 m2/g), substantial pore volume (0.027 cm3 /g), and moderate surface basicity (3234.65 μmol/g), which collectively facilitate efficient deoxygenation via decarboxylation (DCO2) and decarbonylation (DCO) pathways while suppressing undesired cracking. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibited remarkable stability and reusability over four consecutive reaction cycles, retaining 92% hydrocarbon yield and 80.9% kerosene yield, with BJF selectivity increasing to 84%. The gradual decline in performance is attributed to carbon deposition (coke formation), pore blockage, and sintering-induced degradation of the mesoporous network, as confirmed by post-reaction XRD and BET analysis.

papers.title: Detecting the onset and progression of spinodal decomposition using transient grating spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Abstract Spinodal decomposition can degrade corrosion resistance and embrittle materials. The ability to quickly, non-destructively detect spinodal decomposition via elastic property measurements before catastrophic materials degradation would represent a significant advance in materials testing. We demonstrate that spinodal decomposition can be detected in a binary Fe-Cr alloy via modulus stiffening using ex situ (and in situ) transient grating spectroscopy (TGS). The modulus stiffening is attributable to the convex dependence of the $$C{\prime}$$ C ′ elastic modulus on chromium content within certain compositional limits, which has been established by prior density functional theory studies. Over this range of initial chromium compositions, chromium partitioning due to spinodal decomposition raises the average $$C{\prime}$$ C ′ modulus such that the decomposed Fe-Cr alloy is stiffer than the initial solid solution. The presence and extent of spinodal decomposition in a 36 at. % chromium alloy are confirmed using atom probe tomography (APT), and are consistent with atomistic simulations that predict elastic modulus stiffening in the same alloy. The observed spinodal decomposition via APT is used to predict an expected modulus stiffening which, based on a simple model, agrees in sign and order of magnitude with the observed stiffening via TGS. The quantitative link between an observed composition change and a measured elastic response suggests TGS as a potential tool for non-destructive evaluation of spinodal decomposition in high-chromium ferritic phases in steels.

papers.title: Statistical Design of Thermal Protection System Using Physics-Informed Neural Network
papers.journal: ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems Part B Mechanical Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Thermal protection systems of space vehicles are designed computationally rather than experimentally. They are validated using ground experiments, but all aspects of the flight cannot be replicated on ground. This ground-to-flight mapping introduces uncertainties which need to be accounted for while designing any thermal protection system. Thus, precise computational models along with uncertainty quantification in the models are required to design the TPS. The focus of this study is to estimate the thermal material parameters of TPS based on the target reliability requirements using statistical methods. To perform uncertainty quantification of a system, a simulated model of the system needs to be solved many times on statistical samples, increasing the computational time and cost of the overall process. In this study, a physics-informed neural network model is used in the analysis instead of traditional physics-based numerical solutions. The accuracy of PINN is comparable to that of the numerical solution. To find the parameter distribution, sampling of the parameter space is performed using Sequential Monte-Carlo method. The sampling method is efficient as it generates samples based on the target distribution in parallel. The framework can approximate the parameter distributions that satisfy the TPS design reliability constraints. The framework achieved a remarkable increase in the speed; specifically, the time required to process 10,000 samples was reduced 175 times using the proposed PINN-SMC. This reliability analysis can be used for design optimization of the TPS based on risk analysis along with other systems of the vehicle.
papers.summary: Abstract Thermal protection systems of space vehicles are designed computationally rather than experimentally. The focus of this study is to estimate the thermal material parameters of TPS based on the target reliability requirements using statistical methods. To find the parameter distribution, sampling of the parameter space is performed using Sequential Monte-Carlo method.

papers.title: Plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain measured by Simoa and Lumipulse: an inter-platform comparison across neurological disorders
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an accessible biomarker of neuroaxonal injury across a broad range of neurological disorders, but its clinical implementation requires robust cross-platform analytical and clinical comparability. The objective of this study was to evaluate the analytical and clinical comparability of plasma NfL measurements using Simoa and Lumipulse across different neurological conditions, by assessing cross-platform agreement and the ability of both assays to distinguish neurological diseases from healthy controls. Paired CSF analyses were performed in a subset of participants to biologically anchor plasma findings to the central compartment. Methods 383 individuals were included, comprising healthy controls and patients with neurodegenerative conditions, multiple sclerosis and stroke. Plasma NfL was measured in all participants using both Simoa and Lumipulse, with paired CSF analyses in a subset of 92 individuals. The Lumipulse testing intermediate precision and between-day repeatability was assessed as by the CLSI EP15. Cross-platform agreement for plasma NfL was evaluated using correlation analyses, Passing–Bablok regression and Bland–Altman analysis. Associations between plasma/CSF NfL concentrations were assessed using Spearman’s rank correlation analysis for each platform, separately. Age-adjusted cross-diagnostic differences were evaluated using permutation ANCOVA and multiple linear regression models for each platform, separately. Results Plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse showed strong cross-platform concordance in the whole cohort (ρ=0.90), with similarly strong concordance observed for CSF NfL in the subset with paired samples (ρ=0.90). Method-comparison analyses in plasma demonstrated consistent agreement between platforms, with identifiable constant and proportional bias, alongside systematically higher absolute plasma NfL values measured by Lumipulse. Within-platform analyses showed significant correlations between plasma and CSF NfL concentrations (ρ=0.72 for Simoa; ρ=0.78 for Lumipulse). Noteworthy, Lumipulse NfL CSF and Blood kits exhibited high precision and analytical accuracy. Across both assays, plasma NfL increased with age and was significantly elevated in patients with neurological disorders compared with healthy controls. Discussion Simoa and Lumipulse capture a consistent biological signal in plasma across patients with neurological disorders, although their absolute NfL values differ, supporting the use of platform-specific reference ranges in clinical practice.

papers.title: dictyBase 2026: a reimplementation of the Dictyostelium model organism database on minimal infrastructure
papers.abstract: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Many of its genes have human orthologs implicated in disease, making it a useful model organism for studying conditions ranging from cancer to neurodegeneration. dictyBase has served this community for two decades as a home for genomic data, protocols, a stock center, and community news. Here we describe a complete reimplementation of dictyBase as a self-contained service that uses static data files rather than a database server. Each gene record gathers curated function, human-disease context, developmental expression, and protein structure in a single webpage. The site also provides tools for sequence search, genome browsing, enrichment analysis, and experimental design. The complete Dicty Stock Center catalog of 7055 strains and 1265 plasmids is included, and both can be ordered from the site. New literature is curated by an author-in-the-loop pipeline. A language model drafts the annotations, the authors of the paper correct them, and a curator approves them. Analyses can be run on curator-approved annotations alone or extended to include those still awaiting review. dictyBase is freely available at https://dicty.org.
papers.summary: Dictyostelium discoideum is a model organism used to investigate a wide array of biological processes including chemotaxis, cell motility, phagocytosis, multicellular development, and autophagy. Each gene record gathers curated function, human-disease context, developmental expression, and protein structure in a single webpage. dictyBase is freely available at https://dicty.org.

papers.title: PROSWIN: Probabilistic Solar Wind Speed Forecasting Using Deep Distributional Regression From Solar Images
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurately predicting fast solar wind conditions is challenging, as uncertainties are large and unquantified by traditional single‐value prediction models. In particular, the risks of high‐speed solar wind streams (HSSs), which can cause damage to technological infrastructure, cannot be reliably assessed without probabilistic forecasts. We present PROSWIN, a probabilistic machine learning model that forecasts the hourly solar wind speed (SWS) at Earth with a 4‐day lead time. The approach combines solar images and magnetograms using a deep neural network coupled to a distributional regression algorithm. Because standard error metrics underweight the relevance of HSS peaks, we further introduce the prediction score (PS) , a model‐selection metric that jointly rewards timeline and HSS peak accuracy. On 14 years of data, our forecast achieves very well‐calibrated uncertainties (<1% average absolute coverage deviation). Using the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS), a metric that assesses distributional accuracy, we obtain a timeline CRPS of 41.0 km/s, an HSS peak CRPS of 45.3 km/s, and a PS of 42.3 km/s. We find that the 171 Å channel is an important complement to the typically used 193 and 211 Å channels and that the PS for model selection improves the applicability of the model. Compared to selected models from the literature, ours is the only one that is accurate for both timeline and HSS peak values, rather than trading one off against the other. These results support the advantages of probabilistic over single‐value solar wind models. The introduced methods are also transferable to other forecasting problems.

papers.title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl4]− capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g−1. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture. Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.

papers.title: Solar powered membrane distillation for sustainable desalination from configuration selection to deployment readiness
papers.abstract: Water scarcity is increasingly coupled with energy insecurity, particularly in remote and arid regions where conventional desalination is constrained by electricity demand, brine management, and infrastructure cost. Solar powered membrane distillation (SPMD) is attractive because MD can operate with low- to moderate-temperature heat supplied by solar thermal collectors, photovoltaic-assisted subsystems, waste heat, or hybrid energy inputs. This review synthesizes SPMD from an integrated engineering perspective rather than as a catalogue of isolated technologies. A structured literature-selection procedure was applied using database searches, duplicate removal, keyword screening, eligibility criteria, and a quality check focused on configuration, membrane, module, energy, techno-economic, sustainability, and pilot-readiness evidence. The synthesis shows that DCMD provides simple operation and high flux but remains vulnerable to conductive heat loss; AGMD and PGMD improve heat recovery but typically reduce vapor transport; and CGMD/MGMD concepts attempt to recover internal heat while limiting mass-transfer resistance. The revised analysis further demonstrates that collector choice must be matched to the MD temperature window, thermal storage strategy, module geometry, membrane wetting resistance, and deployment scale. Major barriers are wetting, scaling, module heat loss, membrane lifetime, collector and storage cost, inconsistent reporting of GOR/STEC/LCOW, and limited long-duration outdoor validation. Future SPMD research should therefore prioritize collector–module co-design, durable omniphobic or low-impact membranes, standardized performance normalization, brine-management strategies, and field demonstrations that report reliability under real solar variability.

The revised analysis further demonstrates that collector choice must be matched to the MD temperature window, thermal storage strategy, module geometry, membrane wetting resistance, and deployment scale. Future SPMD research should therefore prioritize collector–module co-design, durable omniphobic or low-impact membranes, standardized performance normalization, brine-management strategies, and field demonstrations that report reliability under real solar variability.

papers.title: Chronic stress drives tumorigenesis and progression via central nervous system-mediated neuroimmune circuits
papers.abstract: Chronic exposure to severe social and environmental stressors is a major risk factor for tumor initiation and progression, yet the central nervous system (CNS)-driven mechanisms linking stress to cancer immunity remain poorly defined. Here, we identify activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-bone marrow (HPB) axis as a critical driver of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). Chronic stress activates hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) neurons, inducing pituitary overexpression of POMC and aberrant secretion of α‑MSH. This neuroendocrine activation increases the frequency of PMN-MDSCs in the bone marrow and upregulates the chemokine CXCL13 in the tumor microenvironment. Mechanistic studies show that this stress-responsive neuroendocrine circuit remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting PMN-MDSC recruitment, suppressing CD8⁺ T cell infiltration, and skewing macrophages toward an M2 phenotype, collectively establishing profound immunosuppression. Chronic stress further amplifies this axis, accelerating OSCC progression and recurrence. Therapeutic blockade of MC5R restores antitumor immune surveillance and markedly potentiates PD-1 checkpoint inhibition. These findings delineate a previously underappreciated neuro-immune regulatory pathway governing malignant progression and highlight a tractable target for improving immunotherapy efficacy in stress-associated cancers.

papers.title: SEX-SPECIFIC INFESTATION AND LARVAL STAGE STRUCTURE OF Tirathaba mundella IN OIL PALM INFLORESCENCES
papers.abstract: Tirathaba mundella is a pyralid moth whose larvae infest oil palm inflorescences, causing bunch failure.This study quantified sex-specific infestation patterns and larval stage compositions of T. mundella on peat-grown palms.Over 20 weeks, 882 inflorescences (441 females; 441 males) were harvested from the Jobenar Raya Estate in Sarawak, Malaysia.Larvae were dislodged, counted, and assigned to five instars.Infestation incidence was greater in female inflorescences (27.9%; 123/441) than in male inflorescences (8.2%; 36/441), yielding a risk ratio of 3.42 (95% CI: 2.41-4.83).Among infested inflorescences (n = 159), multinomial logistic regression revealed a strong shift in stage structure by inflorescence sex (likelihood ratio χ² = 1578.9,df = 4, p < 0.001).Females were enriched for later instars (Stage 4-5), whereas males were dominated by early instars (Stage 1-2).These results indicate that female inflorescences serve as the principal developmental sites that sustain advanced stages, whereas male inflorescences may act as transient sites for early-stage establishment.Surveillance and control should prioritise female inflorescences and incorporate male inflorescences into sanitary pruning.Future work should determine whether larvae migrate between inflorescence types or whether dual-site oviposition with differential survival underlies the observed pattern, thereby improving the timing and efficiency of integrated pest management strategies.

papers.title: Hybrid deep feature fusion framework with maximum entropy based selection for accurate diabetic foot ulcer diagnosis from enhanced and segmented medical images
papers.abstract: Abstract Diabetic foot ulcers (DFU) pose significant risks, including delayed wound healing, infection, and, in severe cases, amputation. Early diagnosis is critical to mitigate these risks and enhance patient outcomes. Manual assessment may be affected by inter-observer variability and workflow delays, which motivates the investigation of AI-assisted methods for DFU image classification. In this study, several hybrid artificial neural network (ANN) strategies were developed incorporating features from various convolutional neural network (CNN) models for diabetic ulcer image diagnosis. The use of feature selection algorithms, specifically principal component analysis (PCA) and maximum entropy score based selection (MESbS), enhanced the discriminatory power of the models. Image quality was improved by using fused filters - average and Laplacian - to enhance the images and highlight the features of the diabetic ulcer and highlight the boundaries of the lesion. The geometric active contour (GAC) algorithm facilitated isolation of damaged areas from healthy areas. AlexNet, MobileNetV2 and VGG16 models processed these regions and extracted deep feature maps. These maps are later combined to create global feature vectors, namely, AlexNet-MobileNetV2, MobileNetV2-VGG16, AlexNet-VGG16, and AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16. The fusion of features from multiple CNN models gives rise to high-dimensional vectors, prompting the application of PCA and MESbS for feature selection. The proposed hybrid strategies demonstrated strong diagnostic performance on the evaluated dataset. Among the evaluated configurations, the AlexNet-MobileNetV2-VGG16-ANN model with MESbS achieved the highest performance, reaching an AUC of 99%, sensitivity of 99.7%, accuracy of 99.5%, precision of 99.5%, and specificity of 99.75%. These findings suggest that combining complementary CNN feature representations with feature selection may improve DFU classification under the evaluated experimental conditions.

papers.title: In Situ FTIR Spectroscopy as a Kinetic Study Tool for Potassium Butyl Xanthate Industrial Production
papers.abstract: Abstract In situ FTIR spectroscopy was used for the first time to study the kinetics of the potassium butyl xanthate synthesis from butanol, carbon disulfide, and potassium hydroxide under conditions as close as possible to the industrial method. This method allowed us to obtain kinetic curves for the first time at high conversions of the starting reagents, determine the boundaries of the process kinetic region, and develop a kinetic model that takes into account not only the main reaction but also the side processes. The main reaction kinetic equation confirms the two-stage mechanism of the xanthation reaction as proposed in the literature. In the first stage, the alcoholate anion forms rapidly in equilibrium, and it adds to carbon disulfide in the second rate-limiting stage. Due to the specific mechanism of the studied process, the main reaction kinetic equation includes the concentration ratio of BuOH and H2O. The rate of potassium butyl xanthate formation directly depends on the concentrations of BuOH, CS2, and KOH and inversely depends on the concentration of H2O since the concentration of H2O reduces the butylate anion concentration. The key parameters influencing process selectivity (temperature and the BuOH:H2O molar ratio) were determined. The kinetic model demonstrates good agreement with the experimental data. The obtained results can be used to optimize the potassium butyl xanthate industrial production conditions.

papers.title: High-Performing and Stable Membrane Electrode Assemblies Based on Fluorine-Doped Tin Oxide Catalysts
papers.abstract: Abstract To improve the iridium utilization on proton exchange membrane water electrolysers (PEMWEs), a new support based on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) nanoparticles was developed, characterized, and assessed for the anode side. This approach utilizes a sol–gel method combined with a 500 °C annealing treatment to promote favorable metal–support interactions and contribute to catalyst stability. The resulting IrOx/FTO catalyst exhibits remarkable performance at a low Ir loading of 0.5 mgIr cm–2, corresponding to half the loading of the commercial IrO2 reference. The membrane electrode assembly (MEA) incorporating the FTO-based anode outperformed the electrolyzer employing commercial IrO2, reaching 1.35 A cm–2 at 2 V and 60 °C compared with 0.9 A cm–2 for the commercial catalyst. Moreover, these catalysts demonstrated excellent operational stability, with no significant activity decline during more than 300 h of continuous operation at 1.3 A cm–2 and 80 °C. These findings pave the way for innovative and cost-effective membrane electrode assemblies with enhanced stability.

papers.title: Microstructural Characteristics and High-Temperature Compression Behavior of a Ni-Based ODS-Composition Alloy and Refractory Composite
papers.abstract: Nickel-based alloys have been widely used as high-temperature structural materials owing to their excellent oxidation resistance, phase stability, and mechanical reliability. However, their mechanical properties can rapidly deteriorate under ultrahigh-temperature conditions due to thermally activated dislocation motion, dynamic recovery, and grain-boundary-mediated deformation. Therefore, introducing thermally stable refractory constituents that retain high strength at elevated temperatures may provide an effective strategy for overcoming this limitation. In this study, Nb-Si-Ti-based refractory silicide alloy powder and Mo-based refractory alloy powder were introduced as reinforcing constituents to improve the ultrahigh-temperature deformation resistance of a Ni-based ODS-composition alloy. A Ni-MRC composite was fabricated by spark plasma sintering. The composite powder consisted of 65 wt.% Ni-based ODS-composition alloy powder, 25 wt.% Nb-Si-Ti-based refractory silicide alloy powder, and 10 wt.% Mo-based refractory alloy powder. Powder morphology, phase constitution, SPS-consolidated microstructure and ultrahigh-temperature compression behavior at 1050 °C were analyzed using SEM, XRD, EBSD, and Gleeble-based compression testing to evaluate the role of refractory reinforcements in improving the deformation resistance of the Ni-based matrix. The Ni-MRC composite exhibited a peak stress of 221 MPa at 1050 ℃, approximately 106% higher than that of the Ni-based ODS-composition alloy, indicating improved ultrahigh-temperature deformation resistance.

papers.title: Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against Fusarium oxysporum: biocontrol, metabolites, and simvastatin docking
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates the considerable antagonistic activity of Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against a pathogenic Fusarium oxysporum AUMC3191 isolate. In dual culture assay, soil-isolated Aspergillus terreus Thom effectively hindered F. oxysporum AUMC3191 growth and impressively blocked zearalenone (ZEN) synthesis. Scanning electron microscopy demonstrated significant damage to F. oxysporum hyphae, such as abnormalities, shrinkage, bending, and deformity. Molecular identification through rDNA ITS sequence analysis confirmed the isolate as Aspergillus terreus, registered in GeneBank (Accession No. OR480103). GC/MS profiling of A. terreus MAK153 identified several bioactive secondary metabolites, notably estragole, caryophyllene, 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol, 1-docosene, 1-docosanol, olean-12-ene-3,28-diol, and simvastatin. Statistical analysis revealed a very strong positive correlation (r = 0.99) between chromatographic peak area% and peak area values. The influence of nutrient sources on simvastatin production was evaluated using four culture media. FTIR and HPLC analyses confirmed simvastatin biosynthesis, while HPLC revealed significant medium-dependent variation in yield (p < 0.001). Camellia sinensis Tea broth (CTB) elicited the highest yield, dominating extracellular filtrate accumulation (145.93 ± 1.13 mg/mL). Molecular docking simulations assessed simvastatin’s binding affinity to HMG-CoA reductase and 3-ketosteroid reductase, yielding binding energies of −8.0 and −7.8 kcal/mol, respectively. The interactions involved multiple hydrophobic bonds and hydrogen bonds, suggesting simvastatin functions as a multi-target inhibitor capable of disrupting ergosterol biosynthesis at two distinct sites. Notably, this study represents the first computational exploration of simvastatin’s interaction with 3-ketosteroid reductase, with implications for estrogen signalling modulation and potential therapeutic applications. Key points • Aspergillus terreus MAK153 inhibits F. oxysporum growth and zearalenone production • Aspergillus terreus induces significant hyphal damage in F. oxysporum using SEM • Simvastatin–HMG-CoA and 3-ketosteroid interaction could modulate estrogen-related pathways potentially

papers.title: Synthesis, Physicochemical Characterization, and Metal Complexation of Novel Azo-Diketone Sulfonamide Derivatives
papers.abstract: This study synthesised two novel azo-diketone ligands (N1 and N2) based on sulfonamides, investigated their complexation with copper(II) and nickel(II) ions, and elucidated the structural properties and coordination patterns of the resulting compounds. We prepared the ligands via a standard diazotisation and coupling protocol, and synthesised the solid metal complexes by direct coordination at a 2:1 molar ratio. We characterised the complex systems using a multi-analytical approach and assessed their biological activity. The results showed the formation of (2:1) complexes with high thermal stability. The copper complexes exhibited a planar square structure, while the nickel complexes had an octahedral structure. Bioassays showed that mineralisation significantly enhanced antioxidant and antimicrobial activity. The N2Cu complex had an IC50 of 16.8 lemda g/mL, close to ascorbic acid. Copper complexes also exhibited low minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values, as low as 0.5 mg/mL, against S. aureus. The N2Cu complex surpassed this, with an inhibition zone diameter of 28 mm, demonstrating high efficacy against bacteria and fungi. The results confirm the potential use of copper-sulfonamide complexes as therapeutic agents and highlight the crucial role of metal ion selection in metal drug design.

papers.title: Upcycling spent lithium-ion batteries into multicomponent phosphate catalysts for enhanced sulfur redox kinetics in lithium-sulfur batteries
papers.abstract: Abstract The growing accumulation of spent lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) presents significant environmental challenges, while the complex composition of battery waste complicates efficient resource recovery. Herein, a phosphoric acid-assisted upcycling strategy is developed to recover multimetallic constituents from spent LIBs and reconstruct them into multicomponent phosphate (R-MCP) catalysts for lithium-sulfur batteries, reducing the need for extensive component separation. The resulting R-MCP, containing Ni, Mn, Fe, Cu, and Al, exhibits favorable polysulfide adsorption and sulfur-conversion behavior compared with recycled Ni-Mn-Fe phosphate (R-NMP). Experimental characterizations and density functional theory calculations provide insights into the electronic interactions and favorable sulfur redox kinetics of R-MCP. Consequently, the R-MCP modified separator delivers an initial capacity of 1075 mAh g-1 at 0.5 C and stable cycling over 2000 cycles at 1 C, with a capacity decay rate of 0.029% per cycle. Stable cycling is also achieved at a sulfur loading of 10.14 mg cm-2. This work demonstrates a practical route for converting multimetallic battery waste into functional catalytic materials.

papers.title: Logged Is Not Done: Verifiable AI Operations for the EU AI Act Era (Part 01 of 15)
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: Abstract As AI agents start to act in European critical infrastructure (telecom networks, payment systems, cloud platforms and industrial robots), a recurring gap appears. A system can log that an operation was authorized and acknowledged, yet still be unable to show that the evidence behind it was current, or that the reported result matches what actually happened. This gap matters to obligations under the EU AI Act, including: risk management (Article 9); record-keeping and logging (Article 12); human oversight (Article 14); accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity (Article 15); post-market monitoring and serious-incident reporting (Articles 72–73). This publication presents the foundational part of a 15-part technical series, also submitted as an IETF Internet-Draft. It defines a vendor-neutral evidence-consistency framework built on these elements: every consequential operation receives a stable identity and a declared verification objective; each observation carries its provenance, resource generation, time interval and clock uncertainty; domain-specific checks produce a scoped three-valued result: SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNRESOLVED. UNRESOLVED is a first-class outcome. Missing or stale evidence is recorded honestly rather than reported as success, which gives auditors, oversight personnel and incident investigators a reconstructable decision record. The framework keeps verification separate from authority. A positive result never grants permission to act; any consequential effect stays under a separate, accountable control boundary. Acknowledgement, completion, physical outcome and financial settlement are reconciled as independent evidence. A three-layer architecture keeps shared evidence semantics apart from twelve domain profiles: radio access and network incident recovery; telecom sessions and charging; hardware and DMA command paths; multi-agent negotiation and asynchronous tools; robotics and physical safety; multilingual emergency instructions; browser agents and agent migration; autonomous commerce; accelerator reset. The material is also relevant to engineering work under NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act, DORA and the Machinery Regulation. The PDF includes: a reader's summary with diagrams; an analytical latency and capacity model with a measurement plan; 12 proposed verification tests; threat and edge-case profiles; a searchable catalogue of 639 engineering mechanisms. The document describes technical mechanisms and makes no legal-compliance, certification or conformity claim.

papers.title: Synergistic activation of peroxymonosulfate by Fe 3 O 4 /diatomite composite for efficient tetracycline degradation: mechanistic insights from experiments and density functional theory
papers.abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Tetracycline (TC) is a persistent antibiotic contaminant in water; because conventional treatments cannot adequately remove it, its persistence raises concerns about antibiotic resistance. To enhance degradation, magnetic Fe 3 O 4 /diatomite (DT) composites were synthesized via hydrothermal methods using natural porous DT to prevent the aggregation of Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles and improve the reusability of the catalyst. RESULTS Characterization confirmed the successful Fe 3 O 4 loading onto DT with uniform elemental distribution, preserved pore structure, redox‐active Fe sites, and high thermal stability. The composite with 10% Fe 3 O 4 (10‐FDT) exhibited superior catalytic activity compared to Fe 3 O 4 or peroxymonosulfate alone. Under optimized conditions (25 mg L −1 TC, 0.20 g L−1 10‐FDT, 2.5 mmol L −1 peroxymonosulfate, pH 4), 87.4% TC degradation was achieved in 3 h. Degradation efficiency improved with catalyst and oxidant dosage, moderate acidity, and elevated temperature, but was inhibited by chloride ions and humic acid, while carbonate and dihydrogen phosphate ions enhanced the performance of the system. Radical quenching and electron spin resonance analyses revealed hydroxyl and sulfate radicals, alongside a dominant non‐radical singlet oxygen pathway linked to oxygen vacancies in DT. Density functional theory showed that electron transfer from DT to Fe 3 O 4 promotes oxidant adsorption and lowers the activation barriers for the formation of singlet oxygen. Mass spectrometry and molecular orbital analyses indicated TC degradation via functional group loss and ring opening. CONCLUSION The 10‐FDT composite proves to be an effective and stable catalyst for advanced oxidation processes, retaining 68.4% of its catalytic activity after three cycles and maintaining over 75% degradation efficiency in real wastewater samples. This highlights its strong potential for practical, scalable wastewater treatment applications. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry (SCI).
