papers.title: Biopolymer‐Enhanced PAAc / PAAm Hydrogels: Impact of Carrageenan Incorporation on Structure, Functionality, and Adsorption Behavior for Wastewater Remediation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(acrylic acid‐co‐acrylamide) (PAAc/PAAm) and carrageenan incorporated PAAc/PAAm (CAR/PAAc/PAAm) hydrogels were synthesized via free‐radical polymerization using sodium persulfate as a chemical initiator. The effect of carrageenan incorporation on the structural, thermal, swelling, and adsorption properties of the hydrogels was systematically investigated. FTIR and XRD analyses confirmed successful network formation and increased amorphous character after carrageenan addition, while TGA demonstrated improved thermal stability. SEM, AFM, and EDX analyses revealed a rougher, more porous surface enriched with sulfate functional groups, providing enhanced adsorption sites. The CAR/PAAc/PAAm hydrogel exhibited higher swelling capacity and pH‐responsive behavior compared with pristine PAAc/PAAm. Adsorption studies using methylene blue (MB) and tartrazine yellow (TY) dyes showed significantly higher removal efficiency and faster adsorption kinetics for the carrageenan‐modified hydrogel. Kinetic and isotherm analyses indicated diffusion‐controlled adsorption for TY and chemisorption‐dominated adsorption for MB, confirming the strong role of carrageenan in enhancing dye uptake. These results demonstrate the potential of CAR/PAAc/PAAm hydrogels as efficient and sustainable adsorbents for wastewater treatment.

papers.title: Performance Assessment of Biocomposite Phase Change Materials for Sustainable Thermal Energy Storage
papers.abstract: This study presents a novel, cost‐effective composite phase change material (PCM) using cetyl alcohol (CAL) and shape‐stabilizing biochar derived from industrial waste wood carbon (WWC) for low‐temperature thermal energy storage, and the simultaneous use of Kissinger and Ozawa techniques to assess the kinetics and activation energies of PCM samples. Biochar content was varied from 0 to 3 g per 10 g CAL to synthesize various composite PCM samples. The morphological studies confirmed the encapsulation of molten PCM into biochar. FTIR and XRD investigations confirmed the chemical stability of the synthesized PCM samples, ascribing to the absence of extra peaks/bands. TGA studies divulged the enhanced thermal stability of the CAL4 sample. CAL4 sample has exhibited suitable thermal properties comprising a latent heat of 184.83 J/g, an encapsulation efficiency of 76.76%, and a thermal energy storage capacity of 99.62%. The activation energy of CAL4 calculated by both models, i.e., 551.118 and 531.827 kJ/mol, is superior compared to that of the pure PCM, which is due to the porous matrix of the CAL4 sample. Even after 100 thermal cycles, CAL4 showed negligible thermal property changes and zero leakage, proving it as a cost‐effective leak‐proof solution for long‐term low‐temperature thermal energy storage applications.

papers.title: Design and Characterization of Fluorinated Maleimide-Based Hybrid Nanofiber Composites as Potential Separators for High-Temperature Batteries
papers.abstract: The development of functional polymeric nanofibers having both superior thermal stability and surface wetting properties simultaneously is a significant research topic in advanced materials engineering. For this purpose, copolymers of 3,5-bis((perfluorophenyl)methoxy)benzyl-4-(2,5-dioxo-2,5-dihydro-1 H-pyrrol-1-yl)benzoate (FMI) with acrylonitrile (AN) and styrene (St) were synthesized via free-radical copolymerization. The molecular weights were determined by gel permeation chromatography (GPC), while structural characterization was conducted via 1H-NMR and Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopies. Hybrid nanofiber membranes of the synthesized polymers were fabricated via electrospinning. Thermal stability was assessed by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), which revealed that the incorporation of maleimide groups significantly improved the thermal stability of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) characterization showed a distinct morphological trend that the nanofiber diameter systematically decreased with increasing fluorine content. Furthermore, surface wetting investigations revealed that despite the intrinsic hydrophilicity of the baseline PAN matrix, the integration of fluorinated segments imparted pronounced hydrophobic and oleophobic characteristics to the resulting nanofiber networks.

papers.title: Progressive Organization of Hydrogen‐Bonded Aramide Motifs via Foldamer–Macrocycle–Cage Architectures for Amplified Iodine Capture
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of high‐performance adsorbents is central to environmental remediation and separation. Yet whether assembling identical adsorption‐active motifs into higher‐order architectures can amplify the contribution of each motif beyond simple additivity remains unclear. Herein, the same hydrogen‐bonded aramide building block is progressively organized into acyclic foldamer, macrocycle, and cage architectures, establishing a motif‐conserved platform for isolating architectural effects on iodine capture. Across the designed architecture series, uptake capacity, kinetics, and retention improve stepwise from the acyclic structures to the macrocycle and further to the cage. Normalization to the number of aramide motifs reveals that the adsorption contribution of each motif also increases along this sequence, demonstrating non‐additive amplification rather than simple accumulation of binding sites. Notably, one cage captures up to 84 I 3 − per molecule in the presence of a 100‐fold excess of competing anions, representing the highest value reported for molecular adsorbents. Structural and computational analyses attribute this behavior primarily to strengthened motif‐level host–guest interactions generated by progressive architectural organization, while solid‐state packing modulates the distribution and accessibility of adsorption space. This work identifies progressive organization as a design paradigm for amplifying adsorption performance, offering insights into the development of advanced adsorbent materials.

papers.title: A New Nitrogen–Phosphorus Bio-Based Flame Retardant for Cotton Fabric: Investigation of Combustion Behavior and Fire Safety Parameters
papers.abstract: A bio-based flame retardant, melamine salt of folic phosphate (MFP), was synthesized through a two-step reaction involving phosphoric acid, folic acid, and melamine. The chemical structure of MFP was confirmed using FTIR, 1H NMR, 31P NMR, and XRD analyses. MFP was applied to cotton fabric (CF), resulting in treated samples with weight gains of 10% (CF10) and 20% (CF20). Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) results revealed that MFP improved the char yield of CF at 750°C, indicating its effectiveness as a char-forming agent. The CF20 sample exhibited self-extinguishing properties, in a vertical flame test (VFT), with a char length of 10.4 cm. Additionally, the limiting oxygen index (LOI) increased from 18.2% in CF to 31.5% in CF20, confirming its transition from a flammable to a flame-resistant material. Cone calorimetry results indicated that the MFP treatment significantly improved the fire safety parameters of the CF. Specifically, the peak of heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (THR) were reduced by 48.9% and 34.3%, respectively, for the CF20 sample compared to the untreated CF. Furthermore, the fire growth index (FGI) decreased from 17 kW/m2 s in the untreated CF to 8.2 kW/m2 s in CF20. Conversely, the fire performance index (FPI) increased from 0.008 m2 s/kW to 0.034 m2 s/kW. The mechanical properties analysis indicated that the tensile strength of the treated samples increased by 2.5% for CF20, while the extension at break exhibited a slight decrease of 15.6%. This work offers a new methodology to engineer fire-safe CF without compromising its inherent material properties.

Cone calorimetry results indicated that the MFP treatment significantly improved the fire safety parameters of the CF.

papers.title: Multifidelity Thermochemical–Mechanical Modeling of Pultruded Hollow Composite Profiles
papers.journal: Journal of Manufacturing Science and Engineering
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Pultrusion of hollow composite profiles with fast‐curing polyurethane (PU) resin requires simultaneous control of heat transfer, cure kinetics, viscosity evolution, and pulling resistance, making empirical process optimization costly and uncertain. This work develops a multifidelity thermo–chemical–mechanical modeling framework for hollow glass‐fiber (GF) and carbon‐fiber (CF)‐reinforced PU profiles produced on an industrial PulFlex pultrusion line. Three complementary model tiers are integrated using a common physics backbone: a one‐dimensional (1D) mathematical model for rapid parametric screening, a two‐dimensional (2D) homogeneous finite element model in ABAQUS for process‐scale response, and a three‐dimensional (3D) laminate‐resolved finite element model in ANSYS for fiber‐architecture and through‐thickness gradient prediction. All models employ Kamal–Sourour cure kinetics, Di Benedetto vitrification, cure‐dependent rheology, and cure‐hardening instantaneously linear elastic modulus evolution to predict temperature, degree of cure, viscosity, glass‐transition temperature, and pulling force along a multizone heated die. Embedded thermocouple measurements are used to calibrate the 1D thermal history and to independently evaluate the 2D and 3D thermal predictions at the reference condition, whereas differential scanning calorimetry‐derived degree‐of‐cure data provide an independent check on cure progression for all three model tiers. The models reveal distinct thermochemical behavior between GF and CF systems and quantify the accuracy‐versus‐cost tradeoff across fidelities. Under the tested three‐zone heater configuration, the multifidelity comparison identifies the speed range over which die‐exit cure, vitrification location, and predicted pulling resistance remain favorable for stable hollow‐profile manufacturing. The calibrated 1D model supports efficient process screening and future digital‐twin integration.

papers.title: Atherosclerosis: From Pathogenesis to Therapeutic Interventions
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Atherosclerosis is no longer viewed solely as a lipid‐storage disorder but rather as a complex multisystem inflammatory disease driven by interactions among the vascular, immune, metabolic, and nervous systems. This review integrates recent concepts, including trained immunity, the neuroimmune cardiovascular interface, vascular cell plasticity, and the microbiome–vascular axis, that reshape the understanding of plaque initiation, progression, and instability. We summarize how established lipid‐lowering, antidiabetic, antihypertensive, and revascularization strategies influence atherosclerotic disease and discuss emerging interventions, including RNA therapeutics, anti‐inflammatory agents, gene therapy, and cell‐based approaches. Key ongoing clinical trials that may clarify the cardiovascular benefits and safety of these strategies are also reviewed. Despite therapeutic advances, residual cardiovascular risk persists because of limitations in animal models, sex‐related differences in plaque phenotype, and the lack of clinically applicable biomarkers. Nanotechnology, human microphysiological systems, spatial multiomics, and artificial intelligence may help bridge these translational gaps. Successful clinical implementation will nevertheless require biomarker‐guided patient selection, rational combination therapy, validated surrogate endpoints, long‐term safety assessment, and attention to health economics. In summary, these advances will shape future translational research and clinical trial design, ultimately advancing personalized management of atherosclerosis.

papers.title: 6-Hydroxyrubiadin Regulates TNF-α-Induced MUC5AC Gene Expression via Affecting NF-κB and MAPK Signaling Pathways in Human Airway Epithelial Cells
papers.abstract: Nakai, exerts a regulatory effect on the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin under conditions mimicking pulmonary inflammation in human airway epithelial cells. Confluent NCI-H292 cells were pretreated with 6-HR for 30 min, followed by stimulation with tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α for 24 h. MUC5AC mRNA expression and glycoprotein production were measured using reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), respectively. Further, we examined the effect of 6-HR on TNF-α-induced activation of the nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathways via immunoblot analysis. The results were as follows: (1) 6-HR significantly reduced both the production of MUC5AC glycoprotein and MUC5AC mRNA expression in NCI-H292 cells. (2) 6-HR inhibited TNF-α-induced NF-κB activation through a transforming growth factor-β-activated kinase 1 (TAK1)-dependent mechanism. (3) 6-HR also inhibited TAK1-dependent MAPK signaling pathways activated by TNF-α, resulting in the downregulation of MUC5AC mucin production in NCI-H292 cells. These findings suggest that 6-HR regulates the gene expression of MUC5AC mucin by directly acting on airway epithelial cells through modulation of the MAPK and NF-κB signaling pathways.

papers.title: The mediating effect of ICU nurses’ teamwork level between workload and missed nursing care in infection prevention and control
papers.abstract: Objective To explore the mediating effect of ICU nurses’ teamwork level between workload and Missed Nursing Care in Infection Prevention and Control (MNCIPC) and to provide references for improving the status of MNCIPC in ICUs and enhancing the quality of clinical nursing. Method A total of 350 ICU nurses from six tertiary hospitals in Shanghai were recruited from January to March 2025 via convenience sampling. This study utilized a general data questionnaire, the MNCIPC Survey, the Nurse–Nurse Collaboration Scale (NNCS), and the NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX). Structural equation modeling (SEM) was employed to investigate the mediating effect of ICU nurses’ teamwork level on the relationship between workload and MNCIPC. Results A total of 328 ICU nurses ultimately participated in the survey. Workload was positively correlated with MNCIPC ( p < 0.01) and negatively correlated with nurses’ teamwork level ( p < 0.01). Nurses’ teamwork level was negatively correlated with MNCIPC ( p < 0.01). The mediating effect analysis revealed that nurses’ teamwork level partially mediated the relationship between workload and MNCIPC, with an indirect effect value of 0.055, accounting for 21.74% of the total effect based on bootstrapping with 5,000 samples. Conclusion The level of teamwork among ICU nurses may be a mediating variable between workload and MNCIPC. Nursing managers may closely monitor ICU nurses’ workload and actively foster a work environment that promotes mutual support and close collaboration to enhance teamwork, thereby improving the current situation of MNCIPC.

papers.title: Localized Crystallization of Ce:YIG Thin Films on Si Using CO2 Laser Annealing for Integrated Nonreciprocal Photonic Device Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Laser annealing (LA) has emerged as an effective method for localized crystallization of magneto-optical (MO) garnet thin films on semiconductor substrates. However, few studies have explored the crystallization and magneto-optical (MO) properties of cerium-substituted yttrium iron garnet (Ce:YIG, Ce1Y2Fe5O12) thin films for integrated photonic device applications using the LA technique. In this study, we provide a comprehensive investigation into the laser annealing of Ce:YIG films deposited on SiO2 substrates and silicon nitride photonic waveguides for integrated nonreciprocal photonic device applications. Garnet phase was successfully observed in films grown on SiO2/Si substrates and SiN waveguides with laser annealing of sputtered Ce:YIG films on top of a laser annealed Y3Fe5O12 seed layer. The magneto-optical (MO) properties of Ce:YIG films on oxidized Si substrates were found to be comparable to those prepared by rapid thermal annealing (RTA). A Mach–Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) type optical isolator based on Ce:YIG film on SiN was fabricated, exhibiting a saturation Faraday rotation of −2317.7 ± 94.8 deg/cm and propagation loss of 188.2 ± 16.5 dB/cm. Isolation ratio of 27.1 dB and insertion loss of 10.1 dB were achieved at 1552.7 nm wavelength.

papers.title: 3D Photoprintable Bismuth Methacrylate Resins: From Formulation to Printed Polymers
papers.abstract: Abstract Vat photopolymerization enables the fabrication of complex geometries with high resolution, but incorporating high-density metal compounds into photocurable resins remains challenging due to sedimentation, limited dispersion, and reduced dimensional accuracy. In this work, we report 3D photoprintable resins incorporating bismuth(III) methacrylate [Bi(MA)3], as an alternative strategy for incorporating a high-Z element into photopolymer networks, enabling a largely homogeneous distribution at the bulk scale while mitigating dispersion and processing limitations associated with particulate fillers. Resin formulations included N,N-dimethylacrylamide (DMAA) as a solvent and monomer, either urethane dimethacrylate (UDMA) or poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA), a photoinitiator, and photoabsorbers. Cure depth experiments and Jacob’s working curves guided the optimization of exposure parameters and component ratios, yielding resins with reliable curing behavior at a layer thickness of 100 μm. The influence of Bi content (0–25 wt %) as Bi(MA)3 or its polymerized form was systematically assessed. Increasing the Bi(MA)3 content reduced overpolymerization in both UDMA and PEGDA systems, improving z-axis fidelity in printed structures. Mechanical testing revealed an optimal Bi loading of 10 wt % for UDMA and 20 wt % for PEGDA at which stiffness, tensile strength, and toughness were maximized. At higher Bi contents, embrittlement caused reduced toughness and lower strain at break. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy revealed a largely homogeneous bismuth distribution within the printed networks at the bulk scale, while higher Bi contents led to the formation of localized Bi-rich regions at interlayer interfaces aligned with the printing direction. These microstructural features correlate with the observed changes in mechanical behavior at elevated Bi loadings. At moderate Bi loadings, thermogravimetric analysis revealed lower decomposition temperatures, with partial recovery at higher Bi contents, while residual mass increased with Bi content, consistent with the initial Bi loading. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed glass transition temperatures of approximately 125 °C for both Bi-free and 5 wt % Bi UDMA materials, but no such transitions were observed at higher Bi contents. While polymer films without Bi and 100 μm-thick films with 10 and 20 wt % Bi content exhibited high transparency, increasing film thickness (200–500 μm) and Bi(MA)3 content led to increased opacity. Collectively, these results demonstrate that Bi(MA)3 enables the incorporation of high bismuth loadings into photocurable resins, resulting in a largely homogeneous distribution at the bulk scale. This yields materials with tunable mechanical and thermal properties while preserving printability, enhancing z-axis fidelity, and mitigating the sedimentation and dispersion issues typical of particulate fillers.

papers.title: Mechanical Characteristics and Microstructure Analysis of Carbon Nanotube-Nanosilica-N66 Nanofiber-Reinforced Cementitious Composites
papers.abstract: To overcome brittleness and improve the mechanical performance of cement composites, carbon nanotube-nanosilica-N66 nanofibers were developed in this study using electrospinning technology. To mitigate agglomeration and the limited bridging capability of conventional nanomaterials, carbon nanotubes were aligned within nylon 66 fibers and nanosilica was incorporated onto their surface. Cement pastes reinforced with the developed nanofibers showed substantial performance improvements, increasing tensile strength by 62%, compressive strength by 38%, and fracture toughness by 69% compared to the control group. Field emission scanning electron microscopy analysis visually confirmed the physical bridging and filling effects within the capillary voids. In addition, thermogravimetric, energy-dispersive spectroscopy, and X-ray diffraction analyses demonstrated a chemical pozzolanic reaction, in which the nanosilica on the fiber surface consumed excess calcium hydroxide to generate high-strength calcium silicate hydrate gels.

papers.title: Effects of predator recovery and climate change on the long‐term demography of a flagship herbivore
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT In the western United States, ecosystems are being reshaped from both bottom-up and top-down processes. Widespread carnivore recolonizations after 20 th century extirpations have returned top-down pressures to ecosystems, and climate change is reshaping bottom-up forces through shifts in the timing and length of growing seasons, resulting in reduced forage quality and quantity. Large herbivores, such as elk ( Cervus canadensis ), function as flagship species for conservation and have potential for both top-down and bottom-up forces to shape demography as ecosystems change. To test the roles of top-down (puma density ( Puma concolor )) and bottom-up (drought severity and elk density) processes in shaping large herbivore demography, and to tie those effects to population trajectories, we built an integrated population model (IPM) using 36 years of elk data spanning the recolonization of pumas and long-term climate change in eastern Oregon, USA. We tested the effects of top-down and bottom-up forces on elk recruitment, calf survival, and population growth. We also tested effects of bottom-up forces on elk pregnancy rates. Puma recolonization corresponded with declines in mean recruitment from 0.44 to 0.32 calves per female and in calf survival from 0.92 to 0.69, corresponding with a 4% drop in population growth. Drought severity increased over our study period, explaining a decline in mean recruitment from 0.39 to 0.32 calves per female, which corresponds to a 3% reduction in population growth. Drought severity likely acted on recruitment through reduced pregnancy rates. Lactating females showed lower pregnancy rates in drought conditions, while drought from fall breeding periods to the following fall had no effect on recruitment. While both top-down and bottom-up forces explained variation in elk demography over the course of our study, bottom-up forces are likely to be more influential on large herbivores moving forward. Predator populations stabilized following recovery, limiting the top-down contribution to annual variation in vital rates. Climate change-induced drought patterns, however, are accelerating during summer and fall throughout large areas of the interior western U.S. Thus, our results indicate the potential for increasingly strong bottom-up negative effects on herbivores whose performance depends on a narrow period of summer nutrition. Open Research Statement Data are not yet provided. Many of the data from Starkey Experimental Forest and Range are already publicly available, and we are currently working to post data for this manuscript on the Forest Service Research Data Archive (FSRDA) linked to the rest of the data from Starkey. Upon acceptance, all data and the relevant code will be archived the FSRDA. Currently, the code for the paper is publicly available on Github at https://github.com/keloonam/starkey_ipm

papers.title: Structural conservation and expanded functionality of hyper‐stable human serum albumin variants
papers.abstract: Human serum albumin (hSA) is the most abundant protein in human plasma, and its pharmacological properties, such as long plasma half-life mediated by the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) and its ability to bind endogenous and exogenous molecules, make it attractive for biotechnological applications. Currently, most wild type (WT) SAs are derived from human or bovine serum or produced in yeast and mammalian cells. Although well established, these methods are costly, difficult to reproduce, and not environmentally sustainable. Building on a previous study to design highly mutated hSA sequences, we extend the validation through an in-depth analysis of three engineered hSA variants: hSA1, hSA2, and hSA3, containing 16, 25, or 73 amino acid substitutions, respectively. These variants were designed for enhanced solubility, stability, and expression in Escherichia coli. All three variants showed low micromolar affinities for hFcRn at pH 5.5, and negligible binding at pH 7.4. In a human endothelial cell-based recycling assay (HERA), the engineered hSA variants were recycled by hFcRn to the same extent as hSA isolated from serum. Exploring the properties of canonical drug-binding sites, warfarin affinity was comparable to WT hSA, whereas ibuprofen binding differed. Complementary cytotoxicity assays on human macrophages confirmed negligible toxicity and biocompatibility. The cryo-electron microscopy structure of hSA3 revealed that, despite extensive engineering, the native heart-shape of hSA, folding of domains, and its open conformation were preserved. These findings validate the structural integrity and functional adaptability of engineered hSA variants, underscoring their potential as versatile, animal-free solutions for next-generation therapeutics and biotechnological applications.

papers.title: Ab initio high-pressure phase diagrams of Al-Mg alloys in the low solute concentration limit
papers.abstract: Binary alloy phase diagrams at high pressure are essential for understanding solidification and chemical partitioning in both engineered materials and planetary interiors, yet their experimental determination becomes increasingly challenging under extreme conditions. We apply a fully ab initio approach [J. Chem. Phys. 162, 184502 (2025)], based on density-functional theory, to compute the dilute-limit phase diagram of the Al-Mg system from ambient conditions up to 150 GPa. As a first step, we calculate the melting curves of pure fcc Al and pure hcp/bcc Mg, including the hcp-bcc phase boundary and triple point of Mg, all of which agree closely with available experimental data. The binary phase diagram is then constructed at both compositional extremes. On the Al-rich side, Mg consistently favours the liquid throughout the entire pressure range, with this preference strengthening monotonically under compression. On the Mg-rich side, Al partitions preferentially into the liquid at ambient pressure but undergoes a complete reversal above ~60 GPa, becoming solid-favouring as the Mg host transitions from hcp to bcc. This pressure-driven reversal inverts the topology of the Mg-rich coexistence field from a conventional downward-sloping to an upward-sloping phase boundary, and has direct implications for models of planetary differentiation and interior chemical stratification.

papers.title: Accuracy and Computational Cost of Standard and Sequential Time-Window Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Transient Heat Conduction with a Moving Gaussian Heat Source
papers.abstract: Background The thermal field generated by a moving laser heat source evolves continuously as the laser scans across a material surface. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer an alternative for modeling transient heat transfer, but quantitative comparisons between full-domain and sequential time-window training remain limited. Methods This study compares Standard PINN and Sequential Time-Window PINN for two-dimensional transient heat conduction with a moving Gaussian heat source at scanning speeds of 1, 2, and 3 mms−1 over 10 s. Reference solutions were obtained using the forward-time central-space (FTCS) method on a 500×500 grid after grid-convergence and stability checks. Standard PINN was trained over the full temporal domain, whereas Sequential Time-Window PINN used ten consecutive 1 s windows with parameter transfer between windows. Results Standard PINN achieved a maximum-temperature mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.461–0.619 °C and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.210−0.322% . Sequential Time-Window PINN yielded a maximum-temperature MAE of 19.248−25.581°C . Its absolute errors ranged from 103.05 to 158.16 °C at 1 s and decreased to 0.98−6.64°C at 10 s. Sequential Time-Window PINN trained 6.80−7.89 times faster than Standard PINN. However, both PINN approaches required more computational time than FTCS. Conclusions Standard PINN provided higher predictive accuracy, whereas Sequential Time-Window PINN reduced training time but produced larger errors, particularly during the early simulation. Differences in training-point counts, collocation-point sampling, and temporal strategy prevent attributing the runtime reduction solely to time-windowing. Further controlled experiments are needed to isolate the effects of these factors on accuracy and computational cost.

papers.title: Hierarchical modeling of retailers' issues for lean dairy supply chain: a data-driven decision-making approach
papers.journal: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management
papers.abstract: Purpose This research identifies key retailer-related issues causing inefficiencies in the Indian Dairy Supply Chain (DSC) and develops a hierarchical model aimed at guiding decision-makers towards a leaner and more productive DSC. The study addresses a significant gap in the lean DSC literature, focusing on the challenges retailers face in emerging markets such as India. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a mixed-method approach, beginning with a comprehensive literature review and expert consultations to identify 15 critical retailer issues. A structured questionnaire was administered to industry professionals and academics, resulting in 290 valid responses. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) was applied to uncover underlying constructs, followed by Total Interpretive Structural Modeling (TISM) to map relationships among these issues. The model was statistically validated using a one-sample t-test, and MICMAC analysis classified issues by their driving power and dependence. Findings The study categorizes the identified retailer issues into four constructs: strategic, tactical, operational, and performance. Strategic issues (lack of top management commitment, insufficient financial support, and lack of assured long-term contracts) emerged as the most powerful drivers, underscoring their fundamental role in addressing other retailers' concerns. Tactical issues, including inadequate cold storage and ICT infrastructure, significantly influenced operational efficiency. Performance issues, such as retailer dissatisfaction, were the most dependent and were strongly influenced by strategic and tactical factors. Research limitations/implications The study specifically focuses on the Indian DSC, limiting generalizability to other geographical or sectoral contexts. Additionally, the findings depend heavily on expert input, which may introduce subjectivity. Future research could validate these findings through broader empirical studies and comparative analysis in other regions or industries to enhance generalizability and robustness. Practical implications The hierarchical model developed in this research provides clear prioritization guidelines for decision-makers and policymakers in the dairy industry. Strategic issues, notably management commitment and financial support, must be addressed first to resolve tactical and operational inefficiencies. Policymakers can use these insights to formulate targeted policies, invest strategically, and develop training and infrastructure programs that significantly enhance retailer performance and supply chain efficiency. Originality/value This study contributes to the lean DSC literature by systematically identifying and modeling retailer-level barriers and by integrating EFA, TISM, and MICMAC into a data-driven hierarchical framework. The findings extend existing knowledge on supply chain performance management by demonstrating how strategic-level factors shape tactical and operational outcomes at the retail node of dairy supply chains. The developed model provides a structured decision-support mechanism to improve operational performance, reduce waste, and strengthen performance management practices within the DSC.

papers.title: Gamma-ray calorimetry of Seyfert winds
papers.abstract: Two stacking analyses based on Large Area Telescope (LAT) data have detected GeV emission from local radio-quiet Seyferts. One was selected via an X-ray ultra-fast outflow (UFO) and one is hard-X-ray-bright. Similar luminosities are attributed to different mechanisms: wind-driven shocks and the accretion-disk corona. Fermi We investigated how efficiently Seyfert outflows convert mechanical power into GeV photons, whether the two detections require distinct mechanisms, and how Seyferts compare with low-ionization nuclear emission-line regions (LINERs). We performed no new reduction of -LAT data but homogenized published measurements to 0.1--100 GeV, placed local mechanical accelerators on one L_γ-- Fermi diagram, and expressed η=L_γ/ as a fraction (̊ho) of the fiducial complete-calorimetry efficiency η_ inverting ̊ho for the ambient density required by pp losses. Winds from Seyfert active galactic nuclei (AGNs) have ̊ho=0.020^ +0.018 _ -0.011 for an acceleration efficiency of 0.1, a factor of simeq13.5 below starburst superwinds (̊ho=0.26^ +0.37 _ -0.16 ). The difference exceeds a factor of three with probability 0.95 and is independent of acceleration parameters common to both classes; it is conditional on the wind kinetic powers, collapsing only if every wind sits at its minimum launch radius. The implied densities, sim10 and sim10^2 cm -3 $, are consistency values, as density, shock radius, and speed are degenerate. The two stacking detections agree within a factor of 1.75 in γ-ray output per unit Eddington luminosity, but the 95 percent interval, 0.26--$24, is too wide to distinguish between them. A third stack, of 186 low-luminosity AGNs, extends the comparison 1.5 dex lower, ordered by AGN power. The GeV detectability of a non-jetted AGN is set by the product of mechanical power and calorimetric fraction. LINER outflows lack the power. For the adopted wind energetics, UFO-selected Seyfert winds fall short in calorimetry. Starburst superwinds succeed in both.

papers.title: Ekstraksi Data Formulir Downtime Tulisan Tangan Menggunakan Vision-Language Model Qwen2.5-VL Lokal pada Sistem Pencatatan Produksi PT Intiroda Makmur
papers.abstract: Daily downtime records for the wire drawing process at PT Intiroda Makmur were written on paper forms and then retyped into a Visual Basic 6 desktop application available on a single office computer. Paper cannot be removed because occupational safety rules restrict phones near the machines. During an internship (5 July–14 August 2026), a web-based recording system was built on the company’s existing SQL Server databases, together with a module that extracts form data from photos using the Qwen2.5-VL 3B vision-language model running locally through Ollama, so no production data leaves the intranet. Extraction runs in two stages: a full-page photo for the header (Canny edge detection, perspective correction, CLAHE) and a close-up of the 48-cell downtime grid, rectified by a three-point affine transform. An ink-ratio gate skips empty cells before the model is called, prompts restrict the model to transcription, outputs are validated with Pydantic, machine codes are chosen only from the official master list, and operator names are matched with bidirectional string similarity (threshold 70%). A review screen keeps a human in the loop before data are saved. The ink-ratio gate reduced Section 2 processing time from 150–156 s to 2.0–33.6 s depending on the number of filled cells. All 45 unit tests (165 assertions) and 16 black-box scenarios passed; reading accuracy was evaluated qualitatively and still requires quantitative measurement.

papers.title: Analysis of Thermal and Heat-Release Characteristics of Thermal Runaway with Increasing Number of Lithium-Ion Pouch Cells
papers.abstract: With the increasing use of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs), the need for an effective response to thermal runaway fires has become increasingly important. To evaluate the performance of fire extinguishers specifically designed for battery fires, the scale and thermal behavior of thermal runaway fire sources must be quantified. In this study, the thermal runaway characteristics of lithium-ion pouch cells were investigated as a function of cell number. Test specimens consisting of 1-10 pouch cells were prepared, and thermal runaway was induced using a heating film. The intercell temperature, heat release rate, and total heat release (THR) were measured. The peak heat-release rate generally increased with the number of cells, although variations were observed among the test conditions, and the coefficient of determination from the linear regression analysis was 0.7494. The THR tended to increase relatively consistently with the number of cells, with a coefficient of determination of 0.9573. However, because each cell number condition was tested only once, the regression results should be interpreted as representing the specific experimental conditions rather than as generalized statistical relationships. The study results can serve as fundamental data for examining fire sources and performance evaluation conditions for battery-specific fire extinguishers and extinguishing agents requiring further verification through repeated testing.

papers.title: SMARCA5 facilitates cohesin localization at R-loops to prevent transcription-replication collisions
papers.abstract: The cohesin complex is well recognized for maintaining sister chromatid cohesion during mitosis and meiosis, as well as for its role in genome organization through chromatin loop formation. Recent studies indicate that cohesin can be co-opted in cancer by aiding DNA repair processes to promote cancer cell proliferation. However, the mechanisms, protein partners, and functions by which cohesin is involved in DNA repair remain unclear. Here, we uncover a novel function of cohesin core subunits (RAD21, STAG1/2) in promoting transcription-coupled homologous recombination (TC-HR) at sites of R-loops. We demonstrate that cohesin (SMC1/3, RAD21, STAG1) preferentially localizes to R-loops in vitro and localize to DNA damage-induced R-loops in cells. Through a screen of chromatin remodelers, we identify that chromatin remodeler SMARCA5 recruits RAD21 and STAG at R-loop sites. SMARCA5 forms a complex with RAD21 via its SLIDE domain and is recruited to R-loops, providing a dual mechanism to promote the R-loop localization of the cohesin core subunits. The ATPase activity of SMARCA5 facilitates the localization of RAD21 and RAD51 at sites of R-loops to promote TC-HR and timely resolution of R-loops. Depletion of either core subunits of cohesin or SMARCA5, both of which are overexpressed in a subset of cancers, leads to aberrant R-loop accumulation, stalled replication fork progression, and elevated transcription-replication collision (TRC) events induced cell death. These findings shed new light on a previously unknown function of SMARCA5 through regulating cohesin core subunits RAD21/STAG at R-loops and established their potential as therapeutic targets in treating cancer.

papers.title: ESAD-Net: an efficient steel adaptive detection network for real-time surface defect detection
papers.abstract: Steel surface defect detection is a critical component of quality control in the steel industry. Traditional detection methods face technical challenges including low accuracy and poor real-time performance. This paper proposes ESAD-Net (Efficient Steel Adaptive Detection Network), which achieves an average inference latency of 8.7 ms per frame (115.3 FPS) while ensuring high precision. Through the serial integration of RegNet-X lightweight feature extraction and the ATSS adaptive training sample selection algorithm. RegNet-X constructs a lightweight backbone network based on design space optimization theory. It integrates edge enhancement module and multi-scale feature fusion mechanisms. This achieves computational efficiency optimization while ensuring feature representation capability. The ATSS algorithm adopts an adaptive IoU threshold selection strategy targeting geometric feature differences of steel defects. It dynamically adjusts the positive and negative sample selection mechanism. This effectively alleviates sample imbalance issues and significantly improves small target defect detection performance. Experimental results on the NEU-DET steel defect dataset demonstrate that ESAD-Net achieves 87.0% mAP@0.5 detection accuracy and 115.3 FPS processing speed. Compared to the baseline model YOLOv8n, it improves overall detection accuracy by 6.8 percentage points and small target defect detection by an average of 13.2 percentage points. The algorithm increases positive sample utilization from 15.2% to 24.8% and reduces false positive rate to 6.7%. Training convergence efficiency is improved by 29%. Meanwhile, model parameters are reduced by 25% and inference time is shortened by 17%. While performance benchmarking is conducted on an RTX 3070 GPU, the model is designed with high architectural efficiency aimed at potential industrial edge deployment. By minimizing parameter redundancy (2.4M) and computational complexity (2.4 GFLOPs), the framework establishes a theoretical foundation for operational feasibility on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Lung Segmentation for Lung Transplant Volumetry: Effect of Radiation Dose Reduction
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Accurate lung volumetry is essential for donor-recipient size matching in lung transplantation. This study evaluated the impact of radiation dose reduction on the robustness of AI-based whole-lung segmentation, 5-lobe segmentation, and automated tissue classification. METHODS: Fifty cases from the Cancer Image Archive (TCIA) Low-dose CT Image and Projection Data set were analyzed. A reduced-dose data set at 10% of the routine dose for each case was generated using validated projection-domain noise insertion. Whole-lung and 5-lobe segmentation were performed using the Lung CT Segmenter module with the lungmask deep learning model in 3D Slicer. Segmentation accuracy was quantified using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and maximum Hausdorff distance (HDmax). Automated tissue classification and volumetry were performed using the Lung CT Analyzer module. RESULTS: Whole-lung segmentation demonstrated excellent consistency between full-dose and 10% dose images (mean DSC 0.997±0.002, HD95 0.73±0.26 mm). In contrast, 5-lobe segmentation showed substantially lower accuracy and greater variability, even at routine dose. Automated tissue classification revealed a mean decrease in functional (inflated) lung volume of 17.12%±5.69% in the right lung and 17.15%±5.56% in the left lung, accompanied by marked increases in emphysema, infiltrated, and collapsed volumes. CONCLUSION: AI-based whole-lung segmentation remains highly accurate at 10% of the routine dose, supporting its potential for lung transplant volumetry. However, tissue classification and 5-lobe segmentation exhibited notable degradation, highlighting limitations of existing tools at ultra-low dose levels.

papers.title: Valorization of Artocarpus lakoocha Seed Starch for Biodegradable Food Packaging: Extraction, Characterization, and Application as Strawberry Coating
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The present study investigates the extraction and utilization of starch from Artocarpus lakoocha seeds, an underutilized agricultural byproduct, for the development of biodegradable food packaging films. Starch was extracted using two methods: a control method (water‐extraction method) and an alkaline method (0.1% NaOH, 8 h soaking). The alkaline extraction yielded slightly higher starch (16.12% ± 0.28%) and amylose contents (24.89% ± 0.31%) compared to the control (13.46% ± 0.37% and 22.56% ± 0.25%, respectively). The alkali‐extracted starch exhibited a lower water absorption index (2.71 ± 0.03 g/g), solubility (3.61% ± 0.05%), and swelling capacity (2.38 ± 0.03 g/g) compared to the control starch, which is attributable to its higher amylose content and compact granular structure. Morphological (FESEM) analysis revealed smoother and more uniform granules, while XRD showed A‐type crystallinity with slightly reduced crystallinity in the alkali‐treated sample. FTIR analysis confirmed the retention of characteristic functional groups. Thermal analyses (TGA, DSC) further indicated the enhanced stability of the alkali‐extracted starch. Biodegradable films prepared via solvent casting demonstrated that alkali‐extracted starch films had superior tensile strength (3.33 ± 0.03 MPa), reduced solubility (50.85% ± 0.46%), and improved barrier properties (WVTR: 0.00370 ± 0.0009 g/h·m 2 ) compared to control films. Application testing of strawberries stored at 10°C showed that alkali‐extracted starch films effectively reduced weight loss (18.96% ± 0.38%) and ascorbic acid degradation (11.32% ± 0.38%), and suppressed microbial growth, thereby extending shelf life. These findings highlight A. lakoocha seed starch, especially when alkali‐extracted, as a cost‐effective, sustainable biopolymer with significant potential for biodegradable food packaging and fruit preservation.

papers.title: Facile Synthesis of Cd–ZnO/TiO 2 Nanocomposite for Enhanced UV‐Driven Photocatalytic Dye Degradation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The design of efficient heterostructure photocatalysts with superior light‐harvesting capability and effective charge separation continues to be a significant challenge in wastewater remediation. Herein, a Cd‐doped ZnO/TiO 2 (Cd‐ZnO/TiO 2 ) nanocomposite was synthesized using a chemical co‐precipitation method, and its photocatalytic performance was systematically compared with those of ZnO, TiO 2 , Cd‐ZnO, and ZnO/TiO 2 counterpart catalysts prepared under identical conditions. The synthesized catalysts were comprehensively characterized using X‐Ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FT‐IR), Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Energy dispersive X‐ray spectroscopy (EDS), Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and UV–vis spectroscopy. TEM and HRTEM analyses confirmed the formation of a Cd‐ZnO/TiO 2 heterojunction with distinct interfacial contact between the crystalline domains. The Cd‐ZnO/TiO 2 exhibited a reduced band gap of 2.52 eV, compared with of the reference catalysts. UV‐light‐driven photocatalytic degradation of Safranin‐O (SO) revealed that Cd‐ZnO/TiO 2 attained 87.04% removal in 180 min, significantly outpacing the reference catalysts in degradation. The degradation kinetics followed both pseudo‐first‐order (PFO) and pseudo‐second‐order (PSO) models. The Cd‐ZnO/TiO 2 demonstrated excellent stability/reusability, retaining a degradation efficiency of ∼87% over five consecutive photocatalytic cycles. The enhanced photocatalytic activity is attributed to the synergistic effect of Cd doping and ZnO/TiO 2 heterojunction formation, which collectively promotes charge separation and suppresses electron‐hole recombination. The good photocatalytic activity and operational stability of Cd‐ZnO/TiO 2 underscore its practical viability for treating dye‐contaminated wastewater.

papers.title: Covalently Anchored, LiF‐Reinforced Rigid‐Flexible Interphase for Stable Nano‐Si Anodes
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon‐based materials are ideal alternatives to conventional graphite anodes in lithium‐ion batteries due to their exceptionally high theoretical capacity. However, the dramatic volume changes of silicon during lithiation/delithiation cause pulverization of active particles and repeated fracture and reformation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, severely hindering practical applications. Here, a covalent anchoring in situ crystallization (CAIC) strategy is proposed to construct a multifunctional modification layer composed of triglyme (G3) and nano‐sized LiF on the nano‐silicon surface (denoted as nSi@G3‐LiF). This unique architecture provides multiple synergistic effects: high‐modulus LiF and flexible ether‐chain network buffer volume expansion and dissipate mechanical stress; abundant oxygen coordination sites enable rapid Li + transport; and LiF nanocrystals induce a dense, inorganic‐rich SEI layer that effectively suppresses parasitic reactions. Consequently, the nSi@G3‐LiF electrode achieves a remarkably high initial Coulombic efficiency of 91.3%, outstanding rate capability (1754, 1631, and 1301 mAh g −1 at 2, 3, and 5 A g −1 , respectively), and superior long‐term cycling stability, retaining 1465 mAh g −1 after 900 cycles at 2 A g −1 . This work presents an effective strategy for regulating interfacial mechanics and kinetics through chemical bonding coupled with in situ crystallization reinforcement, offering new insights into interfacial design for silicon‐based anodes.

papers.title: Time-series transcriptome and metabolome profiling reveals GhWRKY33 as positive regulator in cotton response to Verticillium dahliae infection
papers.abstract: Verticillium wilt severely limits global cotton production, yet the molecular basis of early resistance in upland cotton remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated time-series transcriptomics and untargeted metabolomics to resolve early defense dynamics in cotton seedling roots of the VW-resistant cultivar Jinken1775 and the susceptible cultivar Junmian1 at 0, 4, 8, 12, 24, and 72 h post-inoculation (hpi) with Verticillium dahliae . Results revealed distinct early defense dynamics. The resistant genotype exhibited restrained yet sustained transcriptional activation coupled with preferential flavonoid/lipid accumulation, whereas the susceptible cultivar displayed disordered reprogramming. Integrated analysis of DEGs and DAMs resolved resistance circuits enriched in calcium signaling, membrane remodeling, and secondary metabolism. Network inference positioned GhWRKY33 as a central hub connecting early signal transduction with downstream metabolic reprogramming. Virus-induced gene silencing of GhWRKY33 significantly compromised cotton resistance to V. dahliae , indicating its positive regulatory role in the defense response. Haplotype analysis across 419 upland cotton accessions further revealed that favorable GhWRKY33 alleles are preferentially enriched in resistant lines. This study provided molecular targets for genetic improvement of disease resistance.
papers.summary: Verticillium wilt severely limits global cotton production, yet the molecular basis of early resistance in upland cotton remains poorly understood. Results revealed distinct early defense dynamics. Haplotype analysis across 419 upland cotton accessions further revealed that favorable GhWRKY33 alleles are preferentially enriched in resistant lines.

papers.title: Development and Pharmacokinetic Evaluation of Drug-Loaded Mucoadhesive Microsphere For Enhanced Oral Bioavailability in Peptic Ulcer Management
papers.journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: The present study aimed to develop and evaluate Vonoprazan Fumarate-loaded mucoadhesive microspheres for sustained drug release and improved oral drug delivery in the management of peptic ulcer disease. The microspheres were prepared using the ionotropic gelation technique, employing sodium alginate as the primary polymer, chitosan as the mucoadhesive polymer, and calcium chloride as the cross-linking agent. The prepared formulations (F1–F5) were evaluated for percentage yield, particle size, drug entrapment efficiency, mucoadhesion, swelling index, surface morphology, in-vitro drug release, drug–excipient compatibility, and stability. Among the formulations, F4 was selected as the optimized formulation based on its overall formulation characteristics. F4 exhibited a percentage yield of 91.18 ± 0.94%, drug entrapment efficiency of 88.63 ± 1.12%, mucoadhesion of 93.18 ± 1.04%, and a swelling index of 172.94 ± 4.11%. The in-vitro drug release study demonstrated sustained drug release, reaching 88.64% at 24 hours. Differential scanning calorimetry indicated no significant drug–excipient incompatibility under the investigated conditions. During accelerated stability testing at 40 ± 2°C/75 ± 5% relative humidity for two months, the optimized formulation showed minimal changes in drug content and drug release. In the in-vivo evaluation, F4 demonstrated promising gastroprotective activity, with an ulcer index of 1.28 ± 0.12, ulcer protection of 85.19%, and gastric pH of 3.94 ± 0.16. The reported pharmacokinetic findings also indicated increased systemic exposure compared with the conventional drug suspension; however, numerical pharmacokinetic data are required for quantitative confirmation. Overall, the findings suggest that Vonoprazan Fumarate-loaded mucoadhesive microspheres may offer a promising approach for sustained drug release and gastroprotective delivery in peptic ulcer management. Further studies with complete pharmacokinetic data are necessary to confirm the improvement in oral bioavailability.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of novel non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists in diabetic kidney disease: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
papers.abstract: Aims To evaluate the efficacy and safety of novel non-steroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (nsMRAs) in diabetic kidney disease (DKD). Methods Following PRISMA 2020, we searched four databases to 31 July 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing nsMRAs with placebo in adults with DKD. Pooled estimates used random-effects models, with mean differences (MDs) for continuous outcomes and odds ratios (ORs) for dichotomous outcomes, each with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Risk of bias was assessed with Cochrane RoB 2, and certainty of evidence with GRADE. Results Eight RCTs (15,143 patients) were included. nsMRAs reduced log-transformed UACR (MD -0.36 log mg/g, 95% CI -0.44 to −0.28; n = 14,512 from 8 trials, predominantly driven by finerenone (5 of 8 trials), with significant drug-type interaction; P < 0.00001) and systolic BP (MD -4.72 mmHg, 95% CI -8.64 to −0.80; n = 7,538 from 3 trials (6 trials reported systolic BP; only 3 were poolable); predominantly driven by FIGARO-DKD; P = 0.02), but increased serum potassium (MD 0.22 mmol/L, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.29; n = 1,468 from 4 trials (6 trials reported serum potassium; FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD excluded); P < 0.00001) and induced early eGFR decline (MD -3.01 mL/min/1.73 m 2 , 95% CI -4.46 to −1.56; n = 1,218 from 3 trials; P < 0.0001). Hyperkalemia risk was higher (OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.99 to 2.52; n = 14,734 from 6 trials; P < 0.00001), whereas overall adverse events, eGFR decline, and acute kidney injury did not differ. GRADE certainty was low for UACR, systolic BP, serum potassium, and early eGFR decline, and moderate for hyperkalemia. Conclusion In DKD, nsMRAs may reduce UACR and systolic BP. However, UACR was driven by finerenone with significant drug-type interaction, requiring agent-specific interpretation. Systolic BP was driven by FIGARO-DKD. Furthermore, nsMRAs may increase serum potassium and hyperkalemia risk, although the serum potassium analysis excluded two large trials. nsMRAs may also cause early hemodynamic eGFR decline. Notably, this review assessed only surrogate endpoints and safety outcomes. Several outcomes were supported by only 3–4 trials. Given these limitations and low-to-moderate certainty, findings warrant cautious interpretation and risk-benefit assessment. Systematic Review Registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251072300 , identifier CRD420251072300.

Results Eight RCTs (15,143 patients) were included.

papers.title: Bioinspired Hydroxyapatite-Mineralized Silk Fibroin/Ionic Liquid Interpenetrating Hydrogels for Biomedical Applications
papers.abstract: Abstract Surgical site infection remains a critical barrier to successful bone tissue engineering, and silk fibroin (SF)-based scaffolds, despite their excellent biocompatibility, lack intrinsic antibacterial activity. Here, we report a multifunctional biohybrid nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates methacrylated silk fibroin (SFMA) with an antibacterial imidazolium-based ionic liquid monomer, 1-vinyl-3-hexylimidazolium bromide ([C6VIm]Br), fabricated via a bioinspired bidirectional freeze-casting strategy followed by in situ biomineralization with hydroxyapatite (HAp). Successful methacrylation (degree of substitution = 35%) and ionic liquid synthesis were confirmed by NMR spectroscopy, while FT-IR, TGA/DTG, and XRD analyses verified the formation of the interpenetrating SF/IL network and progressive HAp deposition, with mineral content rising from 12.1 to 32.9 wt % over successive mineralization cycles. SEM imaging and elemental mapping revealed a highly interconnected, anisotropic porous architecture with uniform calcium/phosphorus distribution, closely emulating native bone microstructure, and mineralization enhanced the swelling capacity to approximately 170%. Biologically, the ionic liquid component conferred potent, additive-free antibacterial activity against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, while HAp incorporation improved MG-63 osteoblast-like cell adhesion and the viability of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), with MSC viability exceeding 120% of the control in the mineralized sample. All formulations exhibited hemolysis well below accepted safety limits, confirming excellent hemocompatibility. By combining intrinsic antibacterial function, bioinspired anisotropic architecture, and biomimetic mineralization within a single platform, this work offers a promising, metal- and antibiotic-free strategy for infection-resistant scaffolds for bone tissue engineering, with significant potential for advancing bone tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Family physicians’ acceptability, perceived value, and barriers of pharmacist-led medication management in primary care—a theory-based qualitative study
papers.abstract: Background Polypharmacy burdens healthcare systems and increases adverse drug events. While pharmacist-led comprehensive medication management (CMM) mitigates these issues globally, its integration into Turkish primary care remains limited. Objective To explore family physicians’ acceptability of pharmacist-led CMM in Türkiye and identify perceived barriers to interprofessional collaboration. Methods A qualitative descriptive study was conducted among primary care family physicians in Istanbul, Türkiye, between June and August 2025. Purposive sampling was utilized to recruit participants with at least 5 years of clinical experience. We collected data through semi-structured online interviews using a guide developed by an interdisciplinary panel and piloted for structural clarity. With NVivo software, transcripts were analyzed using a hybrid thematic analysis approach, combining inductive coding to identify emergent, context-specific themes with deductive mapping to the seven constructs of the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability (TFA). Inter-coder reliability was established through independent parallel coding, and trustworthiness was reinforced via member checking. Reporting adhered to the COREQ checklist. Results Participants ( n = 12) facing severe daily workloads (>74 patients) viewed clinical pharmacists as a crucial safety net. Analysis revealed three core themes: (1) Needs and Opportunities: CMM offers substantial benefits by managing polypharmacy, mitigating physician fatigue, reinforcing patient medication adherence, and reducing overall workload and costs. (2) Concerns and Barriers: Major structural hurdles include physical space constraints in FHCs, data privacy (KVKK) vulnerabilities, and pharmaceutical industry apprehension. (3) Implementation Conditions: Successful integration requires integrated Electronic Health Records (EHR), formalized legal boundaries, and joint interprofessional training. Subgroup analysis indicated that early- to mid-career physicians demonstrated higher implementation readiness, while late-career peers focused more on operational burdens. Conclusion Family physicians demonstrate highly favorable prospective acceptability toward pharmacist-led CMM. Successful real-world integration requires resolving macro-level infrastructural and legal barriers while establishing actionable interprofessional enablers, shared clinical algorithms, and compatible digital workflows.

We collected data through semi-structured online interviews using a guide developed by an interdisciplinary panel and piloted for structural clarity. Subgroup analysis indicated that early- to mid-career physicians demonstrated higher implementation readiness, while late-career peers focused more on operational burdens.

papers.title: Low‐Outgassing Liquid Metal–Silicone Composites for Multifunctional Space Applications
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Space‐grade elastomers provide critical sealing, adhesion, and damping functions in spacecraft but require low outgassing to avoid contamination of sensitive optical and electronic components. Silicone elastomers are widely adopted due to their environmental stability, mechanical reliability, and ease of processing. Here, we introduce a multifunctional, low‐outgassing liquid metal elastomer composite with a space‐grade silicone matrix (S‐LMEC) that combines the mechanical reliability of the silicone with enhanced thermal and electrical properties. Dispersed LM microdroplets enable a 2.3 higher breaking strain, an 11 increase in thermal conductivity, and a 9.6 increase in dielectric permittivity without hindering curing. Thermogravimetric analysis demonstrates that the embedded LM does not compromise the underlying thermal stability of the polymer matrix while active electronic testing indicates the S‐LMEC significantly lowers the steady‐state temperatures by promoting rapid heat dissipation. Furthermore, the material can be patterned into complex structures via direct ink write 3D printing. The outgassing evaluation of the S‐LMEC indicates a total mass loss (TML) of 1.00%. To demonstrate practical utility, the S‐LMEC was integrated into a wearable capacitive tactile glove for soft robotic skin applications. This materials platform expands the design space for space‐grade elastomers, enabling advancements in planetary exploration soft robotics and on‐demand electronics manufacturing.

To demonstrate practical utility, the S‐LMEC was integrated into a wearable capacitive tactile glove for soft robotic skin applications.

papers.title: DSC-CAN: a cross-attention network with dual-space calibration for RF-based open-set UAV identification
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications increases the demand for reliable low-altitude airspace monitoring. Radio-frequency (RF)-based UAV identification provides a passive and non-visual solution by exploiting transmitter-dependent signal characteristics. In open-world deployments, an RF monitoring system needs to recognize known UAV emitters while rejecting previously unseen RF signals. However, open-world RF monitoring remains challenging because known UAV signals often exhibit substantial intra-class variations, while unseen signals can lie close to known-class distributions. These factors make it difficult to preserve known-class discrimination and reliably reject unknown signals under resource-constrained deployments. To address these limitations, we propose the Dual-Space Calibrated Cross-Attention Network (DSC-CAN), a parameter-efficient framework for open-set RF UAV identification. We first employ a compact local–global cross-attention encoder to coordinate fine-grained RF patterns and long-range contextual dependencies, thereby learning compact and discriminative representations. We then introduce class-adaptive prototype-radius calibration to construct class-specific acceptance regions from known training and calibration data, enabling adaptive boundary estimation without using unknown test samples. Finally, we develop dual-space geometric fusion to combine Euclidean prototype-distance evidence with contrastive cosine evidence, thereby suppressing unreliable acceptance decisions when the two spaces provide inconsistent support for a known class. Experiments on multiple known–unknown class partitions show that DSC-CAN achieves strong and stable open-set performance with only 0.187 M parameters. In the primary scenario, DSC-CAN obtains an H -score of 0.9542, an AUROC of 0.9847, an FPR@95 of 0.0368, and an OSCR of 0.9586. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of the overall design and the complementary roles of its components.

Experiments on multiple known–unknown class partitions show that DSC-CAN achieves strong and stable open-set performance with only 0.187 M parameters.

papers.title: Population-level spatial patterns of body-surface temperature in older adults: a multicenter infrared thermography study across diverse environmental settings
papers.abstract: Background Body-surface temperature reflects peripheral physiological regulation and may provide a useful phenotype for population studies of ageing. Infrared thermography (IRT) enables non-invasive assessment of temperature distribution, but large multicenter evidence remains limited. We aimed to characterise body-surface temperature patterns in older adults and examine their associations with individual and contextual factors. Methods In this multicenter observational study, 5,225 adults aged ≥60 years underwent standardized IRT across multiple regions in China. Temperature was measured at 12 predefined trunk regions. Both absolute regional temperature and plane-specific relative temperature (ΔT) were analyzed. Multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic, anthropometric, physiological, and center-related variables were used to assess constitution-by-region interactions, followed by false discovery rate-adjusted region-specific analysis. Sensitivity analysis included absolute-temperature models and leave-one-site-out validation. Results A total of 62,700 region-level observations were analyzed. Regional setting was the largest contributor to thermal variability, followed by body composition, whereas constitution explained a relatively small proportion of overall variance (2.0–10.9%). Significant constitution-by-region interactions indicated spatially heterogeneous temperature patterns (χ²=732.41, df=88, p<0.001). Constitution-related differences were localized mainly to abdominal, posterior lumbar, and selected thoracic regions, with modest effect sizes (0.08–0.27 °C) that remained directionally consistent across sensitivity analysis. Conclusion Body-surface temperature in older adults exhibits modest but spatially organized variation influenced predominantly by regional setting and body composition. Constitution-related differences are localized and reproducible but should be interpreted as exploratory surface-temperature phenotypes rather than clinically actionable findings.
papers.summary: Background Body-surface temperature reflects peripheral physiological regulation and may provide a useful phenotype for population studies of ageing. Results A total of 62,700 region-level observations were analyzed. Significant constitution-by-region interactions indicated spatially heterogeneous temperature patterns (χ²=732.41, df=88, p<0.001).

papers.title: A conserved EREG+IL1RN+ macrophage program defines an inflammation-associated transcriptional state linked to WTAP reprogramming and preterm premature rupture of membranes
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
papers.abstract: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a major cause of spontaneous preterm birth, yet the cellular mechanisms linking inflammation to membrane dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic datasets from multiple maternal-fetal interface tissues to construct a comprehensive atlas of inflammatory signaling during early pregnancy. Macrophages emerged as the predominant source of basal inflammatory activity, and secondary clustering identified a conserved EREG + IL1RN + macrophages characterized by elevated inflammatory and innate immune programs. Pseudotime analysis revealed a transcriptional progression from proliferative and immunoregulatory macrophage states toward inflammatory and immune-effector states, with EREG + IL1RN + macrophages exhibiting a distinct transcriptional profile. Independent single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic datasets confirmed the transcriptional and spatial conservation of this population. In placental infection datasets, EREG + IL1RN + macrophages were markedly expanded and enriched for cytokine signaling, leukocyte recruitment, and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways. WTAP , an m 6 A-associated candidate regulator, was positively associated with inflammatory macrophage programs, and its depletion attenuated inflammatory gene expression while promoting immunity hub-associated signatures. Clinically, the EREG + IL1RN + macrophage signature was significantly enriched in PPROM fetal membranes and showed the strongest ability to distinguish PPROM from preterm labor controls. Together, these findings identify EREG + IL1RN + macrophages as a conserved inflammatory macrophage program and implicate WTAP in inflammatory macrophage remodeling at the maternal-fetal interface.

papers.title: Sustainable Self-Healing Thermoresponsive Nanocomposite Derived from Shrimp Shells and Lignin Biowaste for Water Shutoff in Ultradeep High-Temperature, High-Salinity Carbonate Reservoirs
papers.abstract: Abstract Excessive water production in ultradeep, extreme high-temperature and high-salinity (HTHS) carbonate reservoirs has emerged as a major challenge, reducing hydrocarbon productivity and creating substantial environmental and economic burdens. Herein, we report, for the first time, the synthesis of a novel, highly resilient, sustainable, self-healing, thermoresponsive chitin-based nanocomposite hydrogel for water shutoff, specifically tailored to endure extreme harsh conditions of 160 °C and 350,000 ppm salinity. The nanocomposite was synthesized via a near-zero-waste approach utilizing chitin and CaCO3 nanoparticles derived from shrimp shell biomass, employing a recyclable, CO2-switchable natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES)-assisted enzymatic process. The extracted chitin was copolymerized with vinyl ester sulfonated lignin (VESL), a green macromonomer derived from industrial lignin waste, and 1-vinylimidazole (VIm) via free radical polymerization. The hydrogel composition has been optimized using response surface methodology (RSM) with central composite design. The nanocomposite was thoroughly characterized by FTIR, 1H NMR, SEM, EDX, TGA, and DTG analysis. The optimized nanocomposite demonstrated a superior swelling ratio and viscoelastic properties even at an ultralow polymer concentration of 0.08 wt % across temperatures of 25 to 160 °C and salinities up to 350,000 ppm. Core-flooding experiments indicated effective fracture plugging with high RRF values of 300.5 ± 5.7 and 191.1 ± 4.8 (with plugging efficiencies of 99.7 ± 0.4% and 99.5 ± 0.5%, respectively) using ultralow nanocomposite concentrations of 0.08 wt % and 0.1 wt %, respectively. This research presents a sustainable strategy that integrates the CO2-switchable green extraction of chitin with lignin for valorization of marine and industrial biowaste into a high-performance self-healing hydrogel for water shutoff in ultra-HTHS reservoirs.

papers.title: Separated thermal–mechanical damage modelling of concrete at elevated temperatures: formulation, ABAQUS implementation, and fire performance prediction
papers.abstract: Predicting the response of concrete to fire remains difficult because of the complex, coupled thermal and mechanical damage that develops at elevated temperatures, which existing constitutive models often treat in a lumped or inconsistent manner. This study develops a thermodynamically consistent damage–plasticity model in which thermal and mechanical damage evolve through independent, energy-based laws, coupled with temperature-dependent plasticity and a full strain decomposition that includes thermal expansion and transient creep. The model is implemented as an ABAQUS UMAT subroutine to enable analysis from the material to the structural scale. Model predictions were validated against published experimental data over the range 20–600 °C. At the material scale, the predicted compressive strength decreases from 39 MPa at ambient temperature to 30 MPa (77%) at 400 °C and 14 MPa (36%) at 600 °C, while the thermal damage variable reaches 0.36 and 0.75, respectively. At the structural scale, the predicted peak capacity of reinforced concrete beams decreases from 470 to 360 and 175 kN over the same range, consistent with test data. A fire-protection design study further shows that, for the specific column geometry and loading condition analysed, a 20 mm coating provides the most favourable balance between capacity retention and material cost for achieving an R120 rating. The proposed framework offers a physically based tool for assessing the high-temperature performance of concrete.

papers.title: Near-infrared responsive theranostic platforms: toxicological challenges, biological interactions, and clinical translation
papers.abstract: The disease microenvironment is a complex milieu containing unique biochemical and biophysical cues, such as acidosis, oxidative stress, hypoxia, enzymatic imbalance, and microorganisms, which influence not only the effectiveness of treatments but also the fate and safety of the nanomedicine. NIR-responsive dyes and dye-conjugated nanomaterials have attracted considerable attention for diagnostic and therapeutic applications owing to their deep tissue penetration, external-stimulus activation, and precise spatiotemporal control. Despite notable progress in developing NIR-responsive systems for cancer, inflammatory diseases, and infections, their clinical use is limited by issues such as toxicity, degradation, biodistribution, accumulation, persistence, and immune reactions to nanomaterials. Importantly, recent studies have shown that the disease microenvironment can significantly affect the degradation, activation, bioactivity, and toxicity of NIR-responsive systems, yet these issues remain scattered in the literature. Specific attention is paid to structure–toxicity relationships, phototoxicity, immunotoxicity, biodegradability, biodistribution, organ-specific accumulation, and long-term safety, as well as emerging contrasts between NIR-I and NIR-II-based systems. We additionally elaborate on advanced experimental models, regulatory approaches, and safety and design approaches, such as biodegradable systems, renal-clearance-based systems, and smart activated nanomaterials.
